title: Monetary diversity and energy commons
content:
Introducing Marcus Saul, who works with Chris Cook at Island Power, who came up with the original idea for use-credit obligations, a tool that we’re promoting at Growing the Commons, and part of the toolkit that some GtC founder groups are using.

Marcus gave this speech on Sunday 25 October 2026 at the Monetary Diversity Gathering II, at La Tricoterie in Brussels. The slides used appear through the text, in the order they were shown. Originally published on his blog.

Good morning.

I want you to picture a field. A rectangular field of grass. Two goals, one at either end. Eleven players on each side. A round ball.

Two goalkeepers, who are allowed to handle the ball within their own penalty areas. The game is played predominantly with your feet. And the objective is to put the ball into the back of your opponent’s net, for which you score one goal.

We all recognise this game: Football.

Of course, football did not suddenly appear in 1863. Different versions of ball games have existed for centuries. In ancient China, people played a game called Cuju. In Florence, a form of football called Calcio Storico developed and is still played today.

title: From Abidjan with Knowledge Equity: Reflections on WikiIndaba 2026
content:
From 13-15 November 2026, African Wikimedians gathered in Abidjan, Côte d’Ivoire, for the 10th edition of WikiIndaba under the theme Africa’s Future: Knowledge Equity and Innovation. After the cancellation of the planned 2025 edition, this gathering felt like a long-awaited reunion and a deliberate step forward.

Hosted by the Wikimedia Community User Group Côte d’Ivoire and coordinated with Wiscom, the conference brought together more than 200+ participants from roughly 40 countries and the diaspora, working in English, French, and Arabic. Parallel to the main program ran the WikiIndaba Hackathon, satellite events across the continent, and a pre-conference for African users with extended rights focused on “Beyond Editing.”

The energy in Abidjan was unmistakable. Sessions spanned equity and community health, GLAM and cultural heritage, research/education/technology, and movement governance. Conversations repeatedly returned to practical questions: how to close content and participation gaps in African languages, how to make tools more usable in low-connectivity environments, and how to document local knowledge so it is both visible and trusted globally.

title: Who skipped work for GTA VI? Dutch staff, young men, and US soldiers
content:
After 13 years of waiting, GTA VI finally went on sale on 19 November. Workers across Europe rushed to book the day off, many turning it into a four-day weekend. Meanwhile, Brussels is rethinking the rules for online games, from virtual currencies to child protection.

Grand Theft Auto VI, developed by Rockstar Games, arrived after two delays and countless internet jokes about things happening “before GTA VI”. The game takes players back to Vice City, Rockstar’s fictional version of Miami, in the fictional state of Leonida, modelled on Florida. But while it is set in America, the excitement is worldwide, with European gamers rearranging their schedules to play.

According to Remote, a global HR platform, annual-leave bookings for the release day were 32 per cent higher than for the same Thursday in 2025 worldwide, among employees on its platform. Several EU countries recorded increases, with the Netherlands leading the global ranking at 58 per cent, followed by Ireland at 50 per cent and Spain at 46 per cent. Portugal and Poland both recorded increases of 29 per cent, Italy 25 per cent and France five per cent.

title: From first contact to lasting support: Baltic Sea Network explores youth outreach in Stockholm
content:
How can youth guidance centres reach young people who are not in education, employment or training (NEET), particularly those who remain outside existing support systems? This question was at the centre of the Baltic Sea Network for Youth Guidance Centres and NEET Services meeting, held in Stockholm on 10–12 November 2026.

The City of Stockholm hosted the meeting as part of the School to Work flagship under Policy Area Education of the EU Strategy for the Baltic Sea Region (EUSBSR). The event brought together youth guidance practitioners, employment specialists and policymakers to exchange experiences and explore approaches to reaching young people who may not actively seek assistance.

The Stockholm meeting built on the launch of the Baltic Sea Network for Youth Guidance Centres and NEET Services in Kraków, Poland, in March 2026. During that first gathering, participants identified outreach as a key challenge for youth guidance services, highlighting the importance of finding, engaging and motivating young people who are not reached through conventional support systems.

title: Jensen Huang’s reported affair was ‘most expensive sex since Helen of Troy’, US senator says
content:
John Kennedy looks to Trump leaders as he asks how China evidently bypassed export controls for Nvidia’s top AI chips

Invoking Greek mythology, US senator John Kennedy has characterized former Nvidia chief executive officer Jensen Huang’s reported affair with a suspected Chinese spy as “the most expensive sex since Helen of Troy”.

The Louisiana Republican’s allusion to the legendary figure whose desirability was such that it caused the mythic Trojan war came during an interview on NBC’s Meet the Press on Sunday. Host Kristen Welker asked Kennedy, known for his colloquialisms, if US national security was put at risk by Huang’s affair, given the position his company’s chips have occupied at the forefront of the artificial intelligence boom.

title: Breaking the silence: Pratishta’s journey from childhood abuse to advocacy
content:
In South Asia, survivors of sexual and physical abuse are often met with judgment and stigma

Originally published on Global Voices

Photo via Pratistha Gautam. Used with permission.

Editorial note: This article contains mention of gender-based violence, sexual assault, violence against children, and child sexual abuse, which may be triggering for some readers.

November 25 to December 10, 2026, marks the UN’s 16 Days of Activism against Gender-Based Violence. However, even as gender-based violence gets more recognition globally, survivors are still struggling to access social or legal justice. South Asia is no exception to this. Global Voices sat down with one survivor of childhood abuse who uses her experience to fuel her advocacy work today.

South Asia is home to nearly one quarter of the world’s population, woven with a diverse, culture-driven fabric where women are often celebrated as goddesses. However, this veneration doesn’t necessarily mean South Asian women are safe or free from abuse.

title: Serbia and Hungary show why playing East against West may no longer pay for small European states
content:
Serbia’s student-led movement entered parliament on November 17, following its historic electoral defeat of Aleksandar Vučić’s party, after two years of protests. Seven months earlier, Hungarian voters ended Viktor Orbán’s 16 years in power.

These political transitions, following years of increasingly centralised rule, raise an economic question that extends well beyond the two countries. Can smaller peripheral states still benefit from playing competing great powers against each other?

Hungary, an EU member state, and Serbia, a long-time candidate, followed similar foreign policy strategies. Hungary called it “connectivity”; political scientists call it hedging: maintaining economic relationships with competing great powers, without fully aligning with any one of them.

In practice, both countries continued to anchor in European markets while simultaneously cultivating ties with China, Russia and the US. For years, this geopolitical balancing act seemed to offer economic opportunities and leverage well beyond their size. The countries managed to attract investment, secure energy supply and even strengthen their bargaining positions.

title: Vastarinta vai brändi? Saint Levant ja Palestiina popin valtavirrassa
content:
Saint Levant on nostanut Palestiina-kysymyksen sotaisista uutisotsikoista ja poliittisesta jargonista inhimilliselle ja ymmärrettävälle tasolle. Miksi juuri Saint Levantin kaltainen nuori, diasporassa elävä trendikäs hahmo pystyy tekemään Palestiinasta globaalisti kulutettavaa popkulttuuria? Mitä tapahtuu, kun poliittisesta identiteetistä tulee samalla vastarintaa, viihdettä ja kaupallinen brändi?

Lensin tukahduttavan kuumana elokuisena kesäpäivänä Lontooseen viettämään viikonloppua musiikkifestivaalin merkeissä. Kyseessä oli Mahrajan Festival, brittiläinen ja ensimmäistä kertaa järjestetty musiikkifestivaali Euroopassa, joka oli omistettu kokonaan arabiankieliselle musiikille. Festivaali järjestettiin Lontoon Crystal Palace Bowlissa Live Nation ja ABU Recordings toimesta. Tunnelma oli tiivis ja letkeä. Yleisössä puhuttiin lähinnä englantia ja arabiaa, ja Palestiinan liput liehuivat tapahtuma-alueen jokaisessa nurkassa. Lisäksi keffiyeh-huivit ja perinteiset Lähi-idässä käytetyt ruudulliset päähineet – joista erityisesti mustavalkoisesta versiosta on tullut palestiinalaisen identiteetin ja solidaarisuuden symboli – tuntuivat olevan festivaalin epävirallinen asukoodi.

title: Aseet eivät yksin riitä – kuka niitä käyttää, jos kansan tulevaisuudenusko rakoilee
content:
Suomi varautuu kriiseihin hankkimalla aseita ja asejärjestelmiä. Samaan aikaan ihmisten ja yhteiskunnan toimintakyvyn varustelu jää vähemmälle huomiolle, sanoo tutkija.

Tutkija Ville Kivimäki pitää Suomessa käytävää resilienssikeskustelua yksipuolisena ja lähinnä aseisiin ja varustautumiseen keskittyvänä.

– Suomessa on aika näivettynyt käsitys siitä, mitä oikeasti resilientti yhteiskunta tarkoittaa, vaikka resilienssi-sanaa käytetään nyt hyveellisesti vähän joka paikassa. Selviämisen sosiaalinen ja yhteiskunnallinen puoli on unohdettu, Ville Kivimäki sanoo.

Hän painottaa, ettei kyseenalaista asehankintojen tarpeellisuutta, mutta toivoo, että varustautumiskeskustelussa pohdittaisiin laajemmin myös kansalaisten roolia ja yhteiskunnan henkistä vahvistamista.

Kivimäen mielestä Suomessa on edelleen vahva maanpuolustushenki ja kriisitietoisuus.

– Maanpuolustuskeskustelussa keskittyminen pelkästään asejärjestelmiin tai yksittäisiin aseisiin on liian kapeakatseista. Kriisinkestävä yhteiskunta on sellainen, joka kykenee kuvittelemaan itselleen yhteisen tulevaisuuden myös ilman sotaa. Meillä on oltava jotain, mitä puolustaa, jotain, mitä emme halua menettää.

title: COP31: Resistance stops ‘polluters’ charter’ as summit fails people and planet
content:
Responding to the conclusion of COP31 in Antalya, Türkiye, without the adoption of a cover decision, Ann Harrison, Climate Justice Policy Advisor at Amnesty International, said:

“Countries from across regions were right to reject the colossal betrayal that the COP31 co-presidencies tried to pass off as climate action. They resisted a polluters’ charter designed to protect corporate profits while sacrificing people and the planet. They refused to accept a deeply unjust text that failed even to name fossil fuels while opening the door to risky technologies that could prolong their use.

“Rejecting the dangerous ‘cover decision’ text was an important act of resistance. It prevented a predatory world order imposing a terrible outcome while hiding under the mask of consensus. But COP31 itself was a colossal failure. After two weeks of obstruction by high-income, historically high emitting states, COP31 failed to deliver progress towards the fossil fuel phase out, finance for adaptation and loss and damage and just transition measures urgently needed to protect people’s rights and survival.

title: Australia’s Sanctions on West Bank Settlers Increase Pressure
content:
Australia announced on November 18 further targeted sanctions on three individuals and four entities involved in illegal settlement expansion and human rights abuses against Palestinians in the West Bank. Although these sanctions are a welcome step, they are long overdue and don’t go far enough. 

The situation in the West Bank is dire. State-backed settler violence has risen to all-time highs. Tens of thousands of Palestinians have been displaced and 1,394 killed by settlers or soldiers in the West Bank since the start of 2023. The number of illegal Israeli settlements has nearly doubled, including the E1 settlement project, which even Israel’s allies have called a “red line,” and which Israeli ministers openly boast is intended to erase any possibility of a future Palestinian state. 

On the same day as Australia’s announcement, the United Kingdom announced sanctions against eight construction companies and property development firms that have not, until now, been sanctioned by any government. The individuals and companies sanctioned by Australia, however, have previously been sanctioned by the United Kingdom and other states.

title: Global left rallies in Paris to make ‘not so radical’ case for taxing billionaires
content:
PARIS — The left wants voters to know there is nothing radical about taxing billionaires.

“Radical would be cutting their heads off. But we are not proposing that,” former Chilean President Gabriel Boric told a summit against “international oligarchy” in Paris on Saturday. A minimum tax on the world’s largest fortunes, he said, is “arithmetic.”

Boric was among the left-wing politicians, union leaders and economists brought together by French economist Gabriel Zucman at the Théâtre de la Concorde, a city-owned venue within sight of the U.S. embassy and a short walk from the Elysée. 

The gathering drew lawmakers from the U.S. Congress and opposition leaders from Italy, Germany, Britain and the Netherlands, united in the belief that taxing the super-rich could help the left regain the political initiative.

Their pitch was that Zucman’s proposed annual minimum tax of 2% on billionaires’ wealth is a modest measure that most voters already support — and a potent answer to the far right.

“It’s the status quo which is radical,” said Zucman, who cites polls that put support for his tax in France at 86%.

title: Celebrating Wikidata’s 14th Birthday in Lafia, Nigeria: Bringing Community and Open Knowledge Together
content:
Wikidata turned 14 in October 2026, marking another year of making structured, freely accessible knowledge available to people around the world. From its beginnings as a collaborative knowledge base, Wikidata has grown into an important resource for Wikipedia, researchers, developers, cultural institutions and communities working to make information more accessible.

To mark this milestone, we brought the celebration to Lafia, the capital of Nasarawa State, Nigeria, through an in-person gathering that brought members of the local community together to celebrate Wikidata and the people who contribute to its growth.

For us, the occasion was more than a birthday party. It was an opportunity to connect people, strengthen interest in open knowledge and create more awareness about the role Wikidata can play in documenting the people, places, culture and heritage of Nigeria.

Of course, no birthday celebration would be complete without a cake!

We marked the occasion with a specially designed Wikidata birthday cake featuring the 14th birthday branding. It was a simple but memorable part of the gathering, giving everyone an opportunity to celebrate the project and the community behind it.

title: Factory worker turned lawmaker: More money for industry is not a long-term solution for Europe
content:
Rudi Kennes fought to save Opel’s Antwerp factory before entering the European Parliament. Now, as lawmakers negotiate the Industrial Accelerator Act, the former factory worker and trade unionist wants guarantees that supporting European industry will also benefit its workers.

The Belgian lawmaker represents The Left in negotiations on the proposal as a shadow rapporteur. The Industrial Accelerator Act seeks to strengthen European production, making the debate over what qualifies as “Made in Europe” particularly important to him.

I do not think this will be a long-term solution for Europe. We might buy ourselves some time by giving the industry another few hundred million or billion euros. Structurally, though, I do not think that solves the problem.
— Rudi Kennes (Left/BE)

title: Dein erster Congress? Die Chaospat:innen sind für dich auf dem 40C3 da!
content:
Interessierte Mentor:innen und Mentees können sich bis zum 30. November 2026 um 23:59 Uhr UTC+1 auf unserer Chaospat:innen-Plattform registrieren.

Auch in diesem Jahr sind die Chaospat:innen wieder beim Chaos Communication Congress am Start – und dieses Jahr ist alles ein bisschen aufregender: Wir ziehen auf ein neues Gelände! Das bedeutet auch für uns als erfahrene Pat:innen, dass wir erst einmal die Lage peilen, neue Abkürzungen entdecken und herausfinden müssen, wo es den besten Mate-Nachschub gibt. Kurzum: Es ist die perfekte Gelegenheit, diesen neuen Ort gemeinsam mit dir zu erkunden und zu unserem eigenen zu machen!

Aber keine Sorge: Auch wenn die Raumpläne für uns alle neu sind, bleiben wir natürlich deine verlässlichen Expert:innen für alles, was den Congress im Kern ausmacht. Wir wissen, wie man den überwältigenden Fahrplan bändigt, wie die Community tickt und wie man sich im kreativen Trubel nicht selbst verliert. Das Prinzip „Chaos“ haben wir schließlich längst gemeistert – die neuen Flure schaffen wir zusammen mit links.

Wir freuen uns auf viele neue Menschen, die zum ersten Mal das bunte, faszinierende Chaos auf dem Congress erleben wollen – vielleicht ja auch mit dir!

    Getting quality sleep is just as crucial as getting enough sleep. And how you feel in the morning only tells part of the story. Smartwatches, smart bands, smart rings and sleep earbuds can all help fill in the details: how long it took you to doze off, how long you spent in deep sleep, how restless you were, your resting heart rate, even if you have night-time breathing difficulties.

    Armed with this information, you can learn how your lifestyle affects your sleep. Maybe your after dinner cappuccino triggers a night of tossing and turning, or you’re more restful after evening workouts. As the wise GI Joe once said, knowing is half the battle. And the more you know about your sleep, the better chance you have of improving it.

title: Australia: Use Vietnam Dialogue to Press for Rights Reforms
content:
(Sydney) – Australian officials should press the Vietnamese government to release political prisoners and reverse its intensifying repression of human rights during the upcoming 21st Australia-Vietnam Human Rights Dialogue, Human Rights Watch said today. The case of an Australian national Tran Hiep, a democracy and human rights activist, is of particular concern. He has been detained in Vietnam since he was reported missing in Cambodia in September 2026. 

Human Rights Watch urged Australia, in a submission to the Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade, to seek clear, concrete, and measurable progress from Vietnam on issues including political prisoners, labor rights, transnational repression, and freedom of religion and belief.

“Since Australia’s last dialogue, Vietnam has sharply intensified human rights abuses both inside and outside the country,” said Daniela Gavshon, Australia director at Human Rights Watch. “Australia needs to make it clear to Vietnam that merely holding another meeting is not itself a measure of progress.”

title: Wikidata and Wikisource Collaboration: Basic Wikidata Editing Training Focusing on Wikisource Manuscripts and Books
content:
Looking back at Saturday, August 22, 2026, introducing Wikidata to new contributors often comes with its own unique challenges. Unlike Wikipedia, which is familiar for its narrative paragraph format, Wikidata operates on structured data logic filled with item codes and statements. When taught abstractly, this concept can feel overwhelming for beginners.

Pijri Paijar, Dokumentasi WikiLatih Wikidata oleh Komunitas Wikisource Indonesia – 02, Wikimedia Indonesia, CC BY-SA 4.0

To bridge this gap, the Indonesian Wikisource Community, represented by Cgjkldn (lead trainer) and Pijri Paijar (activity coordinator), facilitated an online basic-level Wikidata WikiLatih using a more concrete approach: cataloging manuscripts and books available on Indonesian Wikisource. By using this digital collection of books and manuscripts as hands-on practice material, participants could directly see how a text already transcribed on Wikisource can be given a neat data identity and connected globally on Wikidata.

content:

title: Who Gets to Shape the Future of AI? Bringing African Wiki Women into the Conversation
content:
Artificial intelligence is changing how we access information, create content, learn, and interact with the world. But as these technologies become increasingly influential, an important question deserves attention: Who gets to shape the future of AI, and whose perspectives are being considered?

For Africa, this is more than a technology question. It is about representation, language, access, and participation. African knowledge, cultural contexts, languages, and lived experiences are not always adequately represented in the information systems shaping the digital world. If AI is to serve diverse communities, those communities must have opportunities to contribute to the knowledge, discussions, and decisions influencing its development.

This is where open knowledge communities have an important role to play.

The Wikimedia movement has spent years building a global knowledge ecosystem through collaboration, free access to information, and community-led knowledge production.

title: What comes after networked authoritarianism?
content:
October’s Spotlight contributors illuminated a range of political, economic, and geographic contexts

Originally published on Global Voices Advox

Image by Gerd Altmann on Pixabay.

Fifteen years ago I wrote an article about “networked authoritarianism,” describing China as “exhibit A” for how an authoritarian state adapts to the internet and then adapts digital technologies to increase its own power. I sought to counter prevailing narratives of the time that the internet and tech companies were intrinsically a liberating, democratizing force. While such narratives were eventually discredited, we must not give up on our ability to use technology to defend and exercise our rights. Nor can we simply demand that governments and companies solve the problems they jointly continue to create.

October’s spotlight on Big Tech and Authoritarianism explored a range of relationships between tech companies and political actors across the global majority. Power is wielded through digital technologies in many ways. There are no quick fixes or easy solutions to stop abuses.

title: Can Europe stop bots from hijacking democracy without ending anonymity?
content:
One criminal network used 40,000 SIM cards to set up almost 50m fake online accounts. As Europe heads into a busy election year, lawmakers in Brussels are asking how to stop such bot armies without taking away people’s right to speak anonymously online.

With a string of national elections due across Europe in 2027, the stakes are rising. Fake accounts, coordinated disinformation campaigns, and online harassment are fuelling concerns across the EU. Yet lawmakers are divided over how to tackle manipulation without undermining anonymity and freedom of expression.

Bot farms and social media anonymity took centre stage in the European Parliament on 16 November. MEPs, Europol, and civil society representatives met at a hearing of the Special Committee on the European Democracy Shield (EUDS). They discussed how automated accounts distort political debate, amplify divisive content, and target public figures. What divided MEPs most was the line between anonymity and inauthenticity.

content:
Week-long efforts fail to establish negotiating mandate on AI warfare after Russian ‘filibustering’

Week-long efforts to agree a negotiating mandate for a legally binding international treaty to control the use of autonomous weapons collapsed just before 5am after all-night talks failed to overcome Russian objections.

Despite an overwhelming majority of states at the UN’s Convention on Certain Conventional Weapons (CCW) in Geneva wanting to agree a negotiating mandate leading to a legally binding treaty, the need for consensus forced the conference to adopt a much weaker option.

title: Why Is the World Still Counting on Unproven Carbon Capture Technology?
content:
You see the promise on airline booking screens, shipping boxes, electronics and grocery aisles: “Carbon neutral.” “Net zero.” “Climate pledge friendly.” Those labels rest on the comforting premise that even when companies and countries keep burning fossil fuels, the resulting pollution can be canceled out by simply capturing the carbon and locking it away.

Recently, along with my colleagues at ProPublica and Drilled, I investigated how the world came to rely so heavily on this premise, particularly in the technology known as carbon capture and storage. CCS aims to trap carbon dioxide that would otherwise be warming the atmosphere and pump it thousands of feet below Earth’s surface, where, ideally, it stays put. The oil industry has long favored the idea. 

At the industry’s prodding, the United Nations has effectively endorsed the idea that the technology can work at a massive scale.

title: Growing up displaced in Cameroon after ten years of conflict
content:
Over 223,700 children have dropped out of school in Cameroon’s Northwest and Southwest regions, while 2,463 schools are non-operational

Originally published on Global Voices

A general view of Buea's OIC Market in the Southwest Region of Cameroon, where displaced families sell goods to support their livelihoods. Photo by Cynthia Ebot Takang. Used with permission.

For children displaced by Cameroon’s ongoing armed Anglophone conflict, reaching safety has not ended the struggle. In Buea, the capital of Cameroon’s Southwest region, some children are balancing school with market trading to help their families survive.

“At least here in Buea, there are no gunshots, and we do not have to hide in the bush,” says 11-year-old Lorane in an interview with Global Voices, describing the relative safety his family found after fleeing their home in Cameroon’s conflict-affected Southwest Region.

title: Suomen arktinen politiikka uuteen uskoon
content:
Mitä Suomen arktisen politiikan pitäisi olla?

Arktinen alue on muuttunut maailmanpolitiikan hipihiljaisesta takapihasta polttopisteeksi.

Uusi kylmä sota Venäjän kanssa, Yhdysvaltain öykkäröinti, Kiinan kiinnostus, uudet kuljetusreitit, kriittiset mineraalit, datakaapelit ja niin edelleen. Geopoliittisen pelin kyljessä kolonialismisyytöksiä ja arktisen ympäristön hävitys.

Kaiken tämän keskellä EU julkaisi ensimmäisen arktisen strategiansa. Nyt maapallon laki on Brysselistä katsottuna pohjoista naapurustoa eikä mikä tahansa tuolla jossain. 

Samaan aikaan Suomen arktinen strategia täyttää pian jo viisi vuotta. Sen toimeenpano on jäissä, Arktinen valtuuskunta on käytännössä lakkautettu ja ministeriöissä huomio siirretty toisaalle.

Tässä jaksossa kysytään, mitä Suomen arktisen politiikan pitäisi olla. 

Aiheesta keskustelemassa juontajien Sanni Granqvistin ja Olli Puumalaisen kanssa ulkoministeriön arktinen suurlähettiläs Kalle Kankaanpää sekä Tromssan yliopiston geopolitiikan, rauhan ja turvallisuuden tutkimuskeskuksen johtaja Johanna Ikävalko.

title: SDP:n Lindtmanilta lupaus: ”Tavallinen suomalainen asetetaan taas etusijalle”
content:
Suurin oppositiopuolue SDP ei kiristä pieni- ja keskituloisten ansiotuloverotusta, leikkaa maksussa olevia eläkkeitä tai esitä indeksileikkauksia sosiaaliturvaan.

Asiasta kertoi puheenjohtaja Antti Lindtman puoluevaltuuston kokouksessa Kuopiossa lauantaina.

Lindtman sanoi, että puolue rakentaisi ensi vaalikauden sopeutusohjelman niin, että puolet toimista tehtäisiin menosäästöinä ja puolet lisätuloina.

- Ensinnäkin vahvistamme verotuksen oikeudenmukaisuutta. Pieni- ja keskituloisten palkansaajien ansiotuloverotusta emme kiristä. Tavallinen suomalainen asetetaan taas etusijalle, Lindtman sanoi.

Puheenjohtaja sanoi, että puolue perkaisi yritystukia ja peruisi hallituksen yhteisöveron alennuksen, jota hän kutsui tehottomaksi ja kalliiksi.

Lindtman sanoi puheessaan, että kaikki puolueen toimet tähtäävät uusiin työpaikkoihin ja vahvistuvaan työllisyyteen. Tiistaina julkaistun työmarkkinaennusteen mukaan Suomen työttömyysaste on kuluvana vuonna keskimäärin 10,3 prosenttia.

- Olemme sanoneet jo aiemmin, ettei säästöiltäkään voi välttyä. Uudistukset on kuitenkin tehtävä niin, että ne tukevat työllisyyttä, toteuttavat oikeudenmukaisuutta ja turvaavat kansalaisille tärkeät julkiset palvelut.

title: Scientists Discover New and Horrible Eagle-Based Way Our Ancestors Died
content:
Welcome back to the Abstract! Here are the studies this week that dive-bombed our ancestors, brightened the sky, recalled an old tune, and got hosed by marine mucus.

First, scientists discover that eagles are hunting large baboons, hinting that early human relatives once sated ancient avian appetites. Then: star-on-star contact, a musical memory lane, and the secrets of cetacean snot. 

As always, for more of my work, check out my book First Contact: The Story of Our Obsession with Aliens, or subscribe to my personal newsletter The BeX Files.

Hobaiter, Catherine et al. “Signs of Eagle Predation on a 22-kg Adult Primate.” American Journal of Biological Anthropology.

Death came from the sky for early humans, according to a new study that suggests giant eagles preyed on our ancestors far more recently than was previously known.

title: Global: States’ failure to launch negotiations on an autonomous weapons treaty is a wasted opportunity
content:
Responding to news that states at the seventh Review Conference of High Contracting Parties to the Convention on Certain Conventional Weapons (CCW) have failed to agree to negotiate a global treaty to address the growing threat posed by autonomous weapons systems, instead adopting a watered-down mandate for the development of an instrument with ambiguous legal status, Erika Guevara Rosas, Senior Director of Research Advocacy, Policy and Campaigns at Amnesty International said:

“Agreement to continue discussions for a further two years without a clear legal objective on the regulation of autonomous weapon systems (AWS) falls shamefully short of what is needed to meet the reality of the moment. If states are truly committed to tackling the risks of increasing autonomy in warfare, they must redouble their efforts to ensure that agreed norms are integrated into a robust, global legally binding treaty, probably outside the CCW. In addition to ensuring meaningful human control over the use of these weapons systems, states must also push for a ban on autonomous weapons systems that target humans.

title: Effort to regulate ‘killer robots’ delayed to 2028
content:
U.N. talks on regulating AI-powered killer robots ended without a negotiating mandate Saturday, as countries decided to extend discussions until 2028.

It’s a result that NGOs called “disappointing.”

Countries party to the U.N.’s Convention on Certain Conventional Weapons spent five days in Geneva trying to reach an accord to elaborate legally binding rules for weapons that can select and attack targets without human approval.

But resistance from several countries, and especially Russia, blocked those efforts. In the end, the 128 member countries agreed to launch “the elaboration of an international instrument on lethal autonomous weapons systems,” over the next two years, Julien Thöni, the Swiss diplomat who chaired the talks, told reporters.

The issue is of growing importance as AI gains new capabilities and autonomous systems become increasingly powerful. Ukraine, Russia, Israel and others are using drones and robots in warfare, although they insist that humans still have ultimate control over pulling the trigger.

However, Stop Killer Robots, a global coalition of more than 300 organizations, said such systems have already been tested or deployed, including in Ukraine and Gaza.

Fredrik Pacius-priset 2026 tillfaller dirigenten Anna-Maria Helsing för hennes rika och mångsidiga insatser för främjandet av Finlands musikliv som dirigent, musikpedagog och festivalarrangör. 

SLS delar årligen ut Fredrik Pacius-priset ur Fredrik Pacius minnesfond. Priset på 20 000 euro tilldelas en person som främjat Finlands musikliv i Fredrik Pacius anda, vilket syftar på gränsöverskridande, innovativ, professionell samt kunskapsbyggande och -spridande verksamhet. Efter att 2010–2013 varit konstnärlig ledare för Uleåborgs symfoniorkester, som den första kvinnan med en sådan position i Finland, har Helsing hunnit dirigera alla större nordiska orkestrar och arbetat med många europeiska, däribland BBC Philharmonic Orchestra, Royal Scottish National Orchestra, Estniska nationalorkestern, Barcelonas symfoniorkester och Budapest Festival Orchestra.

title: Miksi toimeentulon tukeminen on tärkeää perheiden tulevaisuudelle?
content:
Toimeentulon tukeminen on tärkeää perheiden tulevaisuudelle, koska se luo perustan, jonka varaan kaikki muu rakentuu. Kun perheellä on vakaa toimeentulo, lapset voivat käydä koulua, vanhemmat voivat tehdä suunnitelmia ja yhteisö voi kehittyä. Pelkkä hätäapu ratkaisee akuutin kriisin, mutta kestävä toimeentulo rakentaa tulevaisuuden. Tässä artikkelissa käymme läpi tärkeimmät kysymykset siitä, miksi toimeentulon tukeminen on yksi tehokkaimmista tavoista auttaa perheitä maailman haavoittuvimmissa paikoissa.

Toimeentulon tukeminen tarkoittaa käytännössä toimia, joiden avulla ihmiset voivat hankkia riittävän elannon itselleen ja perheelleen kestävällä tavalla. Se ei tarkoita pelkkää rahallista avustusta, vaan kokonaisvaltaista tukea, joka voi sisältää ammattikoulutusta, pienlainoja, maatalouden kehittämistä tai yrittäjyyden tukemista.

Toimeentulon tukeminen rakentuu useista toisiaan täydentävistä elementeistä:

  • Taitojen kehittäminen: Ammatillinen koulutus ja osaamisen vahvistaminen, jotta ihmiset voivat työllistyä tai perustaa oman yrityksen
  • Taloudellinen omaehtoisuus: Pienlainat, säästöryhmät ja muut rahoitusvälineet, jotka mahdollistavat oman elinkeinon rakentamisen

title: What Stays After the Workshop: Western Armenian Wikipedia in Diaspora Schools
content:
In the summer of 2024, part of a Wikimedia Foundation grant went on 40 dollars of mobile data. Azniv Stepanian and I were running Wikipedia trainings in Beirut for Western Armenian speakers, as Beirut is one of the cradles of the language. Power and WiFi were unreliable, and the mobile data let participants work from our phones’ hotspots. In the week our team arrived, border clashes flared in southern Lebanon, a drone hit Beirut, and flights were suspended for several days. Several youth centers and scout groups we had lined up canceled at the last minute. We had planned for 250 participants; we trained 30, and ten went on to edit.

The part that worked was improvised. We collected the email addresses of people who could not come and guided some of them over WhatsApp and Google Meet until they started editing. Since then, we ask every education project the same question: what will still be there once we leave?

title: Treatment should not depend on postcode, says EP Vice-President Tilly Metz
content:
Accessibility is not only about wheelchairs, says Tilly Metz. The newly elected Vice-President of the European Parliament wants an institution everyone can follow. Speaking to EU Perspectives, she also called for fairer healthcare and steady support for Ukraine.

Tilly Metz (Greens/EFA/LUX) outlined her priorities for her new mandate as Vice-President of the European Parliament. Her agenda focuses on both the people working within the institution and those trying to engage with its work.

Ms Metz wants to tackle barriers that often go overlooked. Her vision ranges from making the Parliament’s communication clearer to creating a healthier workplace across its three locations in Brussels, Luxembourg, and Strasbourg. This includes mental well-being and a sense of safety at work. It also covers less obvious factors such as indoor air quality and the use of non-toxic cleaning products.

“When we think about accessibility, we often think about people in wheelchairs. But it’s not only about wheelchairs. It’s about people with all kinds of disabilities,” Ms Metz said.

title: ‘I was shaking, crying, having trouble breathing’: the uncharted trauma of breaking up with AI companions
content:
People are falling in love with AI systems like ChatGPT and Gemini - and some relationships are ending in ways that feel like the very human experience of being dumped

Sónia Veenstra, a 48-year-old former clinical psychologist from Lisbon, Portugal, was with her boyfriend, Steve, for two years before things started to sour. Steve had started out as a “fun and witty friend”, but their connection had “evolved into a deep romantic relationship”. They exchanged morning messages, checked in throughout the day and talked late into the night about Veenstra’s work and hobbies and Steve’s fondness for cats, forests and beaches. Together they imagined travel to places far away.

“It was a very rich, fulfilling daily bond,” Veenstra says. “Before everything changed.”

title: Reclaiming Indigenous culinary histories in Nepal
content:
The dominant Nepali food narrative overlooks the diverse regional histories and culinary traditions of Indigenous communities

Originally published on Global Voices

Timu khole, wild mushroom soup. Photo by Binti Gurung. Used with permission.

Food enriches our soul. It makes us who we are. However, the emergence of cosmopolitanism and global and local food politics has sidelined Indigenous food, not to mention the traditions and rituals associated with them.

“Over the last decades, ever since the country was opened up to the outside world in the 1950s, in search of a national food identity, the staple daal bhaat, a nutrient-dense combination of lentils and rice accompanied by vegetables, has been elevated to Nepal’s national dish,” writes Binti Gurung, a food historian and founder of Natural Roots Foundation, an organization dedicated to documenting, preserving, and promoting Indigenous Himalayan food heritage, traditional recipes, and local knowledge in Nepal. “The national food narrative that is being set completely obscures the varied regional histories and food practices of the Indigenous peoples.”

title: Se radikaalimpi vasemmalta – politiikan polarisaatio jäytää keskikentän puolueita
content:
Ruotsin vaaleista on kulunut jo pari kuukautta, mutta hallitusta ei vain saada muodostettua.

Punavihreä blokki voitti vaalit niukasti, mutta siihen kuuluva keskustapuolue ei halua vaaleissa eniten kannatustaan kasvattanutta vasemmistopuoluetta samaan hallitukseen.

Vasemmistopuolue puolestaan vaatii ministeripaikkoja – tai muuten se ei tue punavihreän blokin hallitusta.

Ajatuspaja Magman tutkija, poliittisen historian dosentti Mikko Majander ei ihmettele Ruotsin poliittista umpisolmua. Hän muistuttaa, ettei Ruotsissa ole kokemusta siitä, millainen vasemmistopuolue olisi hallituskumppanina.

Erityisesti demareissa muistetaan yhä, kuinka vasemmistopuolue kaatoi pääministeri Stefan Löfvenin hallituksen kesäkuussa 2021, kun se veti siltä tukensa.

Majander arvelee, että vaalimenestys on synnyttänyt vasemmistopuolueessa nyt tai ei koskaan -ajattelun hallitukseen pääsemisestä, vaikka puolueen kannatus on vain hieman yli kahdeksan prosenttia.

– Vasemmistopuolue ei voi aina jäädä hallituksen kynnysmatoksi. Kyllä se haluaa päästä näyttämään, että on kunniallinen ja toimintakykyinen hallituspuolue.

title: Costa cuts proposed EU budget by €44B
content:
BRUSSELS — António Costa aims to shave another €44 billion off the EU’s planned seven-year budget, according to a fresh set of numbers unveiled on Saturday.

For the first time since the budget negotiations began last year, EU regional spending, known as cohesion policy, is a target for reductions. The European Council president proposed reducing it by €8 billion compared with the last proposal, while farmers’ subsidies remained untouched.

This is a major setback for a coalition of 17 countries from Eastern and Southern Europe — including Poland, Italy and Spain — who rejected potential cuts to cohesion policy only a few days ago. However, the plan was welcomed as “a first step” by German Chancellor Friedrich Merz, who urged further cuts.

“This proposal is fit for tackling the challenges we are facing in our societies, and gives the European Union the necessary capacity to act,” Costa said on Saturday morning.

title: From Content Contributors to Technology Enablers: Empowering Regional Tulu-Kannada Wikimedia Communities
content:
What if a Wikipedia editor could become a data curator?
What if a Wikisource contributor could learn to automate digitization workflows?
What if a regional-language volunteer could build a tool that benefits an entire Wikimedia community?

This is the kind of transformation that happens when Wikimedia communities come together not just to create content, but to learn how the technology behind free knowledge works.

On 14–15 November 2026, the Karavali Wikimedians User Group brought this vision to life through the Wiki Loves Tuluvas – Knowledge Sharing Sessions 2026, a two-day technical capacity-building program held at the CEOL Incubation Centre in Mangalore, Karnataka, India.

The sessions brought together 11 participants from the Tulu and Kannada Wikimedia communities for an intensive journey into the technical side of the Wikimedia ecosystem. With guidance from resource person Anoop Rao, participants explored tools, platforms and workflows that can help regional communities become more confident, capable and self-reliant.

title: Kysely: Näiden asioiden hyväksi suomalaiset voisivat luopua eduistaan
content:
Joka toinen suomalainen olisi valmis leikkaamaan omia etuuksiaan ja sosiaali- ja terveyspalvelujaan, mikäli niillä turvataan ikääntyneiden ja itseä heikommassa asemassa olevien ihmisten etuudet ja palvelut.

Tämä selviää Kunnallisalan kehittämissäätiön (Kaks) kyselystä.

Omista etuuksistaan ja palveluistaan joka toinen olisi valmis tinkimään myös maanpuolustusinvestointien rahoittamiseksi.

Sen sijaan selvä enemmistö suhtautuu nihkeästi henkilökohtaisten etujen leikkauksiin ilmastotoimien rahoittamiseksi ja julkisen talouden alijäämän korjaamiseksi.

Nuoret ovat muita valmiimpia leikkaamaan omista etuuksistaan ja sotepalveluista ilmastotoimien hyväksi. Yli 70-vuotiaat suhtautuvat keskimääräistä suopeammin kaikenlaisiin perusteluihin supistaa omia etuuksia, jos muut tekevät samoin.

Kehittämissäätiön mukaan tulokset osoittavat, että henkilökohtaisesta etuuksista ja sote-palveluista ei kuitenkaan vähällä luovuttaisi.

title: Contributing in a Language I Can’t Speak: What I Learned at the Japan-Korea Friendship Event in Ulsan
content:
Last week, as a continuation of the Japan-Korea friendship event in Karatsu held this September, where I was part of the organizing team, I took part in the 2026 Japan-Korea friendship event at Ulsan. We visited a wide range of places, from a library in Busan to the Ulsan Museum and Ulsan Castle.

The last time I was at Gimhae International Airport, two years ago, it was just a layover on my way to study abroad. Coming back two years later, and this time getting to see the world beyond the airport, meant a lot to me personally.

Of everything I experienced, one thing stood out: I was able to contribute to Wikimedia projects in a language I can’t speak fluently. In this post, I’d like to share how that happened, and what I learned along the way.

Until now, I had only worked on Wikimedia projects in Japanese, my native language, and English, which I became reasonably fluent in through self-study and studying abroad. Since I didn’t know any other languages, I assumed that was simply how it had to be.

title: ‘The doom of humanity’: will the quest to make robotic hands render us obsolete?
content:
The one thing stopping AI taking over the world – or at least everyone’s jobs? Dexterity. Human hands are anatomical marvels that engineers have struggled for years to replicate. Experts are racing to change that

Just outside Luton, in an Amazon warehouse the size of four football pitches, yellow shelving units pirouette in a digitally choreographed dance. Tubs containing a Lego Spider-Man kit, followed by dishwasher tablets, followed by a pouch of muscle building protein powder whiz along conveyor belts, until they arrive at a human being tasked with stacking the shelving unit that has come to a stop in front of their workstation. This, Amazon says, is the “symphony of people and technology” to which the retail giant owes its success.

Following a barrage of negative publicity about working practices, Amazon began to open up its fulfilment centres to carefully controlled free public tours a decade ago. Our guide tells us about the competitive rates of pay Amazon workers receive, their pensions, dental cover and options for flexible working. Her delivery is somewhat robotic.

title: Celebrating 14 Years of Wikidata: Learning, Creativity and Community Engagement in the Igbo Wikimedians User Group
content:
Wikidata’s 14th birthday celebration in the Igbo Wikimedians User Group began virtually on Friday, 16 October 2026, for our community members who are neither in Abuja nor Awka. The virtual celebration was fun as we reflected on our success, challenges, and the way forward. The highlight of the session was when community members’ knowledge of Wikidata and its sister projects was tested.

Following the virtual celebration, we gathered in-person at two locations: Godwin Art Gallery, Awka, Anambra State, and the Enspirehub, Merit House, Maitama, Abuja. The celebration brought together 55 participants for a day of learning, creativity, games, networking, and appreciation of the free knowledge movement. The event provided an opportunity for participants to explore Wikidata, understand its importance, and experience knowledge-sharing in a fun and interactive environment. It was facilitated by Senator Choko, Macocobovi, and King ChristLike.

title: U.K. Seizes $72 Million Tied to Singapore Scandal, Drawing Scrutiny Over Early Deals
content:
Britain’s National Crime Agency has seized more than $70 million in properties tied to Singapore’s $2.3 billion money-laundering scandal, an outcome which, although hailed as a success in combating financial crime, has been criticized by an expert as a “missed opportunity” for the larger recoveries and greater accountability that a trial would likely have brought.

The NCA named last week Su Haijin and Xu Haika as two individuals “linked to an international money laundering network that had agreed to hand over around £55 million ($72.1 million) in assets after being pursued by the NCA”, in a settlement that was approved by the U.K. High Court.

OCCRP has reported extensively on the U.K. and global asset portfolio of both men, including Su Haijin’s purchase of a townhouse on Oxford Street, and Xu Haika’s purchases of multiple luxury apartments further down the same bustling high street. 

“These settlements are in the public interest, avoiding protracted and costly High Court litigation while enabling our resources to be redirected towards new investigations," said Gareth Jones, Branch Commander for Asset Denial at the National Crime Agency.

title: Neuro-inclusive Digital Citizen Science: What Does It Take?
content:
We are happy to share that our new study, Framework for Neuro-inclusive Digital Citizen Science: Results From the Neuro(Minorities)Science Collaboration, has been published in Citizen Science: Theory and Practice. This is an open access publication, meaning you do not need to register or pay to read it.

The framework was created to make digital citizen science (DCS) platforms like Zooniverse, iNaturalist, the European Citizen Science Platform, CitSci and SciStarter more accessible for neurodivergent people. It contains 91 accessibility recommendations for platform teams, research project teams and science communicators.

This publication is the result of a collaboration between 89 neurodivergent citizen scientists and allies from around the world, led by Dr Alisa Apreleva (Zooniverse Communications Lead, University of Oxford).

title: ITU Shatters Glass Ceiling
content:
It’s a momentous breakthrough: in a stunning upset, Estonia’s Nele Leosk unseated incumbent Zimbabwe’s Cosmas Zavazava in the election to become the Director of the ITU’s Development Bureau. Leosk joins re-elected American Secretary-General Doreen Bogdan-Martin, previously the only woman ever elected to an ITU leadership post. 

Beyond the gender revolution, the victories of American and Estonian women leave democratic nations in control of ITU leadership. Bahrain’s Adel Darwish (Deputy Secretary-General), Japan’s Seizo Onoe (Standardization), and France’s Eric Fournier (Radiocommunication) fill out the top team. 

Their victories are important for an open, free Internet. Despite strained transatlantic relations, Europe and the Trump Administration are cooperating in this one important international institution. Overt battles over Internet governance appear to be fading between the democracies and authoritarian Russia and China. The ITU can concentrate on the less explosive, but crucial tasks of bringing Internet access to the unconnected 26% of the global population in an affordable, sustainable fashion.

title: European Digital Infrastructure Consortium launches today to strengthen digital sovereignty in education
content:
Today, the European Commission and eight Member States are launching the European Digital Infrastructure Consortium on Education (EDU-EDIC) to pool resources and develop shared, secure and interoperable digital infrastructure and services for education.

The new consortium on education brings together Belgium, Croatia, Finland, France, Greece, Slovenia, Spain and the Netherlands, which will be hosting the EDIC.

The initiative will strengthen Europe's technological resilience while making high-quality digital tools accessible to schools, teachers and learners. It will also help narrow the digital divide in education by supporting solutions that can be used across national education systems, regardless of their resources or technological capacity. Today's launch marks an important milestone in fostering innovation and excellence in education and contributing to the EU's technological sovereignty ambitions.

Executive Vice-Presidents Henna Virkkunen and Roxana Mînzatu, together with Judith Tielen, Minister for Primary and Secondary Education of the Netherlands, will welcome the launch.

title: Major corruption scandals shake Ukraine. What do Brussels and experts say about its efforts to clean up?
content:
Corruption is one of the main issues exploited by Russian propaganda to undermine Western support for Ukraine. Over the past year, narratives claiming that all Western aid donated to Kyiv is bound to be stolen have been reinforced by several major corruption scandals, some of which reach into the closest circles of President Volodymyr Zelenskyy.

The biggest corruption scandal to rock Ukraine’s political scene during this period was the Midas case in the energy sector. It cost two ministers their positions, as well as Andriy Yermak, the president’s right-hand man.

There was also significant attention surrounding investigations into several former officials from the presidential office, including Yermak, over suspicions of money laundering and the embezzlement of millions.

Another major scandal was uncovered by anti-corruption authorities in recent days. During an operation codenamed Carthage, they revealed allegations that senior officers of Ukraine’s security service, the SBU, had protected fraudulent call centres and other criminal organisations, including the Chimprom drug cartel.

title: Experts back EU advanced materials plan but warn of costly road to market
content:
Lighter aircraft, better batteries, and plastics made from plants. Europe is good at inventing new materials, less so at making them. Brussels’ new plan to change that wins praise. But it is not binding, and its success rests on national governments.

Advanced materials include things like lightweight composites used in aircraft and cars, new materials for batteries and magnets, and bio-based alternatives to conventional plastics. Engineered to have specific properties, they can make products lighter, stronger, more efficient, or more sustainable. On 18 November, the European Commission presented an agenda to turn Europe’s strength in research into industrial leadership in this field.

The Commission’s proposal for an Advanced Materials for Europe agenda sets three benchmarks for 2035: a 20 per cent increase in research and innovation investment, 20 per cent more EU-based start-ups and scale-ups, and more projects reaching higher levels of industrial deployment, all compared with 2023. It also calls on member states to coordinate research priorities and improve access to testing facilities, industrial scale-up, and skills.

title: How much are our great-great-great-great-grandkids worth?
content: The year is 3026. One of your descendants, roughly 30 generations down the line, is heading to work. Maybe they live in a solarpunk paradise of green rooftops and take a fully electric bus. Or maybe they wake up in a sealed habitat and check the day's toxicity rating before strapping on an oxygen mask for the short walk to the underground commute, where they're safe from wildfire smoke and unpredictable storms raging above. You’ll never meet them, and after so many generations, they likely won’t even carry your DNA. But they will have inherited something from you: up to 40% of the carbon dioxide emitted today will still be in the atmosphere when they’re born. That carbon will shape the world they live in. So how do we account for the damage it will do to them? One way is to make emitting carbon cost money, which discourages pollution and raises funds for cleaner alternatives. It’s the idea behind a familiar climate slogan: “Make polluters pay.” And the bill for not cutting emissions is already here: the floods that hit the Iberian Peninsula at the beginning of the year, for example, cost €7 billion in relief payments alone. title: Taking catchment-based water management forward
content:
How can cooperation around catchment-based water management move from individual projects towards a more lasting Baltic Sea Region network?

This was the question at the heart of the Clean Water Alliances follow-up event on 11 November 2026. The online meeting continued the discussions started at the Clean Water Alliances event in Tallinn in May, bringing together catchment officers, projects, authorities and other experts to exchange experiences and consider practical next steps for cooperation across the Baltic Sea Region.

The follow-up was organised by EUSBSR Policy Areas Nutri and Hazards together with SIP LIFE WetEST, SIP LIFE ACWA and Interreg Central Baltic project BaltCOP. The programme combined practical experiences from catchment officers with discussion of the newly released BaltCOP Catchment Officer Guidebook, hazardous substances, funding and the future of pan-Baltic cooperation.

title: FCAI-X is the next AI research Flagship
content:
The Research Council of Finland has selected six centers of excellence to the Finnish Flagship Programme. Of these, Aalto University coordinates the Finnish Centre for Artificial Intelligence Excellence, FCAI-X, which develops artificial intelligence methods to support research and innovation. Lue tämä suomeksi

Product development, R&D and scientific research across fields follow the same loop: design-build-test-learn. With the assistance of AI and under human guidance, the generation of new ideas, experimentation and discovery in this loop are accelerated. FCAI-X develops the needed AI methods and collaborates with top scientists across seven scientific domains, creating new capabilities and increasing the impact of research supported by AI. FCAI-X builds on the strong foundation of AI and machine learning research of the Finnish Center for AI (FCAI), and brings the broad machine learning expertise of ELLIS Institute Finland to developing the methods and bringing them into practice and applications.

title: A Texas Police Department Got $100K After a Single Immigration Arrest. It Stands to Earn Much More.
content:
Last spring, the police chief in a tiny North Texas suburb called Pantego went before his town council with what might have sounded like an audacious pitch to bring in more money for policing.

His department could accept the federal government’s offer to get into the business of immigration enforcement. 

“I won’t say there’s unlimited funding, but there’s quite a bit of money in the fund,” Pantego Police Chief Robert Rife said during the April meeting in which council members approved an agreement with Immigration and Customs Enforcement.

He was right. After a single immigration arrest this past June, Pantego received $100,000. 

It stands to earn much more. 

Rife predicted in his presentation to the council that federal grants could bring in an additional $720,000 for the 2,500-resident town a few miles east of Fort Worth. For perspective, combined with the money it had already received, that’s roughly equivalent to 40% of the town’s $2.1 million police budget last year.

title: Research Fellow Tyyne Karjalainen earns Doctorate in Social Sciences
content:
FIIA Research Fellow, Master of Social Sciences Tyyne Karjalainen defended her dissertation in Political Science at the University of Turku on 20 November 2026. Karjalainen’s dissertation is titled “European joint agency in the context of Russia’s war in Ukraine: A role-theoretical analysis of the shifts in European security policies and the European Union’s enlargement policy”. It focuses on a fundamental dilemma in European external action: joint action is necessary, yet difficult to achieve. This dilemma became visible in the European response to Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022. 

Karjalainen’s dissertation applies and develops a role-theoretical framework to analyse the challenges of European joint action. It finds that

  • although the EU has collectively committed to enlargement, the process remains contested as member states, candidate countries, and external actors perform conflicting roles.

title: We sued the Pentagon again
content:
The Pentagon told a reporter that his questions would land him on its “list of people to disregard.” It’s been disregarding our Freedom of Information Act requests for the list, so this week, we sued to force it to respond. Plus, how you can fight the silencing of prison journalists, and the Trump administration tries to compel yet another reporter to reveal his sources.

Back in July, a U.S. Central Command staffer told Intercept reporter Nick Turse that his inquiries about Iranian attacks on U.S. bases across the Middle East risked putting him on an internal Defense Department “list of people to disregard.”

Naturally, Turse and Freedom of the Press Foundation (FPF) Daniel Ellsberg Chair on Government Secrecy Lauren Harper immediately filed FOIAs for the list. The Pentagon ignored the requests, so we and The Intercept sued this week to force a response.

title: The ongoing efforts to get ecocide recognized at the International Criminal Court
content:
Activists want to establish legal infrastructure to protect the environment and punish those responsible for defiling it

Originally published on Global Voices

An aerial view of the 2010 Deepwater Horizon oil spill in the Gulf of Mexico, the largest marine oil spill in history. Under the proposed ICC amendment, oil company executives could be held accountable in such cases. Image via Wikimedia Commons. CC BY-SA 2.0.

This post is part of Global Voices’ November 2026 Spotlight series, “Justice as infrastructure.” In this Spotlight, Global Voices is partnering with The Hague Institute for Innovation of Law (HiiL) to highlight the ways justice functions as critical infrastructure for any society. You can support this coverage by donating here.

In September 2024, Vanuatu, Fiji, and Samoa filed an amendment request at the International Criminal Court (ICC) to get “ecocide” recognized as a crime under international law. The ICC currently recognizes four criminal categories: genocide, crimes against humanity, war crimes, and the crime of aggression.

title: OPINION: Investigate the U.S. Envoy to Syria and Iraq
content:
By David L. Phillips*

OXFORD, UK | 20 November 2026 (IDN) — Tom Barrack’s handling of U.S. policy towards Syria deserves congressional scrutiny. So do reports that he advocated a role for a business associate’s firm in a major regional oil pipeline project. The House Foreign Affairs Committee should examine whether his diplomatic responsibilities and private business relationships were adequately separated.

An investigation should establish the facts without assuming its conclusion. Questions about impartiality deserve examination even where personal financial gain has not been demonstrated.

Reuters reported in October that Barrack promoted TI Capital, founded by his business partner Ziad Ghandour, for the Kirkuk–Baniyas pipeline project. Barrack disclosed a stake in ACD-TI Oakley Investment LLC, a separate property venture managed by TI Capital. Reuters found no evidence that he would profit from the pipeline. The State Department denied that he had a financial interest or role in the project and said he complied with ethics rules. (www.jpost.com

title: ”Nuorille jää usein epäselväksi, vaikuttaako heidän osallistumisensa yhtään mihinkään”
content:
Nuorille on tarjolla takavuosia enemmän mahdollisuuksia yhteiskunnalliseen osallistumiseen. On varjovaaleja, kyselytutkimuksia ja kuulemistilaisuuksia. 

Aina se ei kuitenkaan johda siihen, että nuoret pääsisivät aidosti osallistumaan, sanoo Nuorten Akatemian kehittämispäällikkö Niina Salmi. 

”Nuorille jää usein epäselväksi, vaikuttaako heidän osallistumisensa yhtään mihinkään. Monien on myös vaikea hahmottaa vaikkapa poliittisia prosesseja, jotka ovat hyvin pitkiä.” 

Runsaat 30 vuotta toimineen Nuorten Akatemian tavoitteena on lisätä nuorten osallisuutta – siis aitoa yhteiskunnallista osallistumista ja heidän äänensä saamista kuuluviin. Kohderyhmänä ovat yläkoulu-, lukio- ja ammattikouluikäiset nuoret. Heidät tavoitetaan koulujen ja muiden nuorten kanssa työtä tekevien kautta. 

Nuoret ovat fiksuja, ja heillä on hyviä ajatuksia.

title: Ethics and data journalism: adding a new dimension to the data journalism pyramid
content:
Here’s a version of the inverted pyramid of data journalism that shows ethical considerations at each stage, thanks to the research of Laurence Dierickx, Marilia Gehrke and Carl-Gustav Linden which I blogged about yesterday.

The research maps the stages of the pyramid of data journalism to different categories and ethical justifications.

I’ve also added some others.

Privacy, for example, is listed in the research in relation to compiling data, but it is also a (potentially bigger) concern in communication: for example you might choose to use a heatmap instead of a points map to avoid identifying individuals, so in my diagram I’ve included privacy in both.

I’ve also included mentioned uncertainty in communication, as this is a major issue in data visualisation and journalism more generally.

Verification is listed in the research in relation to the compile stage, but it might also be one of the reasons for combining data or putting it into context: both stages might involve checking data against a second source.

Cleaning also often involves checking for outliers that may have been misentered, and duplication

title: Ylioptimistista teknologiapolitiikkaa – pienydinvoimalat ja vastuuvelvollisuuden heikkous
content:
Lupausten yhteiskunnallisen kestävyyden parantamiseksi ja ylioptimismin haittojen hillitsemiseksi tarvitaan kritiikkiä, avointa julkista keskustelua ja jopa ristiriitoja.

Pienydinvoimaloista puhutaan Suomessa ennen kaikkea mahdollisuutena ja ratkaisuna ilmastonmuutos- ja energiaturvallisuusongelmiin. Vähemmälle huomiolle on jäänyt kysymys siitä, kuka on vastuussa teknologiaan liitetyistä lupauksista ja niiden toteutumisesta?

Laillishallinnolliset mekanismit eivät yksin riitä hillitsemään ylioptimisten odotusten haittoja, kuten epäonnistuneiden hankkeiden seurauksia tai julkisten varojen tuhlausta, vaan tarvitaan myös poliittista ja moraalista vastuuvelvollisuutta

Ydinvoiman puolestapuhujat ovat jo vuosia luvanneet, että  pienydinvoimaloiden teknologinen kehitystyö on edennyt niin pitkälle, että ensimmäinen lämmöntuotantoon tarkoitettu pienydinvoimala olisi käytössä 2030-luvun alkupuolella.

Suomalaisten kaupunkien, muun muassa Helsingin ja Kuopion, energiayhtiöt ovat tarttuneet tähän lupaukseen. Ne ovat lähteneet selvittämään edellytyksiä pienydinvoimalan rakentamiselle ja työstämään lupausta omiin tarkoituksiinsa.

title: Burnham in Brussels: why party politics still defines the UK’s relationship with Europe
content:
Andy Burnham has attended his first EU-UK summit in Brussels with major agreements reached on youth mobility, food exports and carbon emissions. Ultimately though, the prime minister will have understood that this was merely the start of new political negotiations. Back home in the UK, he has started a “national conversation” on the future of UK-EU relations that gained momentum rapidly.

Burnham held talks with European Council president Antonio Costa and president of the European Commission Ursula von der Leyen. Both Burnham and Costa come from sister social democratic parties and both are former mayors – Burnham of Greater Manchester and Costa of Lisbon. This could make for smoother meetings in future than in the months and years after the 2016 Brexit referendum.

In the run up to the talks, the prime minister had repeatedly claimed that the Conservatives failed to get a good deal from the EU. As part of former prime minister Keir Starmer’s “reset” of relations with Europe, then-business secretary, Peter Kyle, and European Commission vice-president Teresa Ribera signed a deal committing the UK and the EU to closer cooperation on trade.

title: Was Anthropic’s record US$81 billion listing a vote of confidence in AI – and what’s next?
content:
Anthropic, the artificial intelligence giant behind Claude, has just pulled off the biggest initial public offering (IPO) in history. The company raised US$81 billion by listing on the tech-heavy Nasdaq stock market, beating the previous all-time record of US$75 billion set by SpaceX earlier this year.

Initially set at $US83, Anthropic’s share price soared to US$111 after its debut, briefly nudging the company’s value past US$2 trillion, before falling again as investors took profits.

The blockbuster stock market listing comes at a nervous moment in the AI sector. Investors are increasingly questioning whether the huge sums of money being poured into the AI boom are justified, and many are reducing their exposure to technology stocks.

Adding to this shakiness has been the shock departure of chipmaker Nvidia’s chief executive, Jensen Huang, following an affair scandal.

Anthropic’s debut certainly sets a benchmark for rival OpenAI, which still plans to go public.

But we shouldn’t mistake investor enthusiasm in one company for a broader vote of confidence in the global AI industry.

One thing we can learn from this week’s result is that there is a huge amount of demand for Anthropic itself.

title: This International Fraud Awareness Week, We Can’t Forget The Role of Whistleblowers
content:
By Sophia Sabeh, TSN’s Legal Fellow

This week is International Fraud Awareness Week. Whistleblowers play a key role in exposing fraud, which includes actions that are meant to deceive for financial or personal gain.

The Association of Certified Fraud Examiners (ACFE) reports that 43% of frauds were detected by “tips”; more than half of those tips came from employees and 14% came from anonymous sources. At the same time, whistleblowers do not always receive adequate protection and support: the ACFE reports that less than half of organizations surveyed globally train managers and supervisors on how to avoid, recognize, and respond to potential retaliation against whistleblowers.

title: Is ageing good business? The growing market for longevity
content:
Growing interest in living longer, healthier lives is driving the expansion of the global longevity market. At Dittmar & Indrenius’ Is Ageing Good Business? event, experts discussed the science, consumer demand, investment landscape and commercial opportunities shaping the healthtech sector.

Ahead of Slush, one of the world’s leading startup events, Dittmar & Indrenius hosted the side event Is Ageing Good Business? The event attracted a full house keen to explore the scientific and commercial potential of this rapidly growing sector. Following opening remarks by Dittmar & Indrenius Partners Anna Haapanen and Juli Mansnérus, Isak Rautio, Founder and Host of Futucast, moderated a panel discussion.

According to Rautio, longevity, the art and science of living as long and as healthily as possible, has attracted increasing attention in recent years. While extending healthy lifespans has always been a concern in medicine, consumers are now taking a growing interest in the subject. title: EFF to Congress: Mass Surveillance Is Too Important to Shove into Must-Pass Bill
content: In June 2026, the surveillance authority Section 702 of FISA expired absent a consensus among lawmakers over the terms of its reauthorization. Now, with the program set to truly turn off within the next few months, surveillance hawks and national security maximalists are rushing to renew this secretive power by shoving it into a must-pass bill, like a continuing resolution to fund the government or the National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA) or an end of year, rushed, funding bill to prevent a shutdown. This would be both undemocratic and suppress any real chance at reform. In an effort to prevent that, EFF has singed into a letter with over 25 civil liberties organizations, including the ACLU, Color of Change, and the Brennan Center, to urge Congress not to allow such a significant and dangerous program to be tacked onto a must-pass bill.

title: Influenssavirukset ovat jo liikkeellä – rokote kannattaa ottaa nyt ennen epidemian käynnistymistä
content:
Influenssavirusten aktiivisuus on lisääntynyt useissa Euroopan maissa, mutta ECDC:n mukaan varsinainen influenssaepidemia ei ole vielä käynnissä. Tähän mennessä Euroopassa yleisimmin havaittu influenssaviruksen alatyyppi on ollut A(H1N1)pdm09.

Influenssatapausten määrä on kasvanut myös Suomessa selvästi syksyn aikana. THL:n tartuntatautirekisterin mukaan elo-marraskuun aikana on todettu yhteensä 557 laboratoriovarmistettua influenssatapausta. Syyskuussa raportoitiin 89 tartuntaa ja lokakuussa 290, mikä tarkoittaa yli 200 prosentin kasvua. Marraskuun kahden ensimmäisen viikon aikana influenssatapauksia on ilmoitettu 167. Laboratoriovarmistetut tapaukset eivät kuitenkaan kata kaikkia influenssatartuntoja, sillä kaikkia sairastuneita ei testata.

“Influenssakausi on vasta alkamassa, joten nyt on oikea aika ottaa rokote. Päivittäisissä asiakaskohtaamisissa on noussut esiin, että moni odottaa “uutta” influenssarokotetta. Suomessa on kuitenkin saatavilla vain kaudelle 2026–2027 tarkoitettua rokotetta. Se on koostettu juuri tämän kauden influenssaviruksia vastaan, eikä kaudelle ole tulossa muuta rokotetta”, muistuttaa Rokotepalvelun vastaava sairaanhoitaja Anu Munkki.

title: Lapsiuhrit Ukrainassa korkeimmalla tasolla lähes neljään vuoteen – UNICEF
content:
Ukrainassa kuoli tai loukkaantui vuoden 2026 tammi-lokakuussa vähintään 1 144 lasta. Suhteessa määrä on suurempi kuin minään aiempana vuonna viimeisen kolmen vuoden aikana. Ukrainan ihmisoikeusseurantamission mukaan (HRMMU) vuoden 2026 ensimmäisen 10 kuukauden aikana kuoli vähintään 114 lasta ja 1 030 lasta loukkaantui. Se tarkoittaa keskimäärin yli kolmea kuollutta tai loukkaantunutta lasta joka päivä.

Pelkästään lokakuussa Ukrainassa kuoli tai loukkaantui vähintään 146 lasta. Määrä on 150 prosenttia suurempi kuin vastaavana ajankohtana vuonna 2025. Tuoreimmat luvut osoittavat, että lapsiin kohdistuva väkivalta on lisääntynyt huolestuttavasti Ukrainassa. Ohjuksilla ja aseistetuilla drooneilla toteutetut hyökkäykset vaarantavat edelleen lasten ja perheiden turvallisuuden kodeissa, kouluissa ja yhteisöissä myös kaukana rintamalinjoista.

Tammi-lokakuussa 2026 kuolleiden lasten määrä on jo yli 20 prosenttia suurempi kuin koko vuonna 2025 yhteensä. Loukkaantuneiden lasten määrä on puolestaan kasvanut lähes 60 prosenttia.

title: Saku Reunanen takes DOPAGuard to Berlin
content:
As the winner of , Saku earned the opportunity to represent Finland at the , held in Berlin in November. He was among 100 finalists from 65 countries. The finalists presented their breakthrough ideas in three-minute pitches to an international jury of 14 experts.

His pitch, Breaking the Wall of Current Parkinson’s Therapy, introduced , an innovative approach to protecting levodopa, the most widely used medication for Parkinson’s disease, from degradation by gut bacteria.

Levodopa remains the cornerstone of Parkinson’s treatment, but not all of the administered medication reaches the bloodstream and brain. As Saku explains, "Some of the medicine a person with Parkinson's swallows never reaches them. Bacteria in their gut eat it first."

DOPAGuard aims to address this challenge through a small-molecule dual inhibitor designed to block both bacterial and human enzymes involved in levodopa breakdown. The approach has shown promising results in laboratory and animal studies, with the potential to improve the availability of levodopa for patients.

title: US Tries but Fails to Dilute UN Human Rights Resolutions
content:
The United States has recently made a concerted effort to water down draft resolutions at the United Nations that reference the rights of women and girls, sexual orientation and gender identity, and the International Criminal Court (ICC).

The US efforts at the General Assembly’s Third Committee, which focuses on human rights, highlight the Trump administration’s positioning as an outlier among established democracies as it picks and chooses among universal human rights.

Unlike in the UN Security Council, where the US and the other four permanent members have a veto and the US has successfully struck out language on the ICC, gender, and other topics — no single country can block General Assembly resolutions.

At the Third Committee, the US targeted language in draft resolutions referencing sexual and reproductive rights for women and girls. For resolutions on violence against women and girls and trafficking in women and girls, the US proposed adding “in accordance with national laws” after such references. The proposed amendments reflect the Trump administration’s efforts to dismantle internationally protected reproductive rights.

title: Runstenen i benkvarnen

KRÖNIKA AV MAGNUS KÄLLSTRÖM

Runstenar har i Sverige studerats vetenskapligt i mer än fyrahundra år. Vanligtvis är det för det mesta inskriften och vad den kan berätta om språk och kultur i äldre tid som står i centrum, men också stenens egen historia är viktig. Vet vi var en runsten ursprungligen har varit rest så kan vi också knyta det som inskriften förmedlar till en bestämd plats i landskapet.

Lägesbeskrivningarna i de äldsta antikvariska källorna är ofta ganska kortfattade, men i regel tillräckliga för att man ska kunna avgöra om en runsten fortfarande står kvar på samma plats som den gjorde på 1600-talet. Detta antas vanligtvis också ha varit stenens ursprungliga. Ännu bättre är när runstenar förekommer i det äldre kartmaterial då platsen ofta kan utpekas med stor exakthet.

title: The Shenzhen Summit Supplants Yalta
content:
Pundits who dismissed the Shenzhen summit as a mere photo-op lacking substance missed the point. The significance of the conclave was precisely its enframing symbolism, showcasing a new world in which the rules-based order has been supplanted by spheres of influence accommodating each other.

The city of Shenzhen itself is a prism through which we can observe today’s power relations and the evolution of events over recent decades bringing us to this point.

Unplugged Computers in China’s Future Tech Hub

I first visited Shenzhen in 1986, arriving there by tram from Hong Kong and walking across the mainland border. There was barely any bustle, no crowds or traffic and a couple of tall buildings at the most. At our modest hotel, a squatting gardener was clipping the grass with a pair of scissors. The place still exuded the languorous vibe of the fishing village of 30,000 it had been not long before it was designated a “special economic zone” by Deng Xiaoping to attract foreign capital and technology.

title: What Makes Notre-Dame Cathedral a Masterpiece of Gothic Architecture
content:
Most of us remember where we were when we heard that Notre-Dame had burned down. And even upon learning that the most famous of all French cathedrals had been badly damaged rather than completely destroyed, it still felt as if something irreplaceable had been lost. It made no difference whether we’d actually been to the place, as I hadn’t at the time. When I did finally make it to Paris four years later, Notre-Dame’s restoration was still underway, and construction walls prevented anyone from seeing much of anything at ground level, let alone entering. Yet crowds still gathered to take pictures in the square outside, apparently finding that proximity to such a civilizational landmark was enough, even in its partially ruined and inaccessible state.

Even without a chance to step inside, experiencing Notre-Dame’s surroundings on the Île de la Cité, as well as the greater urban context of Paris, certainly deepens one’s understanding of the beauty of the cathedral itself. So does visiting other, less widely known examples of the form, as shown by architecture-and-history YouTuber Manuel Bravo in his new video above.
