title: French billionaire hunter takes fight global after California tax defeat
content:
PARIS — Gabriel Zucman wants to put the world’s billionaires on notice.

The 40-year-old French economist, who has spent more than a decade designing ways to tax the ultra-rich, hosts a summit against “international oligarchy” in Paris on Saturday. It comes less than three weeks after California voters rejected a billionaire tax he backed, in a campaign where Google co-founder Sergey Brin and other opponents spent more than $300 million to thwart the initiative.

“Everywhere, we see very, very strong popular support for taxing billionaires,” Zucman told POLITICO this week, arguing that his loss in California was only a minor setback. “That’s true even in the United States.”

Zucman sees fresh hope in the results of the U.S. midterms, in which a string of Democrats campaigning to tax the ultra-rich won their races.

“Now our party has a choice to make: Are we going to stand with the working class or the tech lords?” said Rep. Ro Khanna (D-Calif.), who is flying in for the Paris gathering. “The same inequality is fueling anger and distrust not only in America, but also in France and around the world,” he told POLITICO.

title: Pepparkakor vinner Årets Svenska Måltidslitteratur
content:
Yrsa Lindqvists bok Pepparkakor. En kryddig historia har tilldelats priset Årets Svenska Måltidslitteratur 2026 i kategorin Nordisk måltidslitteratur.

I sin prismotivering lyfter juryn fram den fascinerande historia som mat- och måltidsforskaren Lindqvist skildrar i Pepparkakor. Boken följer pepparkakans resa från medeltida medicin till älskat småbröd och visar hur exotiska kryddor hittade vägen till de nordiska köken. Samtidigt får läsaren svar på en fråga som länge väckt nyfikenhet: Finns det verkligen peppar i pepparkakan?

– Jag är väldigt glad för det här priset och den erkänsla det ger både för mig och för SLS förlag, säger Yrsa Lindqvist.

Pepparkakor innehåller ett urval pepparkaksrecept från de senaste 250 åren, vilka ger läsaren inblick i hur smakideal och baktraditioner förändrats över tid. Samtidigt speglar pepparkakans framfart genom århundraden och kulturer en större berättelse om kryddhandelns framväxt, globaliseringens långa rötter och de koloniala strukturer som möjliggjorde handeln med eftertraktade råvaror.

Priset delades ut vid en ceremoni på Kungl. Skogs- och Lantbruksakademien i Stockholm. Bakom utmärkelsen står Måltidsakademiens biblioteksstiftelse i Sverige.

title: Norjan korkein oikeus kumosi kolmen Pohjanmeren öljykentän luvat – ilmastovaikutukset jäivät arvioimatta
content:
Norjan korkein oikeus on mitätöinyt Breidablikkin, Yggdrasilin ja Tyrvingin kenttien luvat, koska hallitus ei ollut ottanut päätöksissään huomioon kentillä tuotettavan öljyn ja kaasun polttamisesta aiheutuvia ilmastovaikutuksia. Päätös annettiin perjantaina 13. marraskuuta. Se vahvistaa alempien oikeusasteiden aiemmat ratkaisut.

Oikeuden mukaan ympäristövaikutusten arvioinneissa on tarkasteltava myös hiilidioksidia, joka vapautuu siellä, missä polttaminen tapahtuu. Käytännössä tämä tarkoittaa, että Norjan on arvioitava myös ulkomailla poltettavan norjalaisen öljyn ja kaasun päästöt.

Equinor operoi Breidablikkia, Aker BP Yggdrasilia ja Tyrvingiä. Breidablikk ja Tyrving ovat jo tuotannossa. Yggdrasilin on määrä aloittaa tuotanto ensi vuonna.

title: WITNESS and partners launch Reality Check Initiative to Address the Impact of AI on Documentary
content:
WITNESS and a group of leading organizations from the documentary and visual journalism fields have co-created Reality Check, a cross-disciplinary initiative bringing together leaders from technology, archival preservation, research, human rights, and policy to address the growing impact of artificial intelligence on nonfiction media.

As generative AI becomes more common in media production and everyday life, it is changing how documentaries are made, shared, and understood. It raises important questions about what we can trust, how creative work is valued, and how AI is shaping public understanding of the world.

The initiative was developed in partnership with the Co-Creation Studio at MIT, the Archival Producers Alliance (APA), and the International Documentary Association (IDA). Together, the partners aim to strengthen collaboration, research, knowledge sharing, and collective action to help documentary and visual journalism communities navigate the challenges posed by AI.

title: Sudan – maailman suurin humanitaarinen kriisi
content:
TAUKOAMATON sota on kestänyt Sudanissa kolme ja puoli vuotta. Se on pakottanut yli 13,6 miljoonaa ihmistä jättämään kotinsa ja yli 33 miljoonaa ihmistä tarvitsee akuutisti humanitaarista tukea maassa, jossa avustusjärjestelmä on yhä pahemmin vaarassa kaatua.

Toisin kuin Ukrainan sota, maailman suurimmaksi humanitaariseksi kriisiksi luonnehdittu Sudanin tilanne tuskin yltää uutisotsikoihin. Myös avustustyöntekijät ovat olleet sotatoimien kohteena. Lokakuun alussa isku kohdistui Maailman ruokaohjelman WFP:n kuljetukseen, joka oli matkalla Etelä-Kordofan alueelle. Yhden ajoneuvon kuljettaja kuoli.

Siviilit ovat kolmen ja puolen viime vuoden aikana kärsineet paljon. Väkivallan pelon lisäksi monella on nälkä, ja avustusjärjestöjen toiminta Sudanissa on romahduksen partaalla.

“Minusta vaikuttaa siltä, että kriisi tulee vielä syvenemään. Tämän vuoden sadekausi ei ollut kovin hyvä, eli tilanne pahenee. Jos kansainvälinen yhteisö ei reagoi pian, suuri osa maasta saattaa joutua nälänhätään”, sanoo Mohamed Elsanousi, Kirkon Ulkomaanavun (KUA) perustaman uskonnollisten ja perinteisten toimijoiden rauhanverkoston toiminnanjohtaja.

title: Connecting Communities and Sharing Knowledge: My Experience at Wiki Indaba 2026 in Abidjan
content:
From 13 to 15 November 2026, I had the opportunity to participate in the Wiki Indaba 2026 conference in Abidjan, Côte d’Ivoire. The conference brought together Wikimedians, language activists, open knowledge advocates, and representatives of Wikimedia communities from across Africa to share experiences, discuss challenges, and explore opportunities for strengthening the movement on the continent.

Representing the Dagbani Wikimedians User Group, I was particularly excited to meet fellow Wikimedians, learn from their experiences, and explore ideas that could contribute to the growth of our community and other Mabia language projects.

Our presentation highlighted the importance of protecting indigenous languages in the digital space and how Wikimedia projects provide opportunities to document, preserve, and promote the Dagbani language and cultural heritage.

We also shared the work, experiences, and achievements of the Dagbani Wikimedians User Group, including our efforts to make Dagbani knowledge accessible to a global audience.

title: US Sanctions Italian Mafia Group in Canada and Australian Biker Gang with Global Footprint
content:
The latest U.S. sanctions against organized crime stretch from Canada, home to a powerful faction of an Italian mafia group, to Australia where an outlaw motorcycle gang grew into an international drug dealing organization.

Both the Comancheros motorcycle gang and the Toronto-based ‘Ndrangheta mafia faction have ties to Mexican cocaine cartels, according to a statement on Thursday by the U.S. Treasury Department. 

“The Comancheros and the ‘Ndrangheta operate sophisticated transnational criminal networks that facilitate large-scale drug trafficking and money laundering,” the Treasury said.

Three of the sanctioned alleged ‘Ndrangheta members were featured in a multi-part investigation into the Canadian faction published in 2024 by OCCRP, the Toronto Star, and La Repubblica.

One article revealed that Angelo Figliomeni, the group’s alleged boss, was in contact with Toronto-area real estate developers, and was linked to a sprawling property empire.

title: Populists vs. Protesters: Czechs Fight Over Public Broadcasters
content:
For much of the year, Letná Plain has nothing to offer either locals or tourists. 

It’s a large, featureless patch of land opposite the Sparta Prague football stadium. The surface alternates between dust and mud; there’s a car park for buses, and sometimes a circus. 

But every so often, Letná hosts an event that can tilt the world of Czech politics on its axis. Sometimes a little. Sometimes a lot. 

On Saturday, November 25, 1989, around 750,000 people gathered to demand the end of Czechoslovakia’s communist regime. The following day, many returned, and on Wednesday, November 29, parliament abolished the Communist Party’s leading role in society.  

Nothing like that is going to happen this time around, but on Sunday, November 15, there were perhaps 400,000 people on Letná for the largest demonstration in Prague since the Velvet Revolution.  

It looked huge when viewed from a media platform overlooking an ocean of flags and faces.  

The people who had gathered in the tens of thousands were there to protest against government plans to scrap the $10 monthly license fee which funds the nation’s two public broadcasters, Czech TV and Czech Radio.

title: ‘A fascist salute on the euro’: Kremlin narrative about Baltic coins backing Ukraine resurfaces in Slovakia and Czechia
content:
Every year, each euro area member state may issue two commemorative two-euro coins with a design of its own. Most countries use them to mark themes of major national or European importance.

The Baltic states used this option to show their support for Ukraine. In 2022, following the start of the war in Ukraine, Estonia issued a coin bearing the inscription ‘Glory to Ukraine’. A year later, the other two Baltic states followed: Latvia with a coin carrying the same slogan and Lithuania with the slogan ‘Together with Ukraine’. Like all other commemorative two-euro coins, they are legal tender throughout the euro area, including Slovakia.

Although they have been in circulation for years, the coins repeatedly resurfaced as a topic in 2026. In Slovakia, they were brought up in October by Ľuboš Blaha, a Member of the European Parliament for Prime Minister Robert Fico’s Smer party, who sits with the non-attached members. According to him, the slogan ‘Glory to Ukraine’ refers mainly to the historical controversies of Ukrainian nationalism and to the tragic events of the Volhynia massacre during the Second World War.

title: EU farm reform sparks fears of unequal funding across Europe
content:
European farmers may receive uneven financial support during the next round of the EU agricultural policy. Regional leaders fear that changing the rules for funding may end up supporting wealthier countries while neglecting rural development.

Funding for EU farms would be tied to national and regional partnerships in the new policy. The European Commission believes that this would give member states the flexibility to support their rural areas with other EU policies.

But various concerns were brought up during a high level meeting in Brussels as EU officials, parliamentarians and regional leaders discussed the next version of the Common Agricultural Policy (2028-2034). Regional leaders have asked for more guarantees on funding as well as a greater role in decision making.

The reform suggests that national governments can have greater autonomy in organizing farm support. But regional authorities are concerned that they could lose control over decisions that influence local farmers.

“The region cannot be simply somebody who is giving its advice.”

title: Life's cheaper in the east
content: A few weeks ago, I had a train to catch from an Ostbahnhof – the East Station – of a large German city. The area around it felt rougher than the neighbourhoods next to it: a few loveless shopfronts, run-down streets. It wasn’t the first time I’d noticed this at an Ostbahnhof, and it left me wondering. Are the eastern sides of cities generally worse off? There may be something to it. Some cities such as London and Paris have known east-west divides, and researchers studying English cities have found that some of these divides are, in part, a legacy of industrial air pollution. In the late 19th century, the prevailing winds carried factory smoke eastwards. Those who could afford it settled in the cleaner west, and the east stayed poorer. Long after the factories closed, rents there are still cheaper. But the pattern doesn’t hold everywhere. In Brussels, the east is the wealthier side. And in Berlin, the poorer east probably owes more to a different historical divide, the city’s split during the Cold War.

title: Ohio Jobs Program Wants Its Money Back After Company’s Failure to Deliver GMO Salmon
content:
When a biotech company named AquaBounty Technologies announced plans to farm genetically engineered Atlantic salmon at a new plant in Ohio, local and state officials eagerly provided it with incentives. Not long after, the company paused construction and auctioned off “new” and “unused” equipment. Now, the state’s private economic development arm wants its $1 million back.

JobsOhio has requested repayment from AquaBounty by Sunday, according to a company filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission. The filing also notes that, at the end of September, AquaBounty was down to three employees and $122,255 in cash.

AquaBounty said that its salmon could thrive in indoor freshwater farms and help feed the world. Announced in 2021, the new development in Pioneer, Ohio, was supposed to be its first large-scale production facility.

The project came with promises of 112 new jobs, plus more resources for schools and infrastructure. It was believed to be the largest investment ever in rural Williams County.

But AquaBounty, which had never made a profit over its 30 years in business, faced a tangle of regulatory challenges and pushback from environmentalists.

This post is part of Global Voices’ November 2026 Spotlight series, “Justice as infrastructure.” In this Spotlight, Global Voices is partnering with The Hague Institute for Innovation of Law (HiiL) to highlight the ways justice functions as critical infrastructure for any society. You can support this coverage by donating here.

A newborn Black baby delivered at a clinic in Tokyo’s Meguro Ward became the target of a barrage of racist harassment online.

The clinic published the baby’s photo with a congratulatory message on its social media account as part of its routine “babies born this month” photo series. A screenshot of the post spread widely on X, gaining more than 1.3 million views within a day. The post attracted many hateful comments loaded with anti-immigrant sentiment and racial discrimination against non-white and non-Japanese people. Some of the hateful comments received thousands of likes.

title: 2026 Water Conference: What’s at stake for Asia and the Pacific?
content:
By Lorenzo Santucci, Anshuman Varma, and Michael Koch*

BANGKOK, Thailand | 20 November 2026 (IDN) — As the global community gathers in Abu Dhabi for the 2026 United Nations Water Conference (December 8-10) to review progress and accelerate action towards SDG 6 (clean water and sanitation), the stakes for Asia and the Pacific are particularly high.

Despite important advances in recent decades, progress towards Goal 6 remains uneven and too slow to meet the 2030 targets. Climate change is adding further complexities through intensifying droughts, floods and water-related disasters across the region. In May, ministers, policymakers and stakeholders from across the region highlighted both the scale of the challenges and the opportunities to accelerate action. A clear message emerged: while the region remains off track on several SDG 6 targets, the region is home to innovative solutions and strong leadership that can help drive progress.

title: Razmyar: Vien Tynkkysen someväitteet oikeuteen
content:
Kansanedustaja Nasima Razmyar (sd) sanoo vievänsä perussuomalaisten europarlamentaarikko Sebastian Tynkkysen hänestä esittämät someväitteet oikeuteen.

Razmyar kertoo asiasta muun muassa Instagram-päivityksessään.

– Haluan oikeusjärjestelmämme ratkaisevan, missä kulkevat rajat poliitikkojen vihapuheelle, Razmyar kirjoittaa nyt.

Tynkkynen sanoi keskiviikkona X-palvelussa julkaisemassaan päivityksessä, että rajalakia kritisoineesta Razmyarista pitäisi ”päästä eroon” mahdollisimman pian, ja vihjasi hänen olevan eduskunnassa ”Troijan hevonen” eli vaarantamassa Suomen turvallisuutta jonkun muun laskuun.

Hän myös pyysi kannattajiaan peukuttamaan päivitystä, mikäli nämä haluavat Razmyarin ”jättävän Suomen”.

RAZMYAR korostaa, että poliitikkoja pitää saada arvostella välillä rankastikin heidän toiminnastaan, mutta ilman henkilöön menevää uhkailemista.

– Demokratiaan kuuluu oikeus osallistua yhteiskunnalliseen keskusteluun ilman pelkoa häirinnästä, uhkailusta tai vihapuheesta, hän kirjoittaa.

Tynkkysen sanavalintoja ja maastapoistumistarpeella vihjailua arvostelivat torstaina myös monet hallituspuolueiden edustajat.

title: Behind the Blog: Keeping It Together
content:
This is Behind the Blog, where we share our behind-the-scenes thoughts about how a few of our top stories of the week came together. This week, we discuss hippo physiology, Shenmue, and tricky interviews.

SAM: All anyone is talking about this week is GTA VI and a famous hippo, two things I have relatively passing interest in. GTA looks sick but I am very busy playing my interpersonal chores game of choice, Spiritfarer, in 20 minute increments three nights a week max, so I’ll be doing that for a while. 

The hippo situation is honestly very crazy to me (and sad ofc), a merely casual Fiona appreciator. But I'm finding the meta-discourse around the hippo situation more interesting than what actually happened; it seems like a ton of people have become parenting experts, hippo surgery experts, knit hat aerodynamics experts, and zoo enclosure design experts in the span of a week. In some cases it has gotten nasty. I think the situation so perfectly encapsulates the toxicity of online discourse, professors will probably teach it in mass media classes by next semester.

title: Have your say: artists, AI and creator rights
content:
Artificial intelligence is rapidly changing the way creative work is made, shared, and valued. From image generators and creative assistants to increasingly sophisticated AI platforms, artists are being asked to navigate new technologies, new opportunities, and new risks. At Arts Law we’re hearing from creators from all creative disciplines about the impacts of AI on their work and their livelihoods. We are pleased to be participating in a project geared towards visual artists and learning about what legal tools are needed to empower them in this new technological and legal landscape.

What do visual artists actually think about AI? How are these tools being used in practice? And how do copyright law and platform terms and conditions affect artists’ rights and creative control?

Researchers from the University of New South Wales, University of Newcastle, and the Arts Law Centre of Australia are seeking participants for an anonymous survey exploring how visual artists engage with AI tools, applications, and platforms in their creative practice, including experiences of AI, copyright, creator rights, creative control, and the terms and conditions that govern AI technologies.

title: "A COP of Betrayal": U.N. Talks Make No Progress on Fossil Fuel Phaseout, Climate Finance
content:
In our closing broadcast from Antalya, Turkey, the site of the 31st annual U.N. climate change summit, we take a look at what has — and hasn’t — been accomplished at this latest attempt to reach an international framework to stem the impacts of climate change.

“This COP was being touted as a COP of implementation, but what it has become is a COP of betrayal and a COP of distraction,” laments environmental justice advocate Harjeet Singh, the founding director of India’s Satat Sampada Climate Foundation. He’s joined on Democracy Now! by Meena Raman of Friends of the Earth Malaysia and Nafkote Dabi of Oxfam International as a number of NGOs announce their rejection of the conference’s final declaration text, which contains no mentions of fossil fuels or clear financial commitments from polluter countries.

“At the heart of the negotiations right now lies money,” says Dabi. “What rich countries, especially the EU, [are] saying is, 'There is no money at home.' But we know there’s money. They can tax the richest. They can tax the excess profit of fossil fuel companies. They can tax private jets. They can tax extreme wealth and raise the funds that’s needed to support communities.”

title: Pliniuksen Luonnonhistoria on antiikin klassikko, joka pyrki määrittelemään ihmisen paikkaa maailmankaikkeudessa
content:
Plinius vanhemman (23–79 jaa.) jättimäinen Luonnonhistoria sisälsi kaiken saatavilla olevan käytännöllisen tiedon luonnontieteen aloilta. Sami Janssonin, Arto Kivimäen ja Aulikki Vuolan suomentama teos on ensimmäinen osa Luonnonhistorian suomennoksista.

Varakkaaseen ritarisäätyiseen sukuun kuulunut roomalainen kirjailija ja luonnontutkija Plinius vanhempi kokosi Luonnonhistoriaansa kaiken saatavilla olevan käytännöllisen tiedon luonnontieteen eri aloilta. Nopeasti suosituksi noussut teos vakiintui luonnontieteen tärkeimmäksi lähteeksi läpi keskiajan aina uuden ajan tieteen nousuun asti. Niin iltaisin, öisin kuin matkatessakin työskennellyt Plinius oli omaksunut ajatuksen, että tieto on korkeinta hyvää, mitä ihminen voi itselleen saada.

”Koko Luonnonhistorian läpäisee pyrkimys määritellä ihmisen paikka suuressa luonnonlakien hallitsemassa maailmankaikkeudessa, joka on antanut ihmiselle kyvyn oppia ja käyttää viisautta”, Arto Kivimäki kertoo.

title: US reacts cautiously to Myanmar genocide ruling as EU praises ‘critical’ role of UN’s top court
content:
Reactions to ICJ ruling underline global divisions over court with China raising concerns about judicial overreach

The US has greeted with caution the world’s highest court’s ruling that Myanmar committed genocide against its Rohingya minority, while China has raised concerns of judicial overreach.

Reactions to Thursday’s historic ruling underlined deep international division over the role of the court and similar institutions. The international court of justice (ICJ) had never previously found a state responsible for genocide and the decision could set a precedent for future genocide claims, notably a case against Israel.

title: From idea to impact: What happens when students across Europe build solutions together
content:
The Una Europa Project Incubator is a programme that brings together students from the alliance’s partner universities to turn fresh ideas into concrete proposals. Working in international, interdisciplinary teams, students take part in hands-on workshops and mentoring, build skills in design thinking, project management and communication, and present their ideas at a final showcase.  

Each edition explores a new theme, with a flexible format that keeps evolving. Recent editions have welcomed student mentors and company partners, with formats ranging from a multi-week online programme to a one-week summer school in Kraków and an intensive three-day event in Berlin. 

Ideas that start with real problems 

The themes have varied, and so have the solutions the teams came up with: 

  • Europe in the World (2024): Students proposed LangBite, which promotes Europe’s endangered languages through media and community engagement. Roots and Routes tackles stereotypes about migration with videos, podcasts and street interviews. Green Miles is a rewards app that encourages sustainable travel choices.

title: Germany says investors ready to spend €25B to buy TikTok Europe
content:
BRUSSELS — The German government has found investors interested in investing as much as €25 billion to buy the majority of TikTok’s EU operations, Berlin’s culture minister Wolfram Weimer told reporters on Friday.

“We have spoken to a lot of investors already,” he said. “It’s a pan-European initiative and we think that they are able to invest around about 25 billion euros in that kind of business. And TikTok Europe should be open to sell 75% to 80% of the shares.”

Germany and Austria floated the Trump-style initiative earlier this week, citing concerns about TikTok’s influence on European democracy.

A TikTok spokesperson Friday dismissed the push as “nonsense,” saying the company is “already subject to comprehensive European law, including the Digital Services Act and the GDPR, which provide clear legal frameworks for any company investing and operating in Europe.”

title: Presidentti Stubb Berliinissä: Jatkamme tukeamme Ukrainalle
content:
Tasavallan presidentti Alexander Stubb osallistui Ukrainaa tukevien maiden halukkaiden koalition valtionjohtajien kokoukseen Berliinissä torstaina 19. marraskuuta 2026. Kokouksen aiheena oli koalition maiden tuki Ukrainalle ja rauhan edistämiseksi käytävät keskustelut.

”Koalition maiden on autettava Ukrainaa varsinkin ilmapuolustuksessa ja energiainfrastruktuurissa sekä taloudellisesti. Hyvä, että EU-komissio teki ehdotuksen Ukrainan lainatarpeiden kattamiseksi. Toivottavasti asia etenee pian”, presidentti Stubb sanoi.

Suomi on tukenut Ukrainaa laaja-alaisesti koko Venäjän hyökkäyssodan ajan. Berliinin kokouksessa Ukrainan presidentti Volodymyr Zelenskyi nosti erityisesti esille Suomen ja Ukrainan yhteisen väestönsuojakoalition tärkeyden.

”Halukkaiden koalitio työskentelee rauhan eteen. Neuvotteluprosessi etenee. On tärkeää, että Eurooppa on mukana neuvotteluissa”, presidentti jatkoi.

Kokousta isännöivät Saksan liittokansleri Friedrich Merz, Ranskan presidentti Emmanuel Macron ja Ison-Britannian pääministeri Andy Burnham.

title: Wine Distributor Targeted in Latest US Prince Group Sanctions Owns Warehouse Unit in London
content:
A man sanctioned this month for his alleged role in the Prince Group — a Cambodian conglomerate accused by the U.S. of operating major cyber-scams — controls a warehouse unit in London through his now-sanctioned wine distribution company, property documents show.

The U.S. Treasury Department imposed its third round of sanctions on the Prince Group on November 5, designating it as a “Transnational Criminal Organization (TCO)” and alleging it was involved in “cyber-enabled fraud, money laundering, and human trafficking.”

A Prince Group spokesperson told OCCRP the Treasury Department has “no support for any of their latest allegations,” adding: “Once again, the U.S. Government has issued new sanctions with zero factual basis for their claims.”

Included among the newly-sanctioned entities and individuals was Chinese-born Qiu Yong, 39, who holds citizenships from Cambodia, Saint Lucia and Turkey, according to the Treasury Department.

title: Poland Foils Russian ‘Mass Casualty Plot’
content:
For months, Western intelligence agencies have warned that Russia might stage a major provocation that could escalate into a grave confrontation with NATO. Poland now believes it has thwarted precisely such a plot. 

According to a November 18 investigation by the Polish newspaper Rzeczpospolita, which cited unnamed senior sources connected to Poland’s security services, Russian intelligence was preparing a bloody false-flag operation near the border with Kaliningrad, the Russian exclave on Poland’s northeastern border.  

The plan was to stage an attack, possibly on Russian soil, causing mass casualties and planting evidence implicating Ukraine, with Poland portrayed as the base from which the attackers had struck. 

This aimed to drive a wedge between Kyiv and one of its staunchest allies, leaving Poles furious that Ukraine had supposedly dragged their country into a confrontation with Russia. 

Moscow could then have used the incident as a pretext to strike back, although it remains unclear where the bloodshed might have occurred.

title: Hungarian government moves ahead of EU directive with its own women’s rights reform package
content:
• Hungary’s new Tisza government has unveiled a comprehensive women’s rights reform package, marking a significant departure from the policies of previous Orbán governments, under which women’s rights advocates say legal protections steadily deteriorated.
  • Hungary plans to ratify the Istanbul Convention and strengthen legislation against domestic and sexual violence, leaving only four EU member states — Bulgaria, Czechia, Lithuania and Slovakia — that have not ratified the treaty.
  • The government intends to remove prescription requirements for emergency contraception, making the morning-after pill more accessible, although its relatively high cost will remain a significant obstacle for many women.
  • Hungary will ease its controversial fetal heartbeat decree, allowing women seeking an abortion to choose whether to listen to the fetal heartbeat rather than making it mandatory, but critics warn that the revised rules could still expose women to pressure from doctors.

title: Prevention lacks one thing to win over finance ministers. Hard numbers
content:
The average European worker misses almost three weeks of work a year through sickness. A new study puts the cost to the EU at up to €810bn annually, roughly four per cent of its GDP. Yet governments still pour most of their health budgets into treatment rather than prevention.

Europe is losing workers and economic potential to illnesses that could be prevented. Its ageing population adds to the strain on social security systems and public finances. That is why health experts and policymakers argue that governments need to look seriously at prevention, not just at ways to treat disease.

At a conference in the European Parliament, health experts and policymakers warned that governments do not collect all the data they need. Without it, they cannot calculate the full cost of preventable illness, including lost working days, early retirement, and reduced productivity. The real question is whether Europe can afford to keep treating prevention as a secondary issue.

title: AI is imposing a hidden ‘cognitive tax’ on the lowest-paid workers
content:
It’s time to rethink welfare as AI reshapes the economy and wears down the brains of some of the most vulnerable workers

AI is adding to the cognitive load of workers already stretched thin by unpredictable pay, insecure housing and mounting debt – and the lowest paid feel it most. We need to rethink welfare for an economy being reshaped by AI.

Throughout the history of the study of economics, the human brain, which directs our labour, judgment and resilience, has rarely been considered an asset in its own right. The emerging AI economy is changing that. As machines take on routine work, what becomes most valuable is the judgment, creativity and insights only people can provide. Economists coined a term for this in recent years: brain capital.

Professor Dame Henrietta Moore is founder and director of the UCL Institute for Global Prosperity and co-leads The New Alignment, the institute’s G20 policy programme

title: How SNAP Theft Happens — and What to Do if It Happens to You
content:
When Kelly Joly swiped her electronic benefits transfer card at a Kroger in Beaumont, Texas, this August, she was trying to buy groceries for herself and her teenage son. Joly had worked for decades as a waitress. The day before her grocery run, she’d received her monthly $530 in Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program, or food stamp, benefits, she said. But now, her EBT card was being declined. She tried swiping again and began to cry. The cashier told her that this had been happening a lot recently and suggested she report the issue. Joly stepped to the side and called Texas Health and Human Services as her food sat bagged up on the belt. 

The representative at the agency that oversees SNAP in Texas told her there was nothing they could do to replace the funds, Joly recalled. Her benefits were gone, likely stolen by fraudsters. Joly said her account showed transactions from the day before at stores in Illinois, Minnesota and California.

“I don’t understand why they wouldn’t replace [our food assistance] if they can see that it was fraud,” she said. “And on top of that, how am I going to feed me and my son this month?”

content:
Kansanedustaja Timo Harakka (sd.) syyttää Petteri Orpon (kok.) hallitusta epäonnistumisesta nuorisotyöttömyyden torjunnassa.

Nuorisotyöttömyys on noussut yli 25 prosenttiin. OECD:n tuoreen raportin mukaan alle 25-vuotiaan työvoiman työttömyys on Suomessa yli kaksinkertainen OECD-maiden keskiarvoon verrattuna.

SUOMESSA on jo 73 000 alle 30-vuotiasta työtöntä, heistä 18 000 on pitkäaikaistyöttömiä.

Hallituksen ratkaisuksi tarjoaman nuorisosetelin toteutuneita käyttökertoja on kuitenkin vain 1 700, joka on noin kaksi prosenttia nuorten työttömien määrästä. Harakka pitää hallituksen toimenpiteiden mittakaavaa täysin riittämättömänä suhteessa kriisin vakavuuteen.

title: "Historic Judgment": World Court Rules Burma Guilty of Genocide Against Rohingya
content: The world’s top court has ruled that Myanmar committed genocide against the country’s Rohingya Muslim minority in a 2017 military crackdown that killed about 10,000 people and drove more than 730,000 refugees into Bangladesh. The landmark ruling is the first time the International Court of Justice has held a nation directly responsible for violating the 1948 Genocide Convention. “This is a vindication of what Rohingyas have been saying for the last almost 50 years, since 1978, when the first wave of genocidal expulsion was conducted by the very same perpetrating institution,” says Burmese dissident scholar Maung Zarni. By recognizing Myanmar’s “identity-based group destruction” of the Royinghas, he says, “the court vindicated [the] Rohingya’s collective articulation, memory and suffering.”

title: Satotilasto 2026: Viljasato tavanomainen, herneestä ennätyssato ja öljykasvit nousussa
content:
Luonnonvarakeskuksen (Luke) tuoreen tilaston mukaan viljasato oli tänä vuonna tavanomainen, noin 3,3 miljardia kiloa. Viljoista rukiin sato jäi selvästi keskimääräistä pienemmäksi, kun taas hernesato ylsi jälleen ennätykseen. Myös rypsistä ja sokerijuurikkaasta saatiin tavanomaista suurempi sato.

Noin 1,2 miljardin kilon ohrasato on kuusi prosenttia tavanomaista pienempi. Sen sijaan noin 1,1 miljardin kilon kaurasato on neljä prosenttia suurempi ja noin 840 miljoonan kilon vehnäsato yhdeksän prosenttia suurempi kuin kymmenen vuoden keskisato. Noin 62 miljoonan kilon ruissato on neljänneksen kymmenen vuoden keskisatoa pienempi ja jää saman verran vajaaksi myös vuosikulutuksestamme.

Viljantuotannon rakenne heijastaa Suomessa enemmän kotimaista rehutarvetta kuin elintarvikekäyttöä. Viljan ruokakäyttö on vähentynyt lautasellamme ja ohra on lähes kokonaan hävinnyt.

Luomukaurasato on ennätyssuuri, lähes 130 miljoonaa kiloa. Luomukauran osuus on yli kymmenesosa kokonaiskaurasadosta. Koko luomuviljasato, lähes 170 miljoonaa kiloa, on ennätyssuuri kaurasadon ansiosta. Luomuviljasadon osuus kokonaisviljasadosta on vajaa viisi prosenttia.

title: Race to be next UN secretary general exposes divisions among world powers
content:
Debate about dominance of permanent five members could reignite if major powers block Costa Rican frontrunner

The race to become the next UN secretary general could reach a decisive moment on Friday when a UN security council vote is likely to reveal whether the Costa Rican frontrunner for the post would be blocked by the big powers. If so, the setback will reignite a debate about the dominance of the permanent five (P5) members at the United Nations.

Rebeca Grynspan, an economist and UN insider who is from a family of Polish-Jewish wartime refugees to Costa Rica, has been in the lead in all but one of the eight straw polls of the 15 UN security council members since the first secret ballot was held on 30 July. Each member goes down the list of candidates, casting an “encourage”, “discourage” or “no opinion” vote for each candidate.

title: Membrane-like protein filaments boost bacterial energy production
content:
All living cells need energy, and to produce it they rely on quinones, small molecules that carry electrons. Well-known examples are coenzyme Q10 and vitamin K2, both widely used as dietary supplements. Because quinones are water repelling, they normally stay inside the cell membranes; the thin fatty layer that surrounds the cell. There they work like tiny shuttles, carrying electrons from one place to another so that the cell can turn food into usable energy.

Researchers from Monash University and the University of Melbourne in Australia have discovered a new protein structure in bacteria. The protein forms long filaments with a membrane-like channel inside, where quinone molecules can bind and extract electrons. The structure is found in many groups of bacteria and gives them an alternative way to increase their energy production.

The Australian teams used cryo-electron microscopy, a technique that images molecules in near-atomic detail, to see how the proteins form the channel.

title: CEPA Mourns the Loss of Ambassador Eric Rubin
content:
CEPA mourns the loss of Ambassador Eric Rubin, whose contributions to the cause of democracy and freedom, both within and outside government, stand as a testament to the power of thoughtful, dedicated public service. 

Across decades of service, most notably as US Ambassador to Bulgaria and Deputy Chief of Mission in Moscow, Ambassador Rubin brought unwavering integrity and deep diplomatic acumen to international relations. Throughout his distinguished career with the US Department of State, he served as a clear voice for democratic values while playing a pivotal role in strengthening transatlantic alliances and advancing regional stability. 

His influence extended meaningfully to policy analysis and strategic dialogue, including valuable contributions as a senior fellow to CEPA’s work. His investment in the next generation of leaders who benefited from his wisdom and experience made an especially valuable impact. Colleagues who had the privilege to work with him appreciated his warmth, sharp intellect, and collaborative spirit.

title: Sea to sky: How the new Frontex fragments migrant surveillance
content:
Frontex, the EU agency for the control of European borders, has allocated over €1bn for aerial surveillance in 2018–2028. The funding is growing rapidly: from €12m in 2018 to over €330m for next year.

Aerial surveillance is crucial for interceptions. According to LIMINAL, at least 33,000 migrants faced return to Libya and Tunisia between 2018 and 2024. The returns, by the security forces of those two countries, enjoyed the support of Frontex. (LIMINAL is a laboratory of the University of Bologna that investigates intersectional mobility and border violence.)

Lorenzo Pezzani, the mastermind of LIMINAL, told EU Perspectives that Frontex’s reform “comes as absolutely no surprise”. However, one of the main concerns is how Frontex “is playing a significant role in pushing for or enabling the use of drones within European civilian space”. The hotspot is the Central Mediterranean sea.

title: Yllätysnimi haluaa Ranskan presidentiksi
content:
Ranskassa maan entinen oikeistolainen pääministeri Dominique de Villepin on ilmoittanut asettuvansa ehdolle presidentinvaaleissa.

De Villepin toimi pääministerinä vuosina 2005-2007 edesmenneen oikeistopresidentin Jacques Chiracin kaudella.

Ennen pääministerikauttaan de Villepin toimi ulkoministerinä. Hänet muistetaan erityisesti siitä, että hän arvosteli ankarasti Yhdysvaltain suunnitelmia hyökätä Irakiin vuonna 2003 YK:n turvallisuusneuvostossa.

Viime aikoina hän on arvostellut Israelin Gazassa käymää sotaa, mikä on tuonut hänelle kannatusta nuorten keskuudessa.

Mielipidemittaukset ennakoivat Villepinille kuitenkin vain 1-3 prosentin kannatusta. Toiselle kierrokselle olisivat etenemässä äärioikeistolainen Marine Le Pen ja äärivasemmistolainen Jean-Luc Melenchon.

title: Näistä säästöistä kohistaan taas – nyt puhuu SDP:n Pinja Perholehto: ”Tämä epäsuhta on ratkaistava”
content:
SDP haluaa palauttaa kahden viikon hoitotakuun, laajentaa omalääkäri-omahoitaja-mallin kaikkialle Suomeen ja kohtuullistaa liian korkeita asiakasmaksuja, sanoo SDP:n varapuheenjohtaja, kansanedustaja Pinja Perholehto.

Hän sanoo tiedotteessaan, että Orpon-Purran hallitus on vaikeuttanut hoitoon pääsyä tällä hallituskaudella merkittävästi.

– Perusterveydenhuollon hoitoon pääsy on terveydenhuoltojärjestelmämme keskeisin ongelma. SDP haluaa varmistaa, että hoitoon pääsee nopeasti lompakon paksuudesta riippumatta. Ei ole sairastuneen eikä yhteiskunnan etu, että sairaudet pahenevat jonoissa ja niiden hoitaminen on vaikeampaa.

Perholehto tunnistaa tilanteen, että samaan aikaan julkinen talous on tiukalla ja sosiaali- ja terveydenhuollon menot kasvavat nopeammin kuin julkisen talouden kantokyky sallii.

– Tämä epäsuhta on ratkaistava. Menojen kasvua on hillittävä niin, että ihmiset saavat jatkossakin laadukkaat palvelut ja pääsevät hoitoon ajoissa. Ratkaisu on tuottavuuden kasvattaminen.

Perholehto listaa, että SDP parantaisi tuottavuutta esimerkiksi tehostamalla hankintoja, kehittämällä hoitoprosesseja ja laajentamalla hyväksi havaittuja käytäntöjä kaikille hyvinvointialueille.

title: “I Love Lucy” … in the Kitchen
content:
—This is a guest post by Ellie Hart, an archives processing technician in the Music Division. It also appears in the November/December issue of the Library of Congress Magazine.

Many fans know the “Pioneer Women” episode of “I Love Lucy” where Lucy and Ethel overzealously knead a ball of dough and accidentally bake a loaf of bread the size of a sofa. The real-life Lucille Ball and husband Desi Arnaz — a quintessential 1950s showbiz couple — were far more capable in the kitchen than that comic disaster suggests.

The Lucille Ball and Desi Arnaz Papers, part of the collections of the Library’s Music Division, contain two cookbooks plus a cheerful jumble of loose recipes and notes — handwritten, typed or torn from magazines and newspapers — that demonstrate their skill with a skillet.

Their copy of “The Settlement” cookbook is peppered with handwritten notes by Lucille and Desi in the margins. Their own homemade, unpublished cookbook — in a volume emblazoned “Cash” — is filled with page after page of handwritten recipes for favorite dishes: stuffed bell peppers, light tea cake, persimmon cake, cheese blintzes.

title: From FAIR to combinable and meaningful data: the Cross-Domain Interoperability Framework (CDIF)
content:
How can data from different fields be combined and understood by both people and machines, across different technical and scientific ecosystems?

To mark the 10th anniversary of the CODATA-RDA Schools of Research Data Science, CODATA and the GO FAIR Foundation (GFF) organised a session on this question in Trieste on 16 November 2026.

Here are the slides on the FAIR principles and FAIR Implementation Profiles, presented by Dario Bijker (GFF).

Here are the slides on the Cross-Domain Interoperability Framework (CDIF) presented by Nina Grau (CODATA).

Sharing data is no longer enough. There is an increasing need to combine data from different disciplines and across different systems. This is only possible when data is accompanied by clear and consistent information about what it is and what it contains: its metadata. Yet each community describes its data in its own way.

title: Parliament has an AgoraEU deal. What did culture get?
content:
The article was updated on 21 November 2026 to reflect the budget figures in António Costa’s negotiating box.

On 19 November, the European Parliament’s Culture and Education (CULT) and Civil Liberties, Justice and Home Affairs (LIBE) committees achieved a compromise on AgoraEU, the EU’s programme for culture, media and civil society for 2028-2034. The vote sets the basis for Parliament’s position in further negotiations with the Commission and Council — the committees voted to enter interinstitutional negotiations on the basis of the compromise text.

For culture, there is much to welcome. MEPs want to secure the Culture strand’s share of the budget, strengthen provisions on working conditions and simplify funding procedures. Artists facing forced displacement would have dedicated support. The biggest concern is international cooperation: the compromise would make it even harder to work with organisations from countries that do not participate in the programme.

Geopoliittiset, taloudelliset ja globaalit muutokset haastavat Eurooppaa. FIIA Brussels tuo Ulkopoliittisen instituutin laajan asiantuntemuksen nykyistä tiiviimmin osaksi Euroopassa käytäviä keskusteluja maanosan tulevaisuudesta.

FIIA Brussels kokoaa yhteen päättäjiä ja asiantuntijoita Suomesta ja eri puolilta Eurooppaa keskustelemaan näistä ja muista Euroopan tulevaisuuden kannalta keskeisistä kysymyksistä.

title: Tule mukaan rakentamaan kirjastojen lukutaitotyön verkostoa!
content:
Hyvät ideat jakoon, vertaistukea arkeen ja uusia mahdollisuuksia lukutaitotyöhön – yhdessä olemme enemmän!

Lukutaitotyötä tehdään yleisissä kirjastoissa ympäri Suomen monipuolisesti ja aktiivisesti. Yhä useampaan kirjastoon on nimetty lukutaitotyöstä vastaava henkilö, joka suunnittelee, koordinoi ja kehittää työtä omassa kirjastossaan. Vaikka lukutaitotyötä tehdään laajasti eri puolilla Suomea, kirjastoalan ammattilaisille suunnattu oma verkosto on vielä puuttunut.

Nyt on aika koota osaaminen yhteen!

Suomen kirjastoseura kutsuu kaikki yleisten kirjastojen lukutaitotyötä koordinoivat, suunnittelevat ja tekevät ammattilaiset mukaan Kirjaston lukutaitoverkostoon. Verkosto on avoin kaikille lukutaitotyön parissa toimiville – työskentelitpä lasten, nuorten tai aikuisten lukutaitotyön parissa.

Yhdessä jaetut ideat kantavat pidemmälle

Lukutaitotyötä koordinoi kirjastossa usein yksi henkilö. Silloin kollegoiden tuki, yhteinen ideointi ja kokemusten jakaminen voivat olla erityisen arvokkaita. Toisessa kirjastossa hyväksi havaittu toimintamalli voi innostaa muuallakin, ja yhdessä haastaviinkin tilanteisiin löytyy uusia näkökulmia.

title: Tre sager i tovtrækkeriet om AI-musikken
content:
Må AI-virksomheder træne deres modeller på sange som ”Barbie Girl” eller ”Forever Young”?  

Mange musikere, pladeselskaber og rettighedsorganisationer siger klart nej. Og det er de gået rettens vej for at få opbakning til.  

I Danmark sagsøgte Koda for et år siden AI-musiktjenesten Suno for at have trænet sin AI-model på Kodas repertoire uden tilladelse eller betaling. I søgsmålet peger Koda på numre fra Suno, der ligger tæt op ad blandt andet Aquas ”Barbie Girl”, MØ’s ”Final Song” og D-A-D’s ”Sleeping My Day Away”. 

”Først og fremmest er det vigtigt at slå fast, at sagen ikke kun handler om Koda og Suno. Den handler om, hvilke spilleregler vi vil acceptere i AI-økonomien. Hvis tech-giganter frit kan bruge dansk kunst og kultur som gratis råstof til at bygge AI-tjenester, risikerer vi ikke bare at undergrave musikskabernes økonomi, men også selve grundlaget for fremtidens danske kulturliv,” siger Nicky Trebbien, juridisk og politisk direktør i Koda.  

Sagen er henvist til Østre Landsret og er endnu ikke afgjort. Mens vi venter på rettens dom, er her tre sager fra resten af verden, du bør kende.

title: Parlamentarisches Frühstück zur Nachrichtendienstreform
content:
2024 beanstandete das Bundesverfassungsgericht die Kontrolle des Bundesnachrichtendienstes bei der Inland-Ausland-Fernmeldeüberwachung als verfassungswidrig. Hierfür müsse der Gesetzgeber bis zum 31.12.2026 eine verfassungskonforme Regelung schaffen und auch bei der Kontrolle nachbessern. Ein umfassender Gesetzesentwurf für die Nachrichtendienstreform wurde vom Bundeskabinett im August 2026 dieses Jahres beschlossen und eine Woche nach unserem Frühstück vom Bundestag verabschiedet. Der Gesetzentwurf umfasste mehrere hundert Seiten, änderte zahlreiche Gesetze und warf eine Fülle von Detailfragen auf. Eine solche Reform, die Regelungen mit und ohne Frist zusammen verabschieden will, lässt sich in wenigen Wochen kaum umfassend prüfen, geschweige denn öffentlich diskutieren.

Zu diesem Thema veranstaltete das Bündnis F5 am 6.11. sein vierzehntes parlamentarisches Frühstück unter der Schirmherrschaft von Konstantin von Notz, stellvertretender Fraktionsvorsitzender der Bundestagsfraktion von Bündnis 90/Die Grünen und Mitglied des Parlamentarischen Kontrollgremiums.

title: Protecting Norway’s Gas From Russia
content:
In any direct confrontation, European critical infrastructure would almost certainly become a target of the Kremlin’s long-range strikes, as it sought to degrade the continent’s warfighting capacity and population’s will to resist. 

One underappreciated vulnerability in Europe’s economic system is Norway’s natural gas infrastructure. Since 2022, Norway has replaced Russia as the continent’s main supplier, delivering 89 billion cubic meters to the European Union in 2025, almost one-third of the bloc’s gas imports and more than half of its pipeline supply. 

Russia’s share of EU gas continues to decline, while geopolitical volatility is making several other non-EU suppliers, foremost the US, less attractive. Norway’s role can be expected to grow further, both in its share of supply and political weight. 

Dependence on Norwegian gas is particularly high in Germany, the continent’s industrial powerhouse, whose factories are critical to European rearmament. In 2025, Norway supplied 44% of German gas imports, and industrial customers accounted for 60% of German gas consumption.

title: Spain’s open-door migration model: A European alternative or a strategic dilemma?
content:
During the opening ceremony of the 30th Ibero-American Summit, Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez argued that shared culture and values should translate into stronger political, economic and diplomatic influence. Against a global backdrop of increasingly isolationist tendencies, he called for a different approach: greater openness, cooperation and international engagement.

In his speech, he described Madrid as one of the hearts where [missing ending in source material] beats.

Sánchez recalled that the first meeting of Latin American countries took place in Guadalajara 35 years ago. It marked the culmination of decades of exchanges, connections and dialogue between the two sides of the Atlantic. He highlighted the cultural and linguistic similarities that unite more than 700 million Spanish- and Portuguese-speaking people. He also included indigenous languages in this shared heritage, emphasising the geopolitical significance of a common cultural community.

He cited Frida Kahlo, Pablo Picasso, Oscar Niemeyer and Antoni Gaudí, alongside Gabriel García Márquez, José Saramago and Rosalía, as examples of this shared cultural heritage.

title: Can lighter green rules get Europe’s space sector off the ground?
content:
Last year, the US attempted 181 orbital launches, China 92, and Europe just eight. Lawmakers now want to narrow that gap with the bloc’s first common space rules. These would cover satellite safety, cybersecurity, and the environment, with less paperwork for smaller players.

Europe’s space sector moved a step closer to a single rulebook on Thursday. The European Parliament’s Industry, Research and Energy Committee approved its position with 73 votes in favour, one against, and two abstentions. The legislation, which the European Commission proposed in June 2025, would establish the first common EU rules for companies launching satellites, operating spacecraft, or providing space services in Europe. Currently, 13 EU countries have their own space legislation.

title: The last good meal before the front
content: A warm bowl of borscht in a cold country, after a long day of work. Maybe that's what happiness is all about. I'm sitting in Trypichchia, a traditional restaurant in Kharkiv, a city about 30 km from Russian positions. And this borscht, I swear to god, might be the best I've ever had in my entire life. As a devoted enthusiast, I've eaten it in every possible setting: in fancy restaurants, at petrol stations, in village canteens, in shelters, and in trenches. I know my borscht. Mykyta, 29, one of the founders, tells us that the place started out as a local canteen at the beginning of Russia's full-scale invasion. Its sole purpose was to feed soldiers and volunteers who had stayed in the city when Russian forces were on the verge of capturing it. Since then, it has grown into a 300-sq-metre restaurant dedicated to one thing: “Serving the best food at the lowest price while rediscovering Ukrainian cuisine in a Kharkiv that has been Russified for far too long.” And you can feel it. Every recipe, Mykyta explains, is quite complex. The borscht is made with beet “kvass” (fermented beetroot juice), which gives it a lovely acidic kick and an even deeper reddish colour. title: Anthropic closes first day of public trading at $1.3tn valuation after largest-ever IPO
content:
AI startup and Claude chatbot maker became one of the world’s most valuable publicly traded businesses with final share price of $97

  • Anthropic’s historic stock market debut: key takeaways, and what comes next for the AI industry

    • Anthropic’s historic stock market debut: key takeaways, and what comes next for the AI industry

    Anthropic closed its first day of trading on the US stock market about 17% higher than its initial public offering price. At the close of market on Thursday, Anthropic shares were trading at just over $97 with a nearly $1.3tn total market capitalization, $1.75tn fully diluted.

    While the final share value was higher than the IPO price of $83, it marked a dip from an early high of $111.50. The firm’s shares initially soared 34% when trading got under way on its US market debut on Thursday, valuing the company at more than $2tn. Nonetheless, Anthropic’s ranked among the biggest stock market flotations in history. The artificial intelligence startup, founded in 2021, became one of the most valuable publicly traded businesses in the world.

title: The U.S. Paid Insurers Billions to Cover Civilians Harmed in War. Even the Government Says the System Is Ripe for Fraud.
content:
It was supposed to be a safety net for the workers who helped the United States fight its wars — a federal program that provided healthcare and financial support to the employees of government contractors injured or killed in Iraq and Afghanistan.

Instead, a handful of America’s insurance companies have become its biggest beneficiaries. While reaping billions in government payments, they have delayed care for legitimate injuries and received reimbursements for fraudulent claims, a ProPublica investigation found.

Over the past decade, American taxpayers have paid nearly $5 billion to insurers through the obscure program, which the government itself has described as “ripe for potential fraud or, at the very least, gamesmanship for profit,” according to an internal memo ProPublica obtained.

Nobody knows the true amount of misspent money. The official who oversaw the program under the Biden administration estimated that between $100 to $150 million is being wasted annually. The money has poured from a forgotten system for forgotten people who suffered forgotten injuries and deaths in America’s wars.

title: Finnish Institute of International Affairs launches FIIA Brussels to connect Finnish research with European policy debates
content:
As of January 2027, FIIA Brussels will host expert exchanges and policy discussions on European foreign policy, security and international affairs. 

Europe faces fundamental questions about its ability to respond to geopolitical, economic and other global challenges. To contribute to these debates, the Finnish Institute of International Affairs is bringing its broad research expertise closer to European policymaking through FIIA Brussels.  

Demand for Finnish expertise in Brussels has grown in recent years, driven by Finland’s NATO accession and the increased interest in the Nordic-Baltic region and in Finland’s comprehensive security model. FIIA Brussels provides a platform for dialogue and cooperation between Finnish and European researchers, experts and policymakers, to discuss these and other major questions facing Europe. 

“Brussels is the heart of EU, NATO and broader European policymaking. With FIIA Brussels, we want to bring our research closer to European policymakers, contribute to important debates concerning the future of Europe and strengthen the connections between European policymaking and our research in Finland,” says Niklas Helwig, Head of FIIA Brussels.

title: Soome Instituudi SA esinaise Marika Tammeaidi kõne instituudi 35. aastapäeval
content:
Arvoisa suurlähettiläs, instituutin johtaja, ja kaikki paikalla olevat entiset johtajat, hyvät yhteistyökumppanit, hyvä juhlaväki,

Suomen Viron-instituutti perustettiin vuonna 1991 – samana vuonna, jona Viro palasi itsenäisten valtioiden joukkoon. Harvalla kulttuurilaitoksella on yhtä painava syntymävuosi.

Instituutin toiminnan juuret ovat kuitenkin paljon vanhemmat. Voidaan sanoa, että ne ulottuvat vuoteen 1535. Silloin Wittenbergissä, Hans Lufftin kirjapainossa, painettiin Wanradtin ja Koellin katekismus – vanhin säilynyt katkelma vironkielistä tekstiä. Vuotta myöhemmin samaan kaupunkiin saapui nuori mies Pernajasta, Mikael Agricola, opiskelemaan Lutherin ja Melanchthonin johdolla. Hänen aapisensa ilmestyi vuonna 1543.

Ja tarinalla on jatkoa: Agricolan ainoa poika Kristian päätyi aikanaan Tallinnaan piispaksi.

Kirjoitettu viro ja kirjoitettu suomi ovat siis luokkatovereita. Ne kävivät koulunsa samassa saksalaisessa pikkukaupungissa, saman ajatuksen innoittamina: ihmisellä on oikeus kuulla tärkeimmät asiat omalla kielellään.

title: Judge gets First Amendment wrong in greenlighting Trump’s NYT lawsuit
content:
FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE:

New York, Nov. 19, 2026 — A federal judge today allowed parts of President Donald Trump’s defamation lawsuit against The New York Times, its reporters, and publisher Penguin Random House to proceed. Although other claims were thrown out, U.S. District Judge Steven Merryday declined to dismiss claims that the Times defamed Trump by, according to Merryday, suggesting he and his relatives committed tax crimes.

The judge acknowledged the Times had consulted with numerous experts on tax law, but questioned whether the expert opinions they obtained were sufficiently formal and detailed.

title: Family stories keep alive Georgia’s democratic past and the memory of Soviet repression
content:
In the Guria region, an organization is helping people recover a history the Soviets tried to erase

Originally published on Global Voices

Resort in the Guria region of Georgia. Photo by Tinari.totoro on Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 4.0).

This interview is part of a series of spotlights on the work of some of the grantees of the Digital Spark granting scheme, as part of the Regional Support Mechanism EECA project, implemented by the Metamorphosis Foundation and TechSoup, in partnership with CIVICUS and under the Digital Democracy Initiative (DDI) that covers the Global South. It is being published on Global Voices as part of a content-sharing agreement. 

Guria is a region in Georgia, situated in the southwestern part of the country. It has a coastline on the Black Sea to the west, which is about 22 kilometers (13 miles) long, and the region is bordered by the Samegrelo-Zemo Svaneti region to the north, Imereti to the east, and the Autonomous Republic of Adjara to the south. It has a rich history and a historical tradition of democracy.

title: Kenen etua kuvataidealan kasvu palvelee?
content:
Kuvaston puheenjohtaja Sade Kahra tarkastelee blogissa kuvataiteen toimialan kasvun suhdetta taiteilijan toimeentuloon. Puheenvuoro liittyy Uudistuva kuvataiteilijoiden järjestö –hankkeeseen, jonka tavoitteina on tiivistää järjestöjen yhteistyötä ja vahvistaa kuvataiteilijoiden edunvalvontaa.

Taiteen rahoituksen puolustaminen on tärkeää. Lisärahoitus voi mahdollistaa enemmän näyttelyitä, hankkeita ja apurahoja. Taiteilijan kannalta ratkaisevaa on kuitenkin, millä ehdoilla hän osallistuu niihin. Muuttuuko rahoitus korvatuksi työksi vai kasvaako toiminta kenties niin, että yhä suurempi määrä taiteilijoita tekee lisää palkatonta työtä ja kantaa itse suuremman taloudellisen riskin?

Edellisessä kirjoituksessani kysyin, mitä alan edunvalvonnassa halutaan muuttaa. Yksi tapa vastata kysymykseen on tarkastella kuvataiteilijoiden edunvalvonnan vakiotavoitteita, nimittäin pyrkimystä kasvattaa kuvataidealan julkista rahoitusta.

title: Maailman rikkaimmassa maassa viidennes on miljonäärejä
content:
Nobel-palkittu islantilaiskirjailija Haldor Laxness kuvasi teoksissaan köyhyydessä kituuttavia kalastajia ja lammastilallisia. Nykyiset islantilaiskirjailijat sen sijaan joutuvat miettimään, miten kirjoittaa maasta ja kansasta, jossa maallista mammonaa on yllin kyllin.

Islanti on näet maailman vaurain maa, ainakin mikäli on luottaminen sveitsiläisen investointipankki UBS:n Global Wealth Databook -raporttiin. Tässä vertailussa turvaudutaan vuoden 2023 julkaisuun, jossa oli vielä mukana suurin osa maailman maista; sen jälkeen UBS on valitettavasti rajoittanut katsauksensa paljon suppeampaan joukkoon valtioita, eikä esimerkiksi Islanti ole enää mukana.

UBS:n raportin mukaan islantilaisten mediaanivarallisuus on yli 413 000 Yhdysvaltain dollaria, lähes viisi kertaa niin paljon kuin suomalaisten. Lisäksi peräti 20,5 prosenttia islantilaisista on miljonäärejä, eli heidän omaisuutensa arvo ylittää miljoona Yhdysvaltain dollaria. Lukema on hätkähdyttävä, sillä esimerkiksi öljymaa Norjassa miljonäärejä on ”vain” kahdeksan prosenttia ja Suomessa kaksi prosenttia.

title: Are newsroom guidelines fit for purpose when it comes to data journalism?
content:
News organisations’ guidelines haven’t kept up with developments in data-driven journalism, they need to learn from practices in other fields — and principles need to be embedded in practice, according to new research on data journalism ethics.

Researchers Laurence Dierickx, Marilia Gehrke and Carl-Gustav Linden looked at dozens of European news organisations’ ethical codes to see how they relate to each stage of the Data Journalism Pyramid. They conclude that while ethical codes might talk in general about ethical principles, they rarely provide any guidance on how to apply those in practice when it comes to data-driven reporting.

Underpinning the research is the concept of ‘epistemic governance‘: the idea that an individual journalist is not solely responsible for the ethics of newsroom output.

This “governance perspective”, they write, “asks how ethical obligations become embedded in the procedural architecture of journalistic workflows, shifting ethics from values to be held to conditions to be built into practice”.

title: The most iconic sports film of all time taught us winning isn’t everything: 50 years of Rocky
content:
By all measures, Rocky (1976) is the most successful sport film of all time. Half a century on from its release, the story of small-time boxer Rocky Balboa – who rises to square up against heavyweight champion Apollo Creed — continues to capture our imagination.

Directed by John G. Avildsen, the film won the prestigious Best Picture and Best Directing Oscars in 1977. And the broader franchise, consisting of five sequels and three Creed spin-offs, has generated more than US$1 billion at the global box office.

Rocky resonates because it is the ultimate underdog story. The hero is flawed, yet faithful to his dreams – working to overcome his self-doubt. His final victory is not a boxing title, but in proving his worth.

The story of Rocky, written by Sylvester Stallone himself, was inspired by a real-life match between heavy weight champion Muhammad Ali and Chuck Wepner.

Wepner was a little known boxer from New Jersey at the time. While he didn’t win the fight, he held his own, becoming one of few boxers in history to be able to knock Ali down.

title: Lasten oikeuksien päivänä pörsseissä ympäri maailman kellot soivat lasten oikeuksille
content:
Ulkomaankauppa- ja kehitysministeri Ville Tavio osallistuu maailman lasten päivänä 20. marraskuuta järjestettävään Ring the Bell for Children -tapahtumaan, joka nostaa esiin pääomamarkkinoiden roolia lasten oikeuksien edistämisessä. Viime vuonna ensimmäistä kertaa Helsingissä järjestetty tapahtuma laajenee Unicefin innovatiivisen rahoituksen keskuksen johdolla maailmanlaajuiseksi aloitteeksi, kun yli 20 pörssiä eri puolilla maailmaa on tällä kertaa siinä mukana.

Pääomamarkkinoilla on merkittävä mahdollisuus vaikuttaa lasten oikeuksien toteutumiseen. Yritysten ja sijoittajien päätökset vaikuttavat lasten elämään esimerkiksi tuotteiden ja palveluiden, työolojen sekä yritysten toimitusketjujen kautta. Lasten oikeuksien huomioiminen on tärkeää niin yritysten vastuullisuuden kuin kestävän liiketoiminnan ja sijoitustoiminnankin näkökulmasta.

title: Wikipedia Recognized as a Digital Public Good
content:
UPDATE (19 November 2026)  – Wikipedia and Wikidata are now a part of the DPGs for AI (DPG4AI) Collection, a curated set of six digital public goods (DPGs) that can be used for responsible and equitable AI development– tools that place the public interest at their core.

Together with the other DPGs in the collection, Wikipedia and Wikidata provide open tools and knowledge that local developers, civil society, multilaterals, and governments can use as building blocks to develop and adapt AI solutions to their specific cultural and socioeconomic needs. This is particularly important in low-resource contexts and underrepresented domains, since ready-made AI tools can be ill-suited for what communities require and they may  reinforce existing biases or inequalities.

title: SAK:n edustajistossa toivottiin työväenpuolueilta yhteispeliä vaaleissa – ”Ei pidä lähteä kisailemaan siitä, kuka rökittää kenetkin”
content:
Palkansaajakeskusjärjestö SAK:n edustajiston syyskokouksessa puhuttivat muun muassa kevään eduskuntavaalit. Tulevalle hallitukselle asetettiin toiveita, mutta sai myös ammattiyhdistysliikkeen väki.

Edustajistolle pitämässään puheessa Tuuli Elokannas esitti toiveen, ettei ay-liikkeen sisällä ryhdyttäisi nokittelemaan puolueiden välillä. Hän kuvasi, että on kaksi työväenpuoluetta, joista kumpikin ajaa duunarin asiaa.

– Ymmärrän tavallaan sen, miksi halutaan ehkä erottua toinen toisistaan, mutta näen niin, että ay-asioissa olemme lähestulkoon kaikesta yksimielisiä. Meidän ei pitäisi lähteä kisailemaan siitä, että kuka rökittää kenetkin. Molemmat työväenpuolueet ovat kannuksensa ansainneet, Elokannas kiteytti Demokraatille.

– Gallupit ovat nousussa, vasemmistoliitto tekee ennätystuloksia kautta aikain ja demarit ovat ykköskärkenä siellä. Meidän ei tarvitse keskenään kisailla. Täytyy muistaa, että se on tämä hallitus, joka on ammattiyhdistysliikettä vahingoittanut.

title: Historic UN ruling that Myanmar committed genocide against Rohingya is rare victory for survivors
content:
Responding to the ruling by the International Court of Justice (ICJ), the United Nations’ top court, that Myanmar authorities committed the crime of genocide in their clearance operations against Rohingya people in 2017, Amnesty International’s Secretary General Agnes Callamard said:

“Genocide. This is the unequivocal finding of the ICJ. After years of denial, impunity and suppression of truth, this ruling is a historic and authoritative recognition of the atrocities committed against the Rohingya and a rare moment of justice for survivors, victims and their families.

“For decades, Myanmar governments and military authorities have denied the Rohingya citizenship and subjected them to an institutionalized system of segregation, discrimination and persecution that amounts to the crime against humanity of apartheid. They have confined Rohingya to refugee camps, burned their homes and villages, and committed widespread unlawful killings and sexual violence, including during the horrors of the military’s 2017 campaign.

title: Russian Indigenous Activist Daria Egereva Remains Jailed; Arrested After 2025 U.N. Climate Talks
content:
Human rights and climate groups are calling on Russia to release two prominent activists, Daria Egereva and Natalia Leongardt, who have been held in pretrial detention in Moscow for nearly a year, since December 2025. Egereva, a leading Indigenous rights activist in Russia, was arrested shortly after attending the COP30 United Nations climate summit in Belém, Brazil, where she served as co-chair of the International Indigenous Peoples Forum on Climate Change. Leongardt has worked for decades to support Indigenous rights.

“Right now all we are demanding is the release of Daria and Natalia, because they shouldn’t be in prison. You shouldn’t be arrested for activism,” says Viktor Suliandziga-Bagat, an Indigenous rights activist and representative of the Udege people from the Russian Far East. He is living in exile due to the risk against activists. “I don’t think I can come back to Russia,” he says.

title: IPI restrictions in medical device procurement: from early experience to the first review
content:
Over a year into the EU’s IPI restrictions on medical device procurement, early cases highlight challenges with the EUR 5 million threshold and the 50% cap on Chinese-origin supplies. The first review of the IPI Regulation brings these issues into focus for contracting authorities and suppliers.

The International Procurement Instrument (IPI) Regulation (EU) 2022/1031 allows restrictions on access to EU procurement markets to encourage third countries to open theirs to EU companies. This sits within a broader shift towards using procurement to advance EU strategic interests, also reflected in the ‘Buy European’ preferences envisaged in the Commission’s September 2026 proposal for a Public Procurement Act.

title: Outage Chaos: Who Turned Off All The Computer?
content:
It's been a tough couple of weeks for anyone trying to use email, fly, spend money, use an Apple device*, or do signals intelligence. Technical service outages are nothing new, but why do so many big ones seem to be happening all at once? Are hackers, AI, and international conflicts to blame? And what can we do about it?

Since most service interruptions don't make the news, it's hard to get a baseline on how often we see them happen normally. But after a major incident like the Microsoft cloud outage on November 12, any smaller disruption is more likely to become a story as part of a pattern instead of an isolated incident. We would have heard plenty about the Air Traffic Control problems anyway, but the November 18 disruption to the PlayStation Network might have gotten less attention. There might appear to be a spike or an upward trend in outages, but we can't easily verify that, and the increased coverage will tend to make it seem more significant and interconnected than it necessarily is regardless.

title: Malin Andtfolk får Per Brahe-priset 2026
content:
Hur kan robotar, artificiell intelligens och annan teknologi utvecklas för vården utan att människan försvinner ur fokus? Det forskar vårdvetaren Malin Andtfolk om. Nu tilldelas hon Stiftelsens för Åbo Akademi Per Brahe-pris 2026.

Per Brahe-priset tilldelas en lovande forskare vid Åbo Akademi vars fortsatta nära anknytning till akademin anses särskilt värdefull. Malin Andtfolk är docent inom vårdvetenskap med inriktning på vårdande välfärdsteknologi samt tillförordnad ämnesklusteransvarig vid enheten för hälsovetenskaper vid Åbo Akademi i Vasa.

Hon disputerade 2022 och har sedan dess forskat kring mötet mellan vårdvetenskap, teknologi och klinisk praxis. Prisnämnden beskriver henne som en engagerad och väletablerad forskare med en självständig vetenskaplig profil.

– Det är både hedrande och väldigt motiverande att få ett sådant erkännande. Att forskning med en så tydlig vårdvetenskaplig förankring uppmärksammas på det här sättet känns särskilt betydelsefullt, säger Malin Andtfolk.

Andtfolk utbildade sig först till närvårdare vid yrkesakademin i Kristinestad och därefter till socionom och sjukskötare vid yrkeshögskolan i Vasa. Under studietiden arbetade hon vid ett äldreboende.

title: Työllistymisen kannustimet parantuneet selvästi – lisätyön kannustimissa yhä isoja ongelmia
content:
Kokoaikatyön vastaanottamisen taloudelliset esteet eli työttömyysloukut ovat vähentyneet alle kolmannekseen Suomessa viime vuosikymmenen aikana. Etlan tuoreen laskelman mukaan työttömyysloukussa on vuonna 2026 edelleen arviolta 49 000 henkilöä. Jos vuoden 2017 lainsäädäntö olisi jätetty voimaan, työttömyysloukussa olisi ollut peräti 171 000 suomalaista ja vuoden 2022 lainsäädännöllä 128 500. Samalla työttömyysloukun luonne on muuttunut: aiemmin loukussa olivat lapsiperheet, kun nykyään loukku on siirtynyt pienituloisiin toimeentulotukea ja asumistukea saaviin. Ansiopäivärahaa saaneiden työttömyysloukut ovat lähes kadonneet, mutta sen sijaan perusturvan saajilla loukkuja on yhtä paljon kuin aiemmin. Tuloloukut eli työssä olevien esteet pienten lisäansioiden tekemiseen eivät myöskään ole Suomessa vähentyneet.

Keskeiset havainnot: 

  • Työttömyysloukussa on vuonna 2026 arviolta 49 000 henkeä. Työttömyysloukussa olisi ollut 128 500, jos vuoden 2022 lainsäädäntö olisi jätetty voimaan ja 171 000 vuoden 2017 lainsäädännöllä.

title: Building resilience for cultural heritage in the face of climate change: Europa Nostra contributes to SD-WISHEES conference in Tbilisi, Georgia
content:
How can research, international cooperation and civil society advocacy help safeguard cultural heritage from climate change? And how can evidence translate into meaningful changes in policy, funding and practice? These questions were at the heart of the international conference Resilient Cultural Heritage: Building Bridges between Research, Policy and Practice, held in Tbilisi, Georgia, from 10 to 12 November 2026, within the framework of the EU-funded SD-WISHEES project.[1]

Photo: Courtesy of SD-WISHEES

The conference brought together researchers, policymakers, heritage professionals, civil society representatives and international organisations to explore ways of strengthening cultural heritage resilience in the face of hydroclimatic extreme events, including floods and droughts. Discussions addressed the links between water management, climate adaptation and the protection of tangible and intangible heritage.

Vanessa Fraga Prol, Advocacy and Partnerships Manager at Europa Nostra, represented both Europa Nostra and the European Heritage Hub, highlighting the role of civil society, international cooperation and heritage advocacy in climate adaptation and disaster-risk reduction.

title: Vieraana OLGA: Minä menen eteenpäin
content:
Viisi vuotta sitten Olga Heikkala, 26, seisoi helsinkiläisessä studiossa. Sydän hakkasi ja suu kuivui. Jännitykselle ei kuitenkaan voinut antaa enää valtaa. Nyt oli uskallettava. Sitten Heikkala sulki silmänsä ja alkoi laulaa, vaikka samalla pelotti ja hävetti edelleen niin, että hän meinasi pyörtyä.

Kun Heikkala lopetti, hän ei muistanut tilanteesta juuri muuta kuin jalkojensa alla olleen tummasävyisen itämaisen maton ja kahvin tuoksun. Ystävä katsoi Heikkalaa ja oli hetken hiljaa.

– Sinun on jatkettava tätä, ystävä sanoi.

Heikkala nyökkäsi ja teki päätöksensä. Hän ei enää väistelisi välttämätöntä.

Perämeren ranta, Tornio. Ne olivat Heikkalan lapsuudenmaisemat, joissa hän varttui kolmilapsisen perheen esikoisena. Perheeseen kuuluivat äidin ja isän lisäksi pikkuveljet Oliver ja Alvar, edelleen läheiset ja rakkaat.

Lapsena Heikkala vietti mielellään aikaansa sienimetsässä, mutta tärkeintä oli aina laulaminen ja esiintyminen. Vanhemmat kertoivat myöhemmin, että jo päiväkodissa Heikkala asetteli ystävänsä riviin ja piti heille tanssi- ja lauluesityksiä.

Unelma-ammatista kysyttäessä Heikkala ilmoitti topakasti ryhtyvänsä pop-tähdeksi.

title: UN warns against misuse of security laws as UK weighs Palestine Action ban

title: World Court Finds Myanmar Committed Rohingya Genocide
content:
(The Hague) – The International Court of Justice’s (ICJ) landmark ruling that Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya is a historic milestone in their long quest for justice, Human Rights Watch said today. On November 19, 2026, the ICJ found Myanmar responsible for genocide against the Rohingya during the 2016-2017 “clearance operations,” carried out by Myanmar’s military.

In the case brought by Gambia against Myanmar for alleged violations of the Convention on the Prevention and Punishment of the Crime of Genocide (Genocide Convention), the court ruled for Gambia, with a nine to six vote by the judges, that Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya. This is the first time that the ICJ found a country responsible for committing genocide. The court also found that Myanmar violated other obligations under the Genocide Convention, including the obligations to punish those responsible for genocide and to prevent genocide. The court’s ruling is final and cannot be appealed.

title: The End Of Extraction
content:
In the middle of Norway’s Hardangerfjord, I steady myself against waves that jostle the floating metal ring that encircles an enormous fish pen. My burly host laughs as I grip the railing. He needs no such assistance. With one hand, he grips an oversized bucket of pellets; with the other, he launches a spray into the pen. The water ripples and an instant later a silvery-blue cloud of salmon bodies starts breaking the surface.

This little meal is just for show. Throughout the day, a giant Akvasmart feed system shoots an enormous cascade of pellets — a mix of grains, legumes, synthetic astaxanthin pigment and the cooked, pressed and processed bodies of smaller, scaly fish — through long pipes into the pen, where between 150,000 and 200,000 salmon are growing plump. Across all the pens of the facility, more than a million salmon are raised this way.

title: The Amazing Inventions of Ancient Greece: From Plato’s Alarm Clock to Ancient Flamethrowers
content:
“It’s a sunny morning in ancient Greece. Students have started gathering in the Academy, but their famous teacher Plato is nowhere to be seen.” The great philosopher has, it seems, “overslept and missed his own lecture.” The sun and the sound of early-rising animals may have failed Plato that day, as the story goes, but never would he let it happen again — at least after he got the mechanism worked out for the first alarm clock in history. Its design involves a series of containers linked by pipes through which water flows at a steady speed all night long. When the water accumulates in the penultimate, sealed vessel, air is pushed out through the flute embedded in its wall, producing something like birdsong.

Plato’s water alarm clock is just one of the pieces of advanced ancient Greek technology explained in the new video above from Lost in Time, a YouTube channel whose look at ancient Roman technology we posted here on Open Culture last year.
