title: How to watch the UK-EU summit like a pro
content:
BRUSSELS — Andy Burnham has gone big on Britain’s relationship with the EU during the first months of his premiership.

By the weekend, he may actually have something to show for it.

The British prime minister is heading to Brussels on Friday for his first U.K.-EU summit. But on the eve of the meeting, what exactly he’ll be coming back with is still up in the air. 

POLITICO analyzed leaked draft communiqués and spoke to diplomats and officials on both sides of the talks to piece together how the agreements are shaping up — and what’s still to be decided.  

Here’s what you need to know.

The U.K. and EU have committed to holding annual summits to build on the relationship they were left with after Brexit.

This is the second such meeting, and is primarily about concluding negotiations on agreements announced at the first gathering back in May 2025.  

That summit was attended by then-British Prime Minister Keir Starmer. This week’s meeting was originally due to be held in July, but it was postponed after Starmer stepped down — to give Burnham time to put his stamp on the process.

Three new international agreements are set to be announced at the meeting.

title: Avhandling om oavsiktliga graviditeter undersöker normer om moderskap och reproduktivt ansvar
content:
Ansvaret för att skydda sig mot att bli gravid anses fortfarande främst vila på kvinnans axlar. Lina Metsämäki disputerar i nordisk folkloristik vid Åbo Akademi med en avhandling om oavsiktliga graviditeter.

Det har gjorts mycket forskning om erfarenheter av abort men det saknas kulturvetenskaplig forskning kring situationen som föregår en eventuell abort, alltså den oavsiktliga graviditeten. Lina Metsämäki har genom intervjuer och analyser av textmaterial, som nyhetsartiklar, kommentarsfält och myndighetsrekommendationer, undersökt hur kvinnor som blivit oavsiktligt gravida förhåller sig till normer om kvinnlighet, moderskap och reproduktivt ansvar.

Några av de intervjuade upplevde den oavsiktliga graviditeten som skamfylld – fast de själva ifrågasatte den ståndpunkten som gammaldags. Ett vanligare sätt att resonera kring sin graviditet var dock att rama in den som något som kan hända vem som helst.

– Men denna förståelse förutsatte att de hade vidtagit åtgärder för att skydda sig mot en graviditet. Då kunde graviditeten förstås som en olycklig slump. Om kvinnan däremot inte hade skyddat sig var det svårare att framställa sig som moralisk.

title: Vihreät haastaa hallituksen talouslinjan – luontohaitoille hintalappu ja koulutukseen 807 miljoonaa lisää
content:
Johanna Kohvakka

Vihreät julkisti torstaina vaihtoehtobudjettinsa vuodelle 2027. Siinä vihreät esittää mittavia panostuksia luonnonsuojeluun, koulutukseen, ja sosiaaliturvaan. Puolueen vaihtoehdossa ympäristöhaittoja verotettaisiin nykyistä enemmän, ympäristölle haitallisia yritystukia karsittaisiin ja hallituksen tekemiä leikkauksia peruttaisiin.

Vaihtoehtobudjetin rahoitus perustuu yhteensä noin 3,64 miljardin euron julkista taloutta vahvistaviin toimiin. Vastaavasti puolue esittää samansuuruisia menolisäyksiä ja verotuloja vähentäviä toimia. Näin budjetti ei puolueen laskelmien mukaan kasvattaisi velanottoa hallituksen esitykseen verrattuna.

Ympäristölle haitallisten verotukien karsimisesta ja muista ympäristöveroista kertyisi 1,876 miljardia euroa. Muilla veromuutoksilla julkista taloutta vahvistettaisiin 1,055 miljardilla eurolla. Menoleikkaukset, hallituksen menolisäysten peruminen ja muut säästöt toisivat yhteensä noin 709 miljoonaa euroa.

Vihreän eduskuntaryhmän puheenjohtajan Oras Tynkkysen mukaan hallituksen talouspolitiikka on vienyt Suomea väärään suuntaan.

title: Just 15 kilometers from the border: school shelter is a lifeline for Horodnia
content:
FOR UKRAINIANS, SCHOOL SHELTERS have long become more than just the only way for children to continue in-person learning. They also serve as safe spaces for civilians during air raid alerts and emergencies – acting as so-called “Points of Invincibility,” where community members can warm up, charge their devices, and stay connected during prolonged power outages.

Shelters are also used for community and cultural needs, hosting concerts, performances, school assemblies, and academic competitions. It is truly a safe space that gives children the familiar and vital social interaction of childhood.

However, not all children in Ukraine have the opportunity to continue studying at school alongside their classmates. As Minister of Education and Science Andrii Butenko said recently: “82% of schoolchildren and kindergarten pupils are currently covered by shelters, but we should distinguish between shelters used simply to take cover from an enemy attack and shelters where learning can continue. Only 42% of schools can continue the learning process during an air raid alert, rather than just sheltering the children.”

title: Miten joululahjoitus voi auttaa katastrofin uhreja?
content:
Joululahjoitus voi auttaa katastrofin uhreja hyvin konkreettisesti: se rahoittaa ruoka-apua, puhdasta vettä, lääkintätarvikkeita ja turvallista suojaa ihmisille, jotka ovat menettäneet kaiken äkillisessä kriisitilanteessa. Lahjoituksen vaikutus ulottuu välittömästä hädästä selviytymisestä aina pitkäjänteiseen toipumiseen saakka. Alla käymme läpi tärkeimmät kysymykset, joita joululahjoittaja yleensä miettii.

Joululahjoitus ohjataan suoraan kentällä toteutettavaan apuun: ruokaan, veteen, terveydenhuoltoon, suojaan ja koulutukseen. Luotettavat järjestöt käyttävät lahjoitetut varat kohdennetusti humanitaarisiin operaatioihin, ja suuri osa varoista päätyy paikallisten kumppaneiden kautta suoraan avuntarvitsijoille ilman turhia välikäsiä.

title: Sopeutumista vai vastustamista ilmastonmuutoksen edessä?
content: Tätä kirjoitettaessa Varsinais-Suomen ilmastotiekartta vuoteen 2030 on kommentoitavana. Tiekartta julkaistaan marraskuussa 2026. title: ADD-forskere: Den offentlige sektor er ikke et samlebånd
content:
Af Sine N. Just, Alf Rehn og David Budtz Pedersen

Forfatterne er professorer ved hhv. Roskilde Universitet, Syddansk Universitet og Aalborg Universitet. De samarbejder i projektet Algoritmer, Data & Demokrati.

Tilbage i juni 2025 trak Den Digitale Taskforce for Kunstig Intelligens overskrifter med sin målsætning om at ’frigøre’ 30.000 årsværk i den offentlige sektor ved hjælp af kunstig intelligens (AI); dermed, lød det, får sektoren ’mere tid til det vigtige’. Nu har Netcompany udarbejdet et alternativt estimat, hvor det vurderes, at der er potentiale til at frigøre hele 90.000 årsværk, hvis ’alle offentlige ansatte bruger AI-systemer til alle relevante opgaver og med fuld effektivitet’, som det lyder i rapporten. Både det oprindelige målbillede og de nye beregninger bygger imidlertid på problematiske antagelser, der fører til deciderede fejlslutninger. Konklusionerne er forkerte ud fra en værdibaseret vurdering, uanset om man med ’værdi’ forstår kvalitet til borgerne eller kroner og ører på den offentlige bundlinje.

title: Far-right extremist or Ukrainian Fighter? Disinformation rewrote the story of the Krakow attack
content:
Saturday’s events in Krakow triggered a wave of disinformation across the internet. Within hours, false claims began circulating about both the attacker and the circumstances surrounding the shooting.

The perpetrator was attributed radically different political views, linked to Ukrainian military formations, and featured in manipulated photographs and videos generated using artificial intelligence.

There were also false reports concerning the response of emergency services and the alleged absence of police officers at the scene. The misleading claims came from anonymous social media accounts as well as statements made in traditional media outlets.

The incident has also demonstrated how powerful and convincing artificial intelligence has become as a tool for spreading disinformation. AI-generated content is increasingly sophisticated, and in many cases it is difficult to determine whether an image or video is genuine without using specialised tools to analyse it.

title: Journalism could get its first EU budget. If AgoraEU survives the cuts
content:
Artists, independent newsrooms, and civil society groups are caught in a tug of war over EU money. Lawmakers want to boost the bloc’s culture and democracy programme by a quarter. A Council proposal would cut it by almost a third.

The money would go to culture, independent journalism, and civil society. On Thursday, two Parliament committees adopted their position on the 2028–2034 AgoraEU programme, calling for €10.72bn. They were the Culture and Education committee and the Civil Liberties, Justice and Home Affairs committee.

It passed with 64 votes in favour, 17 against, and two abstentions. More than 1,500 amendments were tabled to the Commission’s proposal, with MEPs Emma Rafowicz (S&D/FRA) and Alice Kuhnke (Greens/SWE) serving as co-rapporteurs.

Before the vote, Ms Rafowicz welcomed the compromise reached after difficult negotiations, but warned that Parliament’s ambitions would depend on securing sufficient funding during talks with EU governments. “Everything that we’re defending will never come to light if the budget doesn’t meet the expectations of the programme,” she told MEPs.

title: Here, have some cancer with your smoky bacon crisps
content: The taste of smoke triggers memories of cosy firesides and tasty barbecues. Think smoked ham, smoked salmon, smoked cheese, and the less traditional smoky bacon crisps. Smoke flavourings are usually made by burning wood, capturing the smoke, and turning it into a liquid that can be added to food. But these smoky flavours may damage DNA and risk causing cancer, EU food experts said in 2023, leading to an EU ban on eight substances that came into effect in July for flavours added to sauces, soups, and snacks. And more are now set to be snuffed out: a wider ban on smoke flavourings in ham, fish, and cheese will land in 2029. The traditional method of exposing food to smoke and heat in a smokehouse oven, though it too can introduce some toxic compounds, is still allowed. The flavourings industry has tried, and failed, to fight back. Food flavourings companies Kerry Inc and Kerry Ingredients last week lost their legal fight to overturn the ban for three flavours they make. Kerry and other manufacturers have been trying to find smoky alternatives or evoke smokiness with herbs, spices, or salt, with limited success. title: Corpus Christi Started Pumping Groundwater at “Lightning Speed.” Rural Residents Fear the Consequences.
content:
Late in 2024, Corpus Christi, Texas, was desperate for water after years of drought. So city officials hatched a plan to tap millions of gallons of water a day from an aquifer that serves dozens of counties across the Texas Gulf Coast.

The city would drill wells — lots of them. 

Corpus Christi’s drilling frenzy alarmed rural residents, who worried it threatened their access to water. They mobilized to create a groundwater conservation district that would regulate drilling and, they hoped, limit how much water the city could pump. 

Then Corpus Christi officials came up with a peculiar idea. Fearing the residents’ effort could hamper the city’s ambitious plans to tap significant amounts of groundwater, officials asked a local entity to serve as its well regulator. 

The advantages: City Council members appoint that entity’s board of directors, and its staff is made up entirely of city employees.

Moldova is a relatively small post-Soviet state with a population of three million people. title: Xi-Putin-Trump summit was heavy on symbolism, light on substance – and not exactly a Yalta II
content:
It was touted as a history-making summit of the year. Presidents Donald Trump, Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping sat down on Nov. 19, 2026, in Shenzhen, China, on the sideline of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit, for the first such trilateral meeting of the three leaders.

Going into the talks, the trio had much to dicuss: the ongoing war in Ukraine, Middle East conflict and the march of artificial intelligence technology chief among them.

But what did 90 minutes of conversation deliver?

As an expert on U.S.-China relations at Harvard Kennedy School, I saw a lot of style, but less substance.

The first thing to pay attention to is the symbolism of the occasion. And so much of what was presented in Shenzhen was about the body language of the three men, their interactions and what that may indicate in regards to how they view themselves in a potentially new global order.

And this was on show even before the leaders sat down. At the beginning of the trip, when Trump landed in Shenzhen, he was met by Xi. Meeting a foreign leader at the airport is seen as a special honor bestowed by the Chinese president.

title: Ilmastokokouksen päätöslauselmaluonnoksesta hävisivät fossiiliset polttoaineet
content:
YK:n COP31-ilmastokokouksen tuoreesta päätöslauselmaluonnoksesta on poistettu maininnat fossiilisista polttoaineista.

Alkuviikosta julkaistussa aiemmassa luonnoksessa vaadittiin muun muassa nopeutettuja toimia fossiilisten polttoaineiden käytöstä luopumiseksi. Alkuviikon luonnoksessa oli mainittu myös kivihiili, öljy ja kaasu, mutta torstaina julkaistussa tuoreessa luonnoksessa mainintoja ei enää ollut.

Alkuviikon luonnoksen muotoilujen tiedettiin herättävän vastustusta monissa maissa.

TUOREESSA luonnoksessa on mukana vaatimus sähkön osuuden nostamisesta 35 prosenttiin koko maailman energiakulutuksesta. Luonnostekstin mukaan maailmantalouden sähköistäminen voisi olla ”merkittävästi eduksi” energiaturvallisuuden vahvistamisessa ja kasvihuonekaasupäästöjen vähentämisessä.

Turkin Antalyassa pidettävän COP31-kokouksen on tarkoitus päättyä perjantaina.

title: High-End Furniture Marketplace AptDeco Is Taking People’s Furniture and Not Paying Them
content:
This article has been updated with comment from AptDeco.

Last month, Erin sold a $3,000 large designer table on AptDeco, a white glove high-end furniture marketplace. More than a month later, she feels like she’s been literally robbed.

“AptDeco sent three men to physically collect my table on October 13, and here we are on November 16, with no payment and no concrete explanation for where my $2,000 (after their absurd $900 fee) is,” Erin told me. “It genuinely feels like I’ve had something stolen from me.”

AptDeco is a Y Combinator-backed company whose entire purpose is to take the risk out of places like Facebook Marketplace and Craigslist for designer furniture resale. It advertises itself as “simple and seamless,” and says “we handle pickup, delivery, and payments,” and claims that it pays sellers “within 5-10 business days.” But over the last few months, people who have sold furniture on the platform say that AptDeco has sold their furniture and taken it from their houses, but hasn’t paid them. 404 Media agreed to only use Erin’s first name because she is still trying to get her money from the company.

title: Haiti: Kenscoff violence highlights continued risk of killing, abduction and other abuses against children by gangs – new research
content:
Children in Haiti remain at risk of killings, abductions, sexual violence and other abuses by armed gangs, Amnesty International said in new research ahead of World Children’s Day.

Amnesty International interviewed witnesses to the Kenscoff gang raid on 23 August 2026, in which 55 people were killed and 15 more were injured, according to a municipal official. The UN said at least three boys and two girls were among those killed. A further 67 people, including 13 children, were abducted, according to municipal data.

Witnesses told Amnesty International that the attack began when dozens of gang members raided various parts of the commune of Kenscoff, south of Port-au-Prince. They attacked people in their homes, shooting them and setting houses on fire. They looted belongings and shot residents as they tried to escape. They also attacked displaced people who were taking shelter in the Ark of the New Covenant Church and shot many of them.

Children’s lives have been devastated by these horrors

Scott Edwards, Director of Amnesty International’s Crisis Response Programme

title: "Defend the Sacred": Indigenous Activist on Climate & Alaska Native Mary Peltola's Senate Victory
content:
Democrat Mary Peltola was declared the winner this week of Alaska’s closely watched race for U.S. Senate, making her the first Alaska Native lawmaker elected to the upper chamber of Congress.

At the COP31 climate conference in Turkey, we speak with Aakaluk Adrienne Blatchford, an Inupiaq and Yup’ik organizer from Unalakleet, Alaska. She says Peltola’s win is a significant milestone for Indigenous peoples in Alaska.

“Having somebody represent us in such a large capacity with such a big weight on her shoulders, but still carrying that struggle with her as she continues to advocate for our people and our way of life, is monumental,” says Blatchford.

title: IPCC report delay will threaten global effort to tackle climate crisis, says top scientist
content:
Johan Rockström, one of world’s leading climate experts, says slowing down scientific work puts cooperation at risk

Climate science is “foundational” to the Paris agreement and worldwide progress on tackling global heating, and attempts to delay new scientific reports threaten global cooperation on tackling the crisis, one of the world’s leading climate scientists has warned.

Johan Rockström, the director of the Potsdam Institute for Climate Impact Research, said the world’s leading body of climate scientists, the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change, must be allowed to work as quickly as possible on its next comprehensive assessment of global knowledge of the climate systems.

title: ‘Today the Truth Has Been Recognized’
content:
As the International Court of Justice in The Hague delivered its judgment on November 19 in the landmark case that Gambia brought against Myanmar for violating the Convention on the Prevention and Punishment of the Crime of Genocide, thousands of Rohingya waited anxiously in refugee camps in Bangladesh.  

In the Jamtoli Camp 15 in Cox's Bazar District, many crowded around a television. About two hours into the reading of the judgment, it started to rain. But no one moved.

The court’s president spoke in English, a language rarely heard in the crowded camps where over a million Rohingya sought refuge after fleeing Myanmar military attacks in 2017. At 5:13 p.m. local time, a community leader relayed the court’s ruling in the Rohingya language to the waiting crowd, telling them that, by nine votes to six, the court found Myanmar “committed genocide against the Rohingya group in northern Rakhine State.” 

The crowd clapped and cheered; many were in tears.

“The Myanmar military tried to convince the world that we had lied,” said 58-year-old Monajat Alam, from Rathedaung Township. “Today, the truth has been recognized.”

title: The Psychedelic Animated Video for Kraftwerk’s “Autobahn” (1979)
content:
Ah, yes, “Autobahn.” From the moment the door slams and the ignition starts, prog rockers and pre-new wavers know a journey is afoot. Though Kraftwerk had already made three albums, and the band members still looked like well-meaning, bookish hippies, 1974’s “Autobahn” is considered Year Zero for the denizens of the Electric Café, the four German robots who made human music with machines.

This cel-drawn animation by Roger Mainwood was made in 1979 to promote “Autobahn,” after most of the culture had caught up with the song, and it’s now bopping around pop culture again. By that last year of the ’70s, Omni magazine was a year old, music was sifting through the shockwaves left by Bowie’s Low and Heroes, analog was flirting with digital, and the world was ready to drive on that long, electric highway.

Mainwood’s protagonist is part alien, part human, and he begins looking around in awe in his hip goggles, then sets off for a run straight out of a Muybridge loop, only to wind up floating, flying, sailing and swimming through a landscape indebted to Peter Max, Push Pin Studios, underground comix, and 1930s modernism.

title: Costa eyes tax on Big Tech to boost EU budget after Trump’s poor midterms showing
content:
BRUSSELS — António Costa is seizing on an enfeebled Donald Trump to explore levying a tax on U.S. digital giants to finance the EU’s next seven-year budget.

The European Council president is considering asking governments to back a tax on tech companies such as Google and Meta to boost the EU’s approximately €2 trillion budget and unlock a deal on its final size, according to four EU diplomats and officials. In the past years, there has been little appetite for such a tax in Europe for fear of retaliation from Washington, but the Republicans’ poor showing in elections earlier this month appears to have opened the possibility.

“The probability of trade threats from the Trump administration has been reduced after the results from the midterms,” said Siegfried Mureșan, the budget negotiator for the center-right European People’s Party.

Costa, who is due to present a revised budget proposal for 2028-2034 on Saturday, is pushing leaders to agree on it by the end of this year — before votes in France, Italy and Poland threaten to disrupt negotiations.

title: Hieno kuvaus kipuilusta sukupolvenvaihdoksesta kirjallisuudessa
content:
Eero Karisto

Coda-romaanissa on kaksi keskeistä henkilöä, menestyskirjailija Willy ja kustantaja Andy.

Kirjailija on romaanin epämiellyttävin henkilö. Menestys on noussut päähän ja nyt hän kärvistelee, kun aika näyttää menneen hänen ohitseen. Ei hän tosin nuorenakaan ihannekaveri ollut.

Kustantajassa, tarinan kertojassa, taas on aika paljon reppanaa. Sosiaalisilta taidoiltaan hän on kömpelö siinä missä toinen on itsekeskeinen.

Kirja liikkuu monessa ajassa. Päätasoja ovat 1980-luku ja nykyaika. 40 vuotta sitten muodostui kulttuuria harrastava ja tekevä joukko, joka sitten hajosi. Jäljelle jäi ristiriitoja, traumoja ja selvittämättömiä asioita.

Jokin kaveripiirin dynamiikassa saa aikaan sen, että siitä ei synny elinikäistä ystävyyden verkostoa. Puuttuuko keskinäinen solidaarisuus? Toimitaan selän takana, käytetään toisia hyväksi.

Ihmiset erkaantuvat teilleen, osa katkeroituneina. Menestyminen on tärkeää. Ne, jotka menestyvät heikoimmin, katoavat tehokkaimmin.

Nyt sitten eri syistä ihmiset vähitellen kohtaavat. Mutta kohtaaminen on monelle vaikeaa. Entisten ristiriitojen lisäksi paljastuu uusiakin.

title: Trump loses Congress, but Europe may not benefit
content:
Republicans have experienced a night they are unlikely to forget. Their opponents, the Democratic Party, won control of both chambers of the US Congress in midterm elections (3 November). As a result, Trump will now face a stronger political counterweight in both the House of Representatives and the Senate.

His symbolic defeat is being celebrated not only in the United States but also in Europe. According to a recent pan-European poll, 58 percent of Europeans supported a Democratic victory in the elections, compared with just 18 percent who favoured the Republicans.

Waking up to a “blue morning” may have given pro-democratic voices across the EU a boost. In practical terms, however, not all that much is changing for Brussels.

The Democrats’ victory is likely to make governing at home considerably more difficult for Trump. It could lead to more intensive investigations into his administration, tougher budget negotiations and the blocking of his nominees. However, it may do little to fundamentally change his conduct on the international stage.

title: Grand Theft Wage
content: Grand Theft Auto VI came out yesterday. It's the most anticipated video game of the decade (the last GTA came out in 2013), reportedly one of the most expensive ever made, and potentially one of the most profitable. Some predictions suggest it could bring in up to USD 5 billion in global sales in its first week alone. Europe is a massive market for GTA. The game costs around €80 in most countries, but its affordability varies once you factor in purchasing power. A familiar pattern in globalised products, like a Netflix subscription. For both, Ukrainians get the worst deal. The hype over the past few days has been insane. Gaming is a world of its own, but GTA is one of those rare franchises that breaks out of that bubble and gets everyone talking, including the mainstream media. Some viral headlines have even warned of a productivity drop as employees call in sick to play, something dubbed “GTA Flu”. But as The Guardian points out, GTA Flu seems to be more of a media phenomenon than an actual economic crisis. Still, the fact that we're even talking about it says something about the scale of this cultural moment.

title: The Trump DOJ Quietly Intervened to Ink a Huge Payout to a Trump Golf Pro
content:
Top Trump administration officials intervened to help a longtime golf pro at Trump National Golf Club Hudson Valley secure a half-million-dollar payout from the IRS. A company connected to Trump’s media business also got a half-million.

The deal grew out of a little-noticed federal class-action lawsuit filed in 2025 by five individuals and companies. The group got $2.5 million after accusing the IRS of failing to protect their tax information.

The law permits a $1,000 payment to victims for each instance of an unauthorized inspection or disclosure of tax data. In this case, however, the government’s monetary settlement is 250 times higher than what the law calls for given the allegations. Victims can receive more money if they show actual damages, but multiple officials say such cases almost never result in payments approaching this size. These generous settlements have raised concerns because IRS Office of Chief Counsel attorneys were not consulted about the settlement terms, as is standard practice, according to people familiar with the case and documents seen by ProPublica.

title: Support Global Voices’ December Spotlight: Digital Communities
content:

Digital communications sparked new ways of forming communities: communities that spanned vast distances; that offered asynchronous interaction, innovative forms of constructing identities, and potentially enormous reach. These communities have provided connection for people who are isolated or marginalized, built powerful groups around both professional interests and unusual hobbies, and facilitated astonishing feats of knowledge-sharing and organizing, from Wikipedia to academic sub-field networks to hobby groups and fandoms.

But digital communities bring new challenges as well, from questions of moderation to questions of ownership. Almost all of them are built on the backbone of infrastructure owned by Big Tech — hardware at a minimum, usually several layers of software as well.

title: COP31: Ambition goes missing as fossil fuel language drops from draft deal
content: A cat named Ambition went missing again at COP31 on Thursday. While activists delivered the message with humour, it reflected a serious concern: explicit references to moving away from fossil fuels had disappeared from the latest draft climate agreement. On the eve of the summit's scheduled close, ministers and the Presidency were still trying to bridge sharp differences as civil society groups pressed for stronger action.

title: Myanmar genocide ruling is a watershed moment in international justice – with huge ramifications for other cases
content:
The International Court of Justice’s historic ruling of genocide against Myanmar on Nov. 19, 2026, will have significant consequences for the parties involved in the case – and potentially some who are not.

The Hague’s highly anticipated judgment in Gambia v. Myanmar is a major victory for Gambia, the tiny west African nation that filed a complaint with the court against Myanmar in 2019. It is also a major moment of accountability for the military leadership of Myanmar.

But as an expert in genocide and mass atrocity prevention, I believe the ruling goes far beyond these nations. Indeed, it is also a watershed moment for international legal justice that is bound to have important effects on the court’s other ongoing genocide cases, particularly the case of South Africa v. Israel.

Gambia’s case focused on actions that Myanmar’s military government called “clearance operations” in the course of its decades-long violent persecution of the country’s Muslim Rohingya minority.

title: Ministeri Tavion puhe Lapsen oikeuksien viikon tilaisuudessa
content:
Ulkomaankauppa- ja kehitysministeri Ville Tavion puhe SOS-Lapsikylän lasten oikeuksien viikon tilaisuudessa Helsingissä 19.11.2026

Arvoisat kuulijat,

Kiitos kutsusta osallistua tähän tilaisuuteen, ja erityinen kiitos SOS-Lapsikylälle sen pitkäjänteisestä ja vaikuttavasta työstä lasten, nuorten ja perheiden hyväksi Suomessa ja eri puolilla maailmaa.

Lasten oikeuksien viikko tarjoaa tärkeän hetken pysähtyä pohtimaan, miten lasten oikeudet toteutuvat ympärillämme ja mitä voimme yhdessä tehdä niiden vahvistamiseksi.

Tämän vuoden teema on "Jokainen lapsi on arvokas", ja juuri siinä kiteytyy lasten oikeuksien ydin.

Teema muistuttaa yksinkertaisesta mutta tärkeästä periaatteesta: lapsen arvo ei riipu siitä, missä hän on syntynyt tai millaiset lähtökohdat hänellä elämässä on.

Jokaisella lapsella on oikeus turvallisuuteen, koulutukseen, terveyteen sekä mahdollisuuteen rakentaa omaa tulevaisuuttaan.

Yhteiskunnat, jotka huolehtivat lapsistaan, luovat paremmat edellytykset vakaudelle, turvallisuudelle ja menestykselle myös tulevaisuudessa.

title: ”Suomesta on muuhunkin kuin sellunkeittoon” – Vihreiden vaihtoehdossa alijäämä pysyy ja veroaste nousee
content:
Vihreiden vaihtoehtobudjetti ensi vuodelle on yhtä alijäämäinen kuin hallituksenkin talousarvio. Vihreät on arvostellut hallitusta voimakkaasti siitä, että se ei sopeuta taloutta jo ensi vuonna.

Vihreiden eduskuntaryhmä esitteli vaihtoehtobudjettinsa ensimmäisenä oppositiopuolueena torstaina.

- Olemme pitäneet tämän samassa tasapainossa kuin hallituksen budjetti. Vaihtoehtobudjetin tärkein tehtävä on osoittaa, että hallituksen politiikalle ja valinnoille on olemassa vaihtoehto, budjetin valmistelusta vastannut kansanedustaja Saara Hyrkkö perusteli tiedotustilaisuudessa.

Hänen mukaansa puolue julkaisee parin viikon kuluttua tulevan vaalikauden sopeutustoimia koskevan pakettinsa.

VIHREÄT panostaisi koulutukseen ja luonnonsuojeluun ensi vuonna yli miljardi euroa enemmän kuin Petteri Orpon (kok.) hallitus. Se ei kuitenkaan ottaisi enempää velkaa.

Vihreät peruisi hallituksen päätöksistä muun muassa terveydenhuollon asiakasmaksujen korotukset, sote-järjestöjen leikkaukset ja asumistuen leikkaukset. Sen sijaan se muun muassa asettaisi luontohaitoille hinnan ja karsisi ympäristölle haitallisia yritystukia yli 800 miljoonan euron edestä.

title: Black Neighborhoods Are Twice as Likely To House a Data Center, Study Finds
content:
Developers build data centers in communities of color at more than twice the rate they do in white neighborhoods, according to a new study from researchers at George Washington University and the Center for Security, Innovation & New Technology (CSINT) at American University.

According to the study, “Redlining in the Age of AI: The Relationship between Data Center Locations and Race in the US” majority-Black neighborhoods have 2.2 times the odds of hosting a data center than a white neighborhood in the same state. The number goes up to 2.6 in majority-Hispanic neighborhoods and 4.2 times in majority-Asian neighborhoods. “As the share of Black, Hispanic, and Asian residents in a neighborhood increases, so do the odds that the neighborhood hosts a data center,” the researchers wrote.

title: “Young people can question those in power and demand something better”
content:
Children and young people around the world continue to speak up despite challenges because they believe their actions can make a difference. Many of them are tackling the impact of climate change head on, some are struggling to get an education, while others face dangers when they protest.

The Spark Club is a group of 11 to 18-year-old activists from around the world working with Amnesty International to make sure their voices are included, heard and listened to. They have been instrumental in shaping Amnesty’s new briefing Sparking Change - Children’s Right to Protest: A Perspective from Children and Young Activists, working alongside our researchers.

Here three young activists share more about the challenges they face in their countries and how they’re holding their governments to account.  

I first understood how powerful social protest can be as I held my mother’s hand during a demonstration when I was very little. I learned not to stay quiet facing an injustice. 

Now I study Political Science in Buenos Aires University (UBA) and I focus my activism on fighting for human rights.

title: "This Is Not Going Well": COP31 Draft Text Avoids Fossil Fuel Phaseout, Bets on "Magic Technologies"
content:
As we continue our week of broadcasts from the global United Nations climate conference known as COP31, we get an update on the formal negotiations from German activist Luisa Neubauer. The latest draft text of the key climate commitments that countries are debating has dropped language about phasing out fossil fuels, but it does include an emphasis on carbon capture and storage — a largely unproven technology that critics say cannot be deployed at scale to curb emissions.

“We have much better solutions at hand, like renewables,” says Neubauer. “This is not going well. We are not doing fine. And if anything, after this conference ends, we need people to take the streets and fight for more justice out there.”

title: Workdayn European Workforce Report: Työntekijät pysyvät nykyisissä työpaikoissaan tekoälymuutoksen keskellä – kolmannes pysyy, koska kokee olevansa jumissa
content:
BARCELONA, 19. marraskuuta 2026 – Workday Rising EMEA – Workday, Inc., luotettu henkilöstöhallinnon, talouden ja IT-toimintojen agenttipohjainen alusta, julkaisi tänään vuoden 2026 työvoimaa käsittelevän raportin, European Workforce Report. Raportin mukaan eurooppalaiset työntekijät pysyvät työnantajiensa palveluksessa pidempään kuin työntekijät muualla, mutta pysyvyys ei välttämättä heijasta sitoutumista. Jokaisella analysoidulla eurooppalaisella markkinalla kahden vuoden pysyvyysaste on korkeampi kuin maailmanlaajuinen keskiarvo 69,6 prosenttia. Kärjessä on Saksa 78,8 prosentin osuudella. Yli kolmannes (34 prosenttia) työntekijöistä Isossa-Britanniassa, Ranskassa ja Saksassa kertoo tuntevansa olevansa jumissa työpaikassaan, koska työmarkkinat ovat heikot.

Monet näistä työntekijöistä kokevat saavansa vähemmän tukea työnantajiltaan. Vain 54 prosenttia sanoo, että työnantaja välittää heistä ihmisinä, kun maailmanlaajuisesti luku on 59 prosenttia. Ja vaikka 75 prosenttia vastaajista sanoo tietävänsä, mitä taitoja he tarvitsevat menestyäkseen, harvempi (62 prosenttia) sanoo, että työnantaja auttaa heitä kehittämään tulevaisuudessa tarvittavia taitoja.

title: One in four women globally unable to refuse sex within marriage, says UN
content:
Almost half of women in west and central Africa cannot withhold consent, with girls worst affected, UNFPA finds

One in four women around the world have no power of consent if their husband or partner demands sex, according to a UN report.

In west and central Africa, almost half of women (45%) are not able to say no in their own marriage, while a third of women (33%) in east and southern Africa and in Arab states face the same predicament. In Latin America and the Caribbean, one in 10 women are not able to refuse sex, said the report by the UN Population Fund (UNFPA) published on Thursday.

title: World Court Finds Myanmar Responsible for Rohingya Genocide
content:
(The Hague) – The International Court of Justice on November 19, 2026, found Myanmar responsible for genocide against the Rohingya during the 2016-2017 “clearance operations” carried out by Myanmar’s military, in the case brought by Gambia against Myanmar for alleged violations of the Genocide Convention. The court’s ruling is final and cannot be appealed.

The following quote can be attributed to Maria Elena Vignoli, senior international justice counsel at Human Rights Watch: 

“The International Court of Justice’s landmark ruling is long-awaited recognition of the suffering the Rohingya have endured from Myanmar’s military. The ruling also provides a significant precedent for victims of genocide, and other grave crimes, across the world in their own quest for justice.”

“Myanmar should swiftly comply with the court’s judgment and end its oppression of the Rohingya. Concerned governments should strongly support the Rohingya and promote justice for atrocities, press Myanmar’s junta to comply with the judgment, and ensure the safe and voluntary return of Rohingya refugees to Myanmar.”

title: The web is held together by volunteers. AI could tear it apart.
content:
BRUSSELS — Long before the fresh spate of hacks and website shutdowns, the inherent instability of the web was depicted in an internet-famous cartoon of a rickety tower propped up by a single small block.

Now a near-daily rhythm of outages suggests the supporting block may have come loose.

POLITICO revealed Thursday that internal services at EU institutions had gone offline after a major AI-fueled cyberattack. That came after service interruptions at U.S. national security offices and the federal aviation authority, global outages at Microsoft and a succession of internet-activated attacks on supermarket refrigerators in Europe.

Authorities blame the sudden wave of instability on the capacity of new AI tools to detect vulnerabilities in existing code and for bad actors to exploit them.

Interviews with more than a dozen cybersecurity leaders and those working on maintaining the internet show the scale of the challenge to keep the web up and running, in a world where the pace of finding vulnerabilities has rapidly and permanently accelerated.

title: Anthropic keeps the AI party swinging, but the atmosphere is bubbly | Nils Pratley
content:
Can the newly listed AI company really be worth $2tn? Anyone who remembers the late 1990s has good reason to ask

Roll up, roll up, who wants to buy shares in a company whose technology “could pose catastrophic or existential risks to humanity”, as the prospectus had it? Virtually everybody, as it turned out. Anthropic flew out of the blocks on its first day as a listed company.

From the point of view of the promoters, the result was as good as it gets. The final pricing for the shares at $83 apiece was meaningfully higher than the indicated range of $70 to $78, but still left room for a big initial “pop”. There were positive vibes all round – especially for the battalion of investment banks collecting $550m of underwriting fees.

title: We’re Publishing the Tariff Refunds the Government Has Refused to Disclose
content:
After President Donald Trump’s “emergency” tariffs were overturned by the Supreme Court in February 2026, the government began processing billions in refunds to importers, including many recognizable public companies.

The Trump administration has not publicly detailed which companies are getting roughly $170 billion in refunds or how much they’ve asked for. ProPublica requested the information, but U.S. Customs and Border Protection denied our requests. (We’re appealing.) 

So our reporters found another way: analyzing the financial disclosures of thousands of publicly traded companies.

Today, ProPublica published “Cash Back,” a database of figures on refunds for tariffs paid under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act. The database includes 343 public companies for which we found mentions of refunds, amounting to more than $28 billion recovered or expected.

At least nine companies have disclosed that they are using their refunds not to pay back the cash-strapped consumers who generally covered much of the tariff costs through higher prices, but to give bonuses, according to a ProPublica analysis published earlier this week.

title: Elizabeth Holmes went from a startup darling to powerful seductress – these gendered portrayals profited investors
content:
Despite the countless books, podcasts, TV miniseries and documentaries, people continue to be fascinated by the fall of Elizabeth Holmes and her health-tech startup Theranos. We are now being offered a new insight into the founder through the much-hyped documentary, You Can See Everything.

The initial drama of the documentary takes places 34 days before Holmes started her 11-year prison sentence for investor fraud in 2023. In our research, we examined how Holmes was presented across promotional materials, tweets, talks and interviews over the ten year period from her initial appearance on the public stage in 2013 to the same period in which the documentary begins.

Valued at around US$9 billion (£7 billion) at its peak in 2014, Theranos claimed to have built a device that could run hundreds of lab tests from just a few drops of blood. Holmes and co-founder Sunny Balwani hid that the device could not in fact do what they said, leading to its 2018 shutdown and their convictions for investor fraud (and, in Balwani’s case, defrauding patients as well).

title: Global: Protesting children and young people face human rights abuses, including violence and discrimination
content:
Children and young people around the world face barriers, challenges and human rights abuses while exercising their right to protest, a new briefing from Amnesty International reveals, ahead of World Children’s Day on 20 November.

Sparking Change – Children’s Right to Protest: A Perspective from Children and Young Activists, is a briefing from Amnesty International developed in partnership with the Spark Club, a group of 11- to 17-year-olds from 12 countries across five regions. Drawing on research with more than 500 children and young people worldwide, the briefing examines why children protest, the risks they encounter, and what states and other actors must do to ensure that children can safely exercise their rights.

From the Gen-Z protests in Kenya to the Fridays for Future climate movement and recent youth-led demonstrations across Europe, young people have taken to the streets to make their voices heard. Yet many face violence, discrimination and other barriers when speaking out and putting forward their demands.

title: A New International Order? Xi, Trump & Putin Hold Historic Trilateral Summit in China
content:
Chinese President Xi Jinping hosted his U.S. and Russian counterparts for a historic trilateral summit on Thursday, with the leaders of the three biggest nuclear superpowers meeting for about 90 minutes in Shenzhen. Afterward, the countries published a “peace declaration” that affirmed “nuclear war cannot be won and must never be fought.” The declaration also announced a commitment to increase petroleum production, called for reforms at the United Nations and urged the International Criminal Court and similar bodies to “not abuse their jurisdiction.”

While in China, President Donald Trump also had a separate meeting with President Vladimir Putin to discuss the war in Ukraine, though it’s unclear if they made any progress.

“It’s a significant post-1945 moment, which was the last time that we had great summits,” says Scott Lucas, professor of international politics at University College Dublin. “What is the most important takeaway … is an ascendant China. It was China that really set the terms of what was said.”

title: Männynjuurikääpää esiintyy jo harvakseltaan Pohjois-Pohjanmaalla
content:
Luonnonvarakeskuksen (Luke) tutkimuksessa selvitettiin männynjuurikäävän esiintymistä Pohjois-Suomessa. Tautia löytyi kolmesta metsiköstä Pohjois-Pohjanmaalta. Lapin eteläosista tautia ei ole toistaiseksi löydetty. Löydökset osoittavat, että Etelä-Suomessa yleinen metsätuhoja aiheuttava sieni esiintyy jo harvakseltaan myös pohjoisempana. Männynjuurikääpä hyötyy lämpötilan noususta, ja sen odotetaan ilmastonmuutoksen myötä leviävän yhä pohjoisemmaksi.

Pohjois-Pohjanmaalta löydetyt tuhoalat olivat pieniä ja paikallisia, ja niissä oli vain muutamia männynjuurikäävän tappamia ja harsuunnuttamia puita. Tutkimuksessa oli mukana noin 30 metsikköä, joista kolmesta löytyi männynjuurikääpää.

Sienelle alttiiden puulajien joukko on pohjoisessa laaja. Männynjuurikääpää löydettiin mäntyjen lisäksi yhdestä haavan kannosta. Kahdella alueella sienen itiöemiä löytyi myös kuolleiden katajien juurista.

title: Startups call on Commission to salvage or scrap EU Inc proposal
content:
HELSINKI — The European Commission should withdraw and resubmit its proposal for a new EU-wide corporate law framework, startup lobby groups said, denouncing the current text as a “Frankenstein” proposal.

A position on the law adopted by EU capitals in October “weakened or removed some of the very provisions that would make EU Inc. a true European standard,” Startups for Europe and EU Inc. said in a joint press release.

Both groups pitched the withdrawal to European Commissioners Henna Virkkunen and Ekaterina Zaharieva, who oversee tech policy and startups, during a policy roundtable at Finnish technology conference Slush on Thursday morning.

They also sent a joint letter to European Commission president Ursula von der Leyen earlier this week.

The European Commission published its proposal for a so-called 28th regime, also known as EU Inc., earlier this year, to harmonize how founders can incorporate a company and reward their personnel, so that startups can scale more easily across the bloc.

The scheme was seen as a challenge to the U.S. state of Delaware, which is known for its flexible incorporation laws.

title: James McAvoy’s random encounter triggers a delusional fantasy in Parasocial Activity
content:
Òran Mór, Glasgow
In Briony Martha’s compelling play, a woman generates an alternative ending to her impromptu meeting with the Scottish superstar

Knowing what to believe is getting harder. Technology has blurred the line between truth and lies. Certain facts, though, we can demonstrate. We know, for example, that James McAvoy appeared in Cyrano de Bergerac at the Theatre Royal in Glasgow in the mask-wearing spring of 2022. We can also take playwright Briony Martha at her word when she says she bumped into the actor in a nearby coffee shop.

It is even true that McAvoy was in the audience of Martha’s Parasocial Activity towards the end of this summer’s run on the Edinburgh fringe: a performance that can only have had a heightened air of unreality.

At Òran Mór, Glasgow, until 21 November. At Southwark Playhouse, London, 13-30 January.

title: African glamour: the bold women who styled, wrote and read Drum magazine
content:
Drum magazine was an African institution in the 1950s and 1960s. Launched in South Africa, it would go on to publish five regional pan-African editions across eight countries.

Much has been made of the male reporters of the magazine, but a new open source book considers how women used it to shape their worldviews and opportunities. We spoke with media scholar Wanjirũ G. Mbure about Out For Glamour In Africa.

Initially known as The African Drum, Drum magazine started in South Africa in 1951, three years after apartheid was signed into law. The system of white minority rule would violently disenfranchise Black South Africans.

This was particularly evident in cities like Johannesburg, where large numbers of Black South Africans migrated from rural areas to work on mines. With little investment in housing and social services, they were forced to live on the outskirts of the city.

Ulkoministeri Elina Valtonen osallistuu Oslossa 19.–20.11. järjestettävään Pohjoismaiden ja Afrikan väliseen ulkoministerikokoukseen (Nordic–African Foreign Ministers’ Meeting, NAFM).

Vuorovuosittain Pohjoismaissa ja Afrikassa järjestettävään kokoukseen on ilmoittautunut yli 20 ulkoministeriä ja kokonaisuudessaan edustettuina on yli 30 maata. Kokouksen keskustelunaiheet kattavat laajasti rauhan ja turvallisuuden, kaupan ja investointien sekä kansainvälisen yhteistyön teemoja. Tämän vuoden kokouksessa painottuvat erityisesti monenkeskiseen yhteistyöhön ja tekoälyyn liittyvät kysymykset.

Ulkoministeri Elina Valtonen tapaa kokouksen yhteydessä Afrikan maiden ulkoministereitä myös kahdenvälisesti.

”Suomelle on erittäin tärkeää ylläpitää hyviä suhteita ja dialogia Afrikan maiden kanssa, joiden kansainvälinen painoarvo on yhä suurempi. Lisäksi talouskasvu monessa Afrikan maassa on maailman kärkeä ja on hienoa, että suomalaisyritykset ovat kiinnostuneita Afrikan markkinoista”, kertoo ulkoministeri Valtonen.

title: ICE Is Paying AT&T to Dig Through a Mountain of Call Records
content:
Immigration and Customs Enforcement is paying telecommunications giant AT&T millions of dollars to have AT&T’s analysts sift through mountains of raw AT&T data for a wide variety of investigations, according to an internal ICE document obtained by 404 Media, other procurement records, and experts who reviewed those records. Civil liberty experts have called it a mass surveillance program, and they say the data can include trillions of phone records and location data. 

The AT&T product, interchangeably called Data Analytics and Support Services or Data Analytical Services, appears to be related to an earlier surveillance program called Hemisphere, in which AT&T provided U.S. authorities at state, local, and federal levels access to AT&T user data. Though that program shut down, ICE is still paying for access to raw data under this new arrangement with AT&T, according to the restricted ICE procurement document obtained by 404 Media. The program likely affects more than just AT&T customers because the company connects phone calls for other phone companies, meaning non-customers are likely swept up too, according to a surveillance expert.

title: Miehen työ 2026 -palkinto Nuorisotutkimusseuran erikoistutkija Harry Lunabballe
content:
Tasa-arvoasiain neuvottelukunta (Tane) on myöntänyt vuoden 2026 Miehen työ -palkinnon Nuorisotutkimusseuran erikoistutkija, dosentti Harry Lunabballe. Palkinto myönnetään vuosittain miestenpäivänä 19.11. henkilölle tai taholle, joka on työllään tai muilla ansioillaan edistänyt sukupuolten tasa-arvon toteutumista erityisesti miehiin ja poikiin liittyen. Lunabballe palkinto myönnetään erityisesti hänen pitkäjänteisestä työstään poikien ja nuorten miesten osallisuuden vahvistamiseksi.

Lunabba on Suomen tunnetuimpia poikatutkijoita, joka on tutkimustyössään keskittynyt poikien ja nuorten miesten hyvinvointiin, maskuliinisuuksiin sekä sukupuolten väliseen tasa-arvoon. Lunabba tunnetaan myös aktiivisesta julkisen keskustelijan roolistaan, josta käsin hän on usein tuonut esiin, kuinka poikien ongelmat yhteiskunnassa jäävät tunnistamatta.

Sen sijaan, että pojat ja miehet nähtäisiin ongelmana, tulisi ongelmaa tarkastella järjestelmän kykenemättömyytenä tunnistaa poikien ja nuorten miesten haavoittuvuuksia”, toteaa Lunabba.

title: Why depth beats breadth in Europe’s hunt for an AI edge
content:
​​​An artificial intelligence (AI) system is judged on the job it does, not on how clever it is in general. For European businesses, that is an opening. For example, a pharmaceutical company does not need a model that can discuss biology. It needs one that can flag the rare adverse-event signal in its own trial data. An energy grid operator needs load forecasts built on its own network topology, not generic ones. A defen​s​​​e manufacturer needs a system that can verify a weld against its own specification, and say why it passed or failed. Each needs a system that understands its domain, works on its data, follows its rules and guardrails, and can be trusted to execute in a protected, controlled environment.

title: Accused South American Drug Lord Faces US Trial after Judge Rejects Motions
content:
Sebastián Marset, an accused South American drug lord, appears headed for a January jury trial after a federal judge in Virginia this week rejected multiple efforts by the defense to dismiss charges.

U.S. District Judge Rossie Alston Jr. on Tuesday rejected arguments from Marset’s lawyers that the Uruguayan national was being subjected to a vindictive prosecution and misconduct by prosecutors.

Marset’s defense team had argued their client’s Miranda rights, which protect against self-incrimination, were violated when agents from the Drug Enforcement Administration interviewed him without a lawyer present.

But the judge held that Marset had initiated some of the conversations after his arrest in southern Bolivia and was not coerced into talking with DEA agents during his expulsion to Peru and subsequent transfer to the United States and custody in Virginia.

The judge also rejected the defense’s “fruit of the poisonous tree” motion that asserted that evidence should be excluded because it was obtained improperly.

title: Europe and China 3 – The Coming Showdown
content:
This is the third of a three-part series on China’s relationship with Europe. 

The negative numbers began to cascade across European balance sheets as soon as China entered the World Trade Organization in late 2001.  

But the cost-benefit calculations were not equal for all Europeans. Some nations, such as Germany, initially gained from high-value exports and joint ventures. Others, like Greece and Portugal, faced a surge of low-cost Chinese goods and strategic investments by entities linked to the Chinese state. 

The Chinese economy was barely one-eighth the size of that of the European Economic Community before the People’s Republic embarked on its policy of “reform and opening up” at the Third Plenum of the Eleventh Central Committee in December 1978. By 2025, the relative economic weight of China and the European Union was almost equal.  

Together they account for about a third of world trade. In 1975, their bilateral trade was worth about €2bn ($2.2bn) annually; 50 years later, it was €2bn a day, according to figures compiled for the Institut Jacques Delors.

title: Climate Justice and Community Resilience: Mutual Aid, Organising and Disaster Recovery
content:
The resources on this page have been collated by the Commons librarians to support community leaders, organisers and others building resilience and readiness for climate impacts, emergencies and natural disasters.

As the climate crisis escalates more and more extreme weather events are occurring, with big impacts on people and the environment. How communities prepare for these events can make a crucial difference.

On this page we have gathered links to resources in the following areas:

  • Organising: An approach to social change which involves recruiting community members, developing leaders, identifying issues, taking collective action and building and using power for positive outcomes.
  • Mutual Aid: Sharing resources and care at the grassroots level, not waiting for interventions from the state or corporations.
  • Resilience: Building the capacity of individuals, organisations and communities to respond to, and recover from, crisis.
  • Just Recovery: An approach to disaster recovery which centres social justice, addressing power relationships and systemic harms.
  • Collaboration: Ways organisations, communities and government agencies can work together to prepare, respond and recover.

title: Five Years of CC’s Open Culture Program: Landmarks, Lessons, and Legacy
content:
Five years ago, we set out to build a coordinated global effort to help cultural heritage institutions (libraries, museums, archives…) open up access to the knowledge and culture they steward in their collections for everyone, everywhere, to enjoy. Thanks to a $5 million grant from the Arcadia Fund, in 2021 we launched the Open Culture program to promote more equitable access to culture and heritage in the digital environment. From new practical resources for practitioners and policymakers, to opportunities for local action through community engagement, all the way to the co-creation of an ambitious manifesto—the Open Heritage Statement—we’ve built a solid foundation for open culture on a global scale. What started as a niche field in the open family evolved into one of CC’s largest programs in the organization’s 25-year history.  

In this blog post, we first offer a retrospective of the key milestones we reached over half a decade of activity, share lessons learned, and end with reflections as one chapter closes and a new one opens.

  • 30+ funded community activities in the global majority world

title: Poland’s new security reality: When terrorism hits close to home
content:
Until recently, terrorism was far less common in Poland than in countries such as France, Belgium or Spain. Attacks involving firearms were virtually unheard of. The main security concerns identified by the police included sabotage, disinformation, cyberattacks and espionage. These threats were largely linked to Poland’s geographical proximity to Russia, which continues its war against Ukraine while conducting hybrid operations against NATO and EU member states.

The events of 7 November 2026 have shifted these priorities. Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk described the incident as an act of terrorism. Interior Minister Marcin Kierwiński said the evidence collected so far suggested that the perpetrator was fascinated by far-right ideology. However, the authorities have not confirmed any links to radical organisations, nor has any foreign involvement been established.

Above all, the incident highlighted how difficult it can be to prevent an attack in the heart of a major city.

Dr Paulina Piasecka, director of the Terrorism Research Centre at Collegium Civitas, believes the response of Kraków’s emergency services demonstrated the readiness of Poland’s state institutions.

title: The trouble with pet turtles and pink flowers
content: If you went on a walk this summer, you might not have noticed anything out of place. Pink flowers blooming near the riverbank. A turtle with a red stripe behind its eye sunbathing on a log. A raccoon enjoying its breakfast next to your rubbish bin. But the Himalayan balsam, pond slider, and raccoon that you might have seen are all on an EU list of species it considers a major threat to native ones. The list of “invasive alien species of Union concern” currently includes 114 plant and animal species that were introduced accidentally or deliberately into a natural environment where they are not normally found. EU countries are required to try to prevent accidental introductions, catch and eradicate new arrivals quickly, and manage the species that have already become widespread. A TEC analysis of the geographical spread of 75 invasive alien species of Union concern shows that 83% are present in more than one country, and 60% are reported in at least five. The success of invasive alien species can be attributed to a couple of important shared characteristics, according to Piero Genovesi, biologist and chair of the IUCN SSC Invasive Species Specialist Group. title: Chicago’s City Council Orders Independent Review of Finances as Scrutiny Intensifies
content:
The debate over Chicago’s financial struggles — out in the open as never before — took a new turn on Wednesday as the City Council added to the scrutiny.

The City Council voted 45-5 in a special meeting to give a leading alderperson the authority to hire an outside firm to independently review Chicago’s finances.

It’s unclear if an audit would be complete in time for the City Council to consider its findings before the Dec. 29 deadline mandated by state law to pass a 2027 budget, in what likely will be contentious negotiations with Mayor Brandon Johnson. Later in the day came another sign of distress: S&P Global put the city on credit watch with a warning that the budget wrangling is likely to result in a credit downgrade within 90 days.

The intense council debate over the city’s financial future comes in the wake of a package of stories published Monday by WTTW News and ProPublica that examined how a $55 billion debt burden, decades in the making, was hampering efforts to service Chicagoans and how the Johnson administration was turning to more borrowing to plug holes, such as large police settlements.
snippet: The debate over Chicago’s financial struggles — out in the open as never before — took a new turn on Wednesday as the City Council added to the scrutiny.

Jaa

Ulkomaankauppa- ja kehitysministeri Ville Tavio (ps.) eväsi tuet neljältä Somaliaan suunnitellulta kehitysyhteistyöhankkeelta, joille virkahenkilöt olivat esittäneet rahoitusta. Varsinainen päätös ilmoitettiin järjestöille tänään keskiviikkona, ja ulkoministeriö myös tiedotti asiasta.

title: Trump administration targets yet another journalist’s sources
content:
Tomorrow, a federal court in Virginia will hold a hearing in a case that offers a troubling look at just how far the Trump administration will go to attack journalists and their confidential sources.

Journalist Matthew Cole is facing a Department of Justice that seems determined to force him to reveal his confidential sources. Cole was one of several journalists behind a September 2025 New York Times article about a disastrous American military operation in North Korea during the first Trump administration, one that resulted in civilian deaths.

Just five months after the article was published, the DOJ issued a grand jury subpoena to Cole, seeking to compel him to identify his sources and testify about his reporting. Cole moved to quash the subpoena, but in July, a magistrate judge recommended that his motion be denied.

If the district judge hearing the case tomorrow adopts that recommendation, it’s very possible that Cole will have to decide between burning sources and, potentially, facing crippling fines or even jail time.

title: ESSAY: Beyond the Hive — Freedom, Community, and the Rivals of Amziah King
content:
By Sam Ben-Meir*

NEW YORK | 18 November 2026 (IDN) — Andrew Patterson’s The Rivals of Amziah King (2026) appears at first to be a story about competition, community, and revenge. But beneath its exuberant musical performances, eccentric characters, and increasingly violent confrontations lies a more radical philosophical proposition: that human beings are capable of organizing their lives according to principles fundamentally different from those governing capitalist exchange. The film’s recurring images of honeybee colonies are crucial to this vision, as are its extraordinary scenes of communal music-making. Together, they suggest a conception of freedom that is neither individualistic nor hierarchical, but realized through relationships of mutual dependence, responsiveness, and care.

title: Kulttuuri kuuluu kaikille lapsille, ei vain varakkaista perheistä tuleville
content:
Elämme yhteiskunnassa, jossa perhetausta määrittää yhä vahvemmin lapsen tulevaisuutta, hyvinvointia ja harrastusmahdollisuuksia. Kun julkisesta taloudesta leikataan, kohdistuvat iskut usein kaikkein herkimpiin, kuten lapsiin, nuoriin ja kulttuuriin. Tämä kehityssuunta on paitsi epäoikeudenmukainen, myös yhteiskunnallisesti lyhytnäköinen. Kulttuuri ja taide eivät ole luksustuotteita, joita ostetaan silloin kun rahaa jää yli. Ne ovat inhimillisen kasvun perusta, itsetunnon rakennuspalikoita ja jokaisen lapsen oikeus.

”Tasa-arvoinen kulttuuripolitiikka on tehokkainta mahdollista ennaltaehkäisevää mielenterveystyötä ja segregaation torjuntaa.”

– Pia Lohikoski (vas.)

Tasa-arvoinen taidekasvatus vaatii rakenteita, jotka murtavat varallisuuden asettamia esteitä. Tässä keskiöön nousee taiteen perusopetus. Vasemmistoliitto on pitkään ajanut taiteen perusopetuksen saavutettavuuden parantamista.

title: Slushin suojelumetsäverkosto kasvoi 40 hehtaarilla – metsiä suojeltiin Pohjois-Savossa, Kainuussa ja Pohjois-Pohjanmaalla
content:
Kansainvälisesti tunnetun teknologia- ja kasvuyritystapahtuma Slushin suojelumetsä kasvoi tänä vuonna kolmella uudella metsäalueella. Luonnonperintösäätiön avulla pysyvään suojeluun hankittiin yhteensä noin 40 hehtaaria metsää Kiuruvedeltä, Kajaanista ja Muhokselta. Metsien suojelu on meille konkreettinen tapa antaa jotain takaisin. Olemme olleet tyytyväisiä Luonnonperintösäätiön tapaan toimia metsien suojelussa ja siihen, miten säätiö on tukenut tavoitteitamme”, Mäkelä jatkaa.

title: Novaja Gazetan sulkeminen jättää aukon, jota on vaikea paikata
content:
Kyläläisiä pyydettiin kertomaan mielipiteensä. Mielipiteellä ei tosin olisi mitään merkitystä, selitti piirin johtaja suorasukaisesti.

Nikolsk on 700 asukkaan kylä Arkangelin alueella Pohjois-Venäjällä. Viranomaiset aikoivat lakkauttaa kyläkoulun kaksi ylintä luokkaa sota-ajan budjettipaineisiin vedoten. Säästöä kertyisi viisi miljoonaa ruplaa eli noin 55 000 euroa.

Kyläläiset olivat eri mieltä. Ilman ylimpiä luokkia lapsiperheet lakkaisivat muuttamasta kylään ja yksi Venäjän harvoista yhä kasvavista kylistä alkaisi kutistua. He ottivat yhteyttä valtuutettuihin, keräsivät nimiä, vaativat kansanäänestystä ja veivät asian oikeuteen. Lopulta aluehallinto lupasi ylimmille luokille viisi vuotta lisäaikaa.

Tämä on kertomus venäläisistä, jotka eivät hyväksyneet heidän puolestaan tehtyä päätöstä. Se on myös kertomus sanomalehdestä. Novaja Gazeta kirjoitti kiistasta helmikuussa ja palasi toukokuussa kertomaan, mitä kyläläiset olivat saaneet aikaan.

Marraskuun 9. päivänä 2026 tuo lehti lopetti toimintansa Venäjällä. (Novaja Gazeta Europe on erillinen, maanpaossa toimiva julkaisu.)

title: 8th International Open Search Symposium – A review (day three)
content:
The third and final day of #ossym started on a controversial note. The keynote by Aline Blankertz from Structural Integrity brought in valuable new angles to the open search discussion. She argued that openness enables AI and further deepens dependencies.

Aline stated that people “like openness because it encourages sharing and transparency”.
But she also pointed out that openness feeds AI, because AI is best at exploiting openness effectively. It takes the open web and closes it by encouraging people to use a chatbot that delivers the answers easily!

One example she mentioned, which illustrates the situation, was Wikipedia.
Wikimedia and Google used to have a mutual dependence. Wikimedia needed visibility and Google needed good content! Google used to make donations. But Wikipedia page views have fallen by over a third between 2020 and 2025. Wikipedia cannot do anything because of their commitment to openness. And it seems that as Wikipedia becomes less visible, Wikipedia might decline.

Aline concluded: High quality content should not be free!

title: Eduskuntavaalit 2027: Tekoälyä ja sisältöähkyä?
content:
Tekoälyn käyttö vaikuttaa siihen, millaista tietoa ehdokkaista ja puolueista välittyy äänestäjille. Muutokset kampanjoinnissa ja äänestyskäyttäytymisessä voivat näkyä jo ensi kevään eduskuntavaaleissa.

Tekoäly muuttaa vaalikampanjointia ja äänestäjien tiedonhakua myös Suomessa. Kevään 2027 eduskuntavaaleissa tekoäly auttaa ehdokkaita tuottamaan sisältöä sekä äänestäjiä vertailemaan poliittisia vaihtoehtoja. Se ei kuitenkaan itsessään ratkaise, kenen viestit tulevat näkyviin tai millaisina ehdokkaat ja heidän tavoitteensa esitetään.

Tekoälyn merkitystä onkin tarkasteltava osana laajempaa viestinnän ympäristöä, jossa alustat, kampanjat ja tiedonhakupalvelut vaikuttavat siihen, mitä ihmiset näkevät ja voivat arvioida.

Poliittinen näkyvyys ei ole sidoksissa vain julkaisujen määrään. Siihen vaikuttaa myös, millaisena ehdokas esiintyy, mitä hän kertoo poliittisista tavoitteistaan ja miten sisältö toimii eri kanavissa. Samaan aikaan yleisöjen sitoutuminen viesteihin, reaktiot, kommentit ja jaot vaikuttavat merkittävästi sisältöjen leviämiseen.

title: How we discovered a 115 million-year-old ‘algae rebellion’ in Portugal’s sea cliffs
content:
Quite a few scientific discoveries are a product of chance. You set out looking for one thing, but often end up finding something totally unexpected. In micropalaeontology, the study of microscopic fossils, this is especially common. You never know what you’re going to find until you start examining the samples under the microscope.

This story began in the spring of 2024, when we were travelling through the Algarve, in southern Portugal, with the aim of determining the age of rocks there by studying fossils of charophytes, a group of green freshwater algae that includes the closest descendants of land plants. This field is known as biostratigraphy: a branch of geology that determines the age of rocks based on the fossils they contain.

We visited several locations that had been studied between the 1960s and the 1980s. Among them was Praia da Luz, which would hold the biggest surprises for us. We collected 120kg of rock, mostly clay, and sent it all to Barcelona – much to the disbelief of the post office clerk in the Algarve town of Loulé, when we told him the (rather heavy) parcel contained “stones”.

title: Missä kulkee raja? Maahanmuuton turvallistaminen heikentää kansainvälisen suojelun ehtoja
content:
Ihmisten liikkuminen on aina ollut osa kansainvälistä politiikkaa, mutta viime vuosina siitä on tullut yhä selvemmin valtioiden turvallisuuspolitiikan ja geopoliittisen kilpailun väline. Muuttoliikkeiden kytkeminen kansalliseen turvallisuuteen muuttaa tapaa, jolla valtiot suhtautuvat rajoihinsa, suvereniteettiinsa ja kansainvälisiin suojeluvelvoitteisiinsa. Samalla kasvaa riski, että turvapaikanhakijoiden oikeudet jäävät turvallisuuspoliittisten tavoitteiden varjoon.

Marraskuussa 2021 tuhannet ihmiset kokoontuivat Puolan ja Valko-Venäjän rajalle. He olivat lähteneet kotimaistaan eri syistä, mutta päätyneet tilanteeseen, jossa heidän liikkumisestaan oli tullut osa valtioiden välistä vastakkainasettelua. Valko-Venäjän hallintoa syytettiin ihmisten kuljettamisesta Euroopan unionin ulkorajalle tarkoituksenaan painostaa unionia ja horjuttaa sen jäsenvaltioita. Rajalle saapuneiden ihmisten tilanteesta tuli samalla osa turvallisuuspoliittista kertomusta, jossa kysymys heidän liikkumisestaan yhdistyi Euroopan vakauteen ja suvereniteettiin.

title: Sudan: Devastating RSF drone strikes on civilians in El Obeid should be investigated as war crimes
content:
Drone strikes by Rapid Support Forces (RSF), which hit residential areas and civilian infrastructure in El Obeid city, in Sudan’s North Kordofan State, killing dozens and disrupting essential services, should be investigated as war crimes, Amnesty International said today.

The organization investigated nine RSF drone strikes in El Obeid and its surroundings, which killed 37 civilians and injured 10 between June and August 2026. Three of the strikes hit residential areas; four struck key civilian infrastructure, including El Obeid’s power plant, fuel stations, and the main market; and two targeted moving vehicles. In all incidents, interviewees said they either saw or heard the drones, moments before or after the strikes. Amnesty International’s investigation did not identify military objectives in the vicinity of the sites at the time they were struck.

title: Ecuador Pushes to Expand Amazon Oil Drilling While Land Defenders Face Threats
content: Ecuadorians voted overwhelmingly in 2023 to stop oil extraction at Yasuní National Park, one of the most biodiverse places on Earth, yet oil drilling has continued despite that historic referendum. “The government does not want to close the wells,” says Ivonne Yánez, the president of Acción Ecológica, an environmental nonprofit group based in Ecuador. The Ecuadorian government is also “continuing expanding the oil activities in the Amazon,” she points out. Yánez also speaks about how dangerous Latin America is for environmental activists. It is where “the most number of defenders that are just defending their lands, their rivers, their rights,” are killed. “And in Ecuador, this is also happening.”

content:
Years ago, Germany's Deutsche Bank quietly dropped MKB Bank, a lender close to the Orbán government, from its client list. An international investigation involving Direkt36 has found that what caught the Germans' eye at the Hungarian bank – which later merged into MBH Bank – was a suspected money laundering network with Russian links and overly close political ties.

The post Suspicious money flows and the Orbán connection: the inside story of MKB Bank’s secret crisis first appeared on Direkt36.

title: The concept of scientific research in data protection law: current state and future prospects?
content: The EU’s General Data Protection Regulation 2016/679 (“GDPR”) applies also where personal data is processed for scientific research purposes. However, the GDPR does not formally define “scientific research”, and so far, there has not been a clear consensus on the definition of the term under the GDPR.1 The distinction matters, as processing personal data for scientific research purposes benefits from specific rules and flexibilities under the GDPR, including, for example, presumed compatibility of further processing and the possibility of longer retention under Article 5, subject to Article 89 safeguards. Article 17 also provides a conditional exception to erasure where erasure would make research impossible or seriously impair its objectives.

title: Outage Chaos: When Tech is too Big to Fail
content:
Outages happen, but we deserve a resilient internet where no one outage at one company can put people at risk and disrupt the global economy. We can only get there by addressing an over-reliance on a few cloud monopolists through effective antitrust laws and interoperability requirements.

Service outages, like we’ve seen recently at Microsoft, Apple*, banks, courts, airlines, and elsewhere, can be more than an annoying hurdle. Losing a vital service due to an error can cause the same impacts as a government-ordered internet shutdown—people losing access to vital information and lines of communication.  As usual, the greatest harms are faced by people on the margins globally.

There’s not much hope in companies out-nerding these issues either. Technical errors will always exist, whether it’s a bug, negligence from an administrator, or a malicious attack. The problem is an over-reliance on any one company or system when these inevitable outages occur. It’s a matter of public safety and economic stability that policymakers mitigate the impact of these disruptions before they occur.

title: Tiedekeskus Auroran aluetaloudellinen ennakkoarvio on julkaistu – tutustu Sodankylään suunniteltuun tiedekeskukseen!
content:
Sodankylään suunniteltu Tiedekeskus Aurora yhdistää tutkimuksen, oppimisen, matkailun ja alueen elinvoiman. Auroran lähtökohtana on Sodankylässä jo olemassa oleva kansainvälisesti merkittävä arktinen tutkimus ja osaaminen. Tavoitteena on tehdä tutkittu tieto suurelle yleisölle ymmärrettäväksi ja koettavaksi sekä rakentaa sen ympärille ympärivuotista oppimista, matkailua, yritystoimintaa ja uusia palveluja. Auroran sisältöaihioihin kuuluvat muun muassa avaruus, revontulet, arktinen ympäristö sekä geologia ja mineraalit.

Syksyn 2026 aikana Tiedekeskus Auroran valmistelu on edennyt uuteen vaiheeseen: vuonna 2027 ratkaistaan tiedekeskuksen toimintamalli sekä valmistellaan kiinteistöinvestoinnin omistus-, rahoitus- ja toteutusvaihtoehtojen markkinatestausta.

Auroran sisällöllinen perusta rakentuu tiiviissä yhteistyössä tutkimusorganisaatioiden kanssa. Keskeisiä sisältökumppaneita ovat Ilmatieteen laitos, Oulun yliopiston Sodankylän geofysiikan observatorio ja Geologian tutkimuskeskus GTK.

title: Kuntien nihkeys ekologiseen valokuiturakentamiseen ihmetyttää alan toimijoita – ”Vaatimus 70 sentin syvyydestä on historiallinen jäänne”
content:
Tekniikka & Talous nosti äskettäin esiin valokuidun rakentamisessa käytettävän mikrosahauksen, joka on yleisesti käytössä esimerkiksi Ruotsissa ja muissa Pohjoismaissa, mutta tyssännyt Suomessa kuntien lupakäytäntöihin.

Artikkelissa haastateltu Tietoliikenteen ja tietotekniikan keskusliitto Ficomin lakiasiainpäällikkö Marko Lahtinen kummastelee tilannetta. Mikrosahauksessa ja muissa matala-asennusmenetelmissä kaapeli sijoitetaan noin 30–50 senttimetrin syvyyteen perinteisen 70 senttimetrin sijaan. Menetelmä on jopa kymmenen kertaa perinteistä kaivamista nopeampi ja sen ympäristökuormitus on merkittävästi pienempi.

Valoo käyttää ekologista matala-asennustekniikkaa kaikkialla, missä se on mahdollista. Klaus Varis kuitenkin kertoo, että moni kunta ei edelleenkään salli nykyaikaisten menetelmien käyttöä.

”Pidän kuntien asennetta todella outona. Kun ottaa huomioon, miten paljon asukkaita harmittaa kotikadulla pyörivä kaivinkone, on suorastaan hullunkurista, että matala-asennuksia ei sallita”, Varis sanoo.

Jopa sähkökaapeleita syvemmälle – täysin turhaan

title: Music Now! Musica Nostra! Forum in Mafra put music and listening at the heart of Europe’s living cultural heritage
content:
Bringing together European heritage professionals, musicians, researchers, policymakers and young people, the ‘Music Now! Musica Nostra!’ Forum took place on 7-8 November 2026 at the Royal Building of Mafra, Portugal, a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Through two days of discussions, musical experiences and exchanges, participants explored how music and listening can strengthen democracy, foster intercultural dialogue, safeguard living heritage and contribute to a more sustainable and peaceful Europe.

Organised by the Centre Européen de Musique, a partner of the European Heritage Hub, in collaboration with Europa Nostra, the Municipality of Mafra and the Centro Nacional de Cultura, which operates the Europa Nostra Heritage Hub in Lisbon, the conference built on the first ‘Music Now! Musica Nostra!’ gathering held in April 2025 and the European Manifesto it inspired. The event brought together voices from across Europe and beyond, with a particular emphasis on the role of younger generations in shaping the future of Europe’s cultural heritage.

title: World ‘held hostage by oil mafia’, says Panama minister at Cop 31
content:
Key issues unresolved as summit enters final days, with 30 countries signed up to forge fossil fuel treaty separate to UN process

The world is “being held hostage by the petroleum mafia” and seems unable to break free, Panama’s environment minister has warned, as key issues remain unresolved in the final days of the UN Cop31 climate summit.

“We are in love with our kidnappers,” said Juan Carlos Navarro, at a press conference to announce 30 countries were now signed up to forge a new fossil fuel treaty, separate to the UN process. “We love the petroleum guys. We can’t live without them, and they are so smart they have convinced us that they are doing this for our own good.”
