title: Azerbaijan Jails Parliamentary Watchdog Activists
content:
An Azerbaijani court sentenced two activists affiliated with Meclis.info, an independent platform monitoring the country’s parliament, to lengthy prison terms on dubious financial crime charges on November 12, 2026. These are the latest convictions as part of a wider crackdown that has seen scores of journalists, human rights defenders, and civic activists prosecuted on politically motivated charged since late 2023.

The Baku Grave Crimes Court sentenced Imran Aliyev, Meclis.info’s co-founder, to 10 years in prison, and Elgiz Gahraman, another co-founder and data analyst, to nine years. A third defendant, the platform’s accountant Tamella Musayeva, received a suspended prison sentence. All three were convicted of illegal entrepreneurship, money laundering, currency smuggling, tax evasion, and document forgery.

Launched in 2023, Meclis.info published analyses of Azerbaijan's parliament, scrutinizing lawmakers’ attendance, voting records, and public statements. Aliyev has been in detention since his arrest in April 2024. Gahraman and Musayeva were placed under police supervision in February 2025; Gahraman was taken into custody in the courtroom after the verdict.

title: Le vol des cygnes – A Concert with the Mirjam Helin Academy
content:
Le vol des cygnes – A Concert with the Mirjam Helin Academy
Wednesday, 2 December 2026 | 8pm

Through a dialogue between musical traditions and cultural heritage, Institut finlandais invites you to discover Le vol des cygnes, a concert exploring themes of longing, roots and identity.

The concert dives into the connections between Finnish Romanticism and Italian and Argentine folk song traditions. Works by Sibelius, Berio, Ginastera and Pylkkänen take the audience on a musical journey through ideas of home, belonging and the search for identity, brought to life by three artists whose backgrounds span across multiple cultures.

The concert pays homage to Finnish soprano Aino Ackté (1876–1944), marking the 150th anniversary of her birth. One of the first Finnish opera singers to achieve major international recognition, Ackté made her mark during her years in Paris, from 1894 to 1903, which were decisive in establishing her European reputation and launching her international career.

In honour of her legacy, the artists will perform Höstkväll by Jean Sibelius, a work dedicated to Ackté, thereby following in the footsteps of her international career, which began in Paris.

title: Tietoisku kirjastosta — Kirjasto ei vaadi eikä valikoi
content:
Tietoisku kirjastosta – Kirjasto ei vaadi eikä valikoi -video muistuttaa, että kirjasto on kaikille. Kirjastoon saa tulla kuka tahansa, eikä tulosyytä tai taustaa tarvitse selittää.

Arjessa meitä lähestytään jatkuvasti vaatimuksilla: joku myy, joku kysyy, joku haluaa jotain. Kirjasto on poikkeus, sillä sinne saa tulla ilman selittelyjä, eikä kukaan kysy, miksi tulit. Kirjasto edistää jokaisen yhdenvertaisia mahdollisuuksia sivistykseen ja kulttuuriin, ja kirjastoon ovat tervetulleita kaikki.

Tämä video on osa Tietoisku kirjastosta -sarjaa, jota tuottavat yhdessä Kirjastokaista ja Suomen kirjastoseura yhteistyössä yleisten kirjastojen kanssa.

Tietoisku kirjastosta -sarja nostaa esiin kirjastojen näkökulmia ajankohtaisiin ja yhteisiin asioihin sekä ihmisten arkeen. Yle on esittänyt kanavillaan klassikoiksi muodostuneita tietoiskuja, joissa on muistutettu ja opastettu kansalaisia yhteiskunnallisesti tärkeissä asioissa, kuten turvallisuudessa, terveydessä ja arjen valinnoissa. Kirjastot herättävät tämän mainion kerronnan tavan henkiin omassa kontekstissaan ja tuottavat tietoiskuja kaikelle kansalle.

title: Lämnade du in en ansökan i september?
content:
I september hade många av våra specialfonder ansökningstid och också många bidragsformer med specifika ändamål. Vi fick över 2 000 ansökningar och behandlingen av de flesta ansökningar är ännu i full gång.

De allra flesta som lämnade in en ansökan i september måste vänta på besked till mitten av december.

Då beslutar Kulturfondens styrelse om de nästan 1 200 ansökningar som lämnades in inom våra bidragsformer med österbottnisk eller nyländsk anknytning.

Redan i november kunde vår styrelse ta beslut om utdelningen inom en del bidragsformer med ansökningstid i september. Det här gäller:

title: When Jorge Luis Borges Co-Wrote a Surreal Sci-Fi Noir Film: Invasión (1969)
content: “La ciudad es más que la gente.” So declares a character called Don Porfirio in Invasión, the debut feature by Argentine director Hugo Santiago. The line is the film’s most memorable, not least because of the reversal it pulls on our expectations. Saying that a city is really its people must have been a somewhat banal observation even in 1969, when Invasión came out, but saying that a city is more than its people still sounds contrarian enough to be intriguing. It’s even more compelling coming from Don Porfirio, a mastermind whose intensely abstracted manner and refined literary diction will remind some viewers of no figure so much as Jorge Luis Borges — and as well he might, since Borges co-wrote the script.

title: Dutch resist ‘unacceptable’ US bid to tighten semiconductor export controls
content:
BRUSSELS — The Netherlands has pushed back against a U.S. congressional bid to tighten restrictions on exports of advanced chipmaking equipment to China, warning that Washington’s attempt to dictate the rules for Dutch companies such as ASML is unacceptable.

The Dutch objections come as the proposed MATCH Act gains fresh momentum in Washington following revelations about Nvidia’s former chief executive Jensen Huang and his links to a suspected Chinese spy, intensifying concerns in Congress about Beijing’s access to advanced U.S. technology.

The bipartisan legislation would give U.S. allies, including the Netherlands and Japan, 150 days to align restrictions on sales and servicing of advanced chipmaking equipment to China with those imposed by Washington, or show progress toward doing so. If they fail to comply, the U.S. Commerce Department would be required to extend American export controls unilaterally to equipment supplied from those countries.

“The main concern is the bill’s extraterritorial character,” a spokesperson for the Dutch Ministry of Foreign Affairs told POLITICO on Tuesday.

content:

Muutosvarauksin

Herra presidentti,

Aluksi haluan vilpittömästi kiittää presidentti Gauckia hänen ystävällisistä sanoistaan. Minulle on suuri kunnia vastaanottaa Walther-Rathenau-palkinto.

Otan palkinnon vastaan kiitollisena sekä Suomen puolesta että kaikkien niiden puolesta, jotka uskovat. etteivät rauha, vapaus ja kansainvälinen yhteistyö ole itsestäänselvyyksiä. Ne ovat valintoja, jotka jokaisen sukupolven on tehtävä uudelleen.

Walther Rathenau ymmärsi tämän. Hän oli monessa mielessä eurooppalainen jo ennen kuin Eurooppa oli olemassa sellaisena kuin me sen nykyään tunnemme. Hän ymmärsi, että vauraus edellyttää avoimuutta, turvallisuus yhteistyötä ja demokratia vastuullisuutta.

Nämä ajatukset muovasivat Eurooppaa 1900-luvulla. Ne ovat yhtä tärkeitä 2000-luvulla.

Elämme parhaillaan syvällisen murroksen aikaa. Saksassa on sille oma sana: Zeitenwende. Tämä osuva sana on vakiintunut kansainväliseen sanastoon samaan tapaan kuin Schadenfreude, Zeitgeist ja Kindergarten. Suomesta vain yksi sana on saavuttanut vastaavan maailmanlaajuisen menestyksen: sauna.

Mutta Zeitenwende on paljon enemmän kuin vain sana. Se on kuvaus ajastamme.

title: Nuoret arkkitehdit vievät suomalaista kiertotalousosaamista maailmalle apurahan turvin
content:
Bryggman-apuraha luovutettiin Turun Sampotalossa 17.11. järjestetyssä tilaisuudessa.

Heljä Nieminen ja Havu Järvelä perustivat yhdessä Keltaisen toimiston vuonna 2021. Kaksikko on menestynyt arkkitehtuurikilpailuissa: he sijoittuivat toiseksi muun muassa Trondheimin taidemuseon (2025) ja Keran hallien uudelleenkäytön (2023) kilpailuissa ja jakoivat kolmannen sijan Sara Hildénin taidemuseon kilpailussa (2021).

Apurahan turvin arkkitehdit osallistuvat kolmeen kilpailuun, joiden tehtävät sopivat kiertotalousratkaisujen kehittämiseen. Kilpailut valitaan myöhemmin. Kilpailutöissä tarkastellaan rakennuskannan ja rakennusosien uudelleenkäyttöä, rakennusten muuntojoustavuutta ja ehjänä purettavuutta sekä vähähiilisten materiaalien arkkitehtonisia mahdollisuuksia.

Suomessa avoimet arkkitehtuurikilpailut ovat perinteisesti olleet nuorille tekijöille väylä uudistaa alaa.

“Haluamme kehittää kiertotalousratkaisuja kilpailuissa, koska niissä voi soveltaa uusinta tutkimustietoa vapaasti. Toteutusratkaisut ovat vielä auki”, Nieminen sanoo.

Kaksikon mukaan Keski-Euroopassa ollaan Suomea selvästi edellä monissa kiertotalouden ratkaisuissa, esimerkiksi rakennusosien laajamittaisessa uudelleenkäytössä.

title: Herneen viljelyala nousi yli 50 000 hehtaariin
content:
Suomalaiset peltoviljelijät uudistavat tuotantoaan, ja herneen viljelyala nousi yli 50 000 hehtaariin, tiedottaa Maa- ja Metsätaloustuottajain Keskusliitto (MTK). 

Peltoviljelyn kannattavuus on edelleen Suomessa heikkoa. Vuonna 2026 peltoalaa siirtyi muun muassa valkuais- ja öljykasveille, ja viljakasvien ala pieneni noin seitsemän prosenttia.

MTK:n mukaan peltokasvien monipuolistaminen avaa mahdollisuuksia, mutta niiden hyödyntäminen edellyttää toimivia markkinoita ja yhteistyötä koko ruokaketjulta. Huoltovarmuus ja kotimainen ruoantuotanto säilyvät vain, jos niiden perustana on kannattavat maatilat, järjestö vetoaa.

"Kulunut kasvukausi osoitti, että viljelijät ovat valmiita vaihtamaan perinteisiä viljakasveja muihin tuotantokasveihin ja haluavat vahvistaa kotimaisen kasvivalkuaisen tuotantoa. Myös näiden kasvien tuottamisen on kuitenkin oltava taloudellisesti kannattavaa", MTK:n asiantuntija Max Schulman toteaa tiedotteessa.

title: Kuuntelemiskeskuksessa naiset saavat puhua vapaasti
content:
NAISET istuvat pienellä sisäpihalla ryhmissä. Yksi ryhmä pyörittelee saippuamassaa palloiksI, toinen vaivaa käsin taikinaa. Kolmas ryhmä ompelee ompelukoneilla. Olemme Kirkon Ulkomaanavun (KUA) naisille suunnatussa ”kuuntelemiskeskuksessa”, paikassa, jonne naiset voivat tulla, kun he kohtaavat ongelmia.

Arki Paouassa on haastavaa. Alueella on levoton lähihistoria, ja viimeisimmän konfliktin, joka oli pahimmillaan vuosina 2013–2014, jäljet näkyvät yhä sekä tuhoutuneissa rakennuksissa että ihmisten käyttäytymisessä. Väkivalta leimahtaa nopeasti, mikä näkyy myös kodeissa.

”Tulin tänne ensimmäisen kerran, koska mieheni pahoinpiteli minua”, kertoo Dendo Rosine, yksi saippuaa valmistavista naisista.

Häneltä puuttuu edelleen useita etuhampaita.

”Kuuntelemiskeskuksesta sain apua. Sain henkistä tukea ja tukea yhteydenpidossa sairaalaan. Keskuksen työntekijät puhuivat myös mieheni kanssa. Kotona on nyt rauhallisempaa”, Dendo Rosine jatkaa.

Hänen tarinansa on hyvin tavallinen niiden naisten joukossa, joita keskukseen saapuu.

title: Kyrgyz Man Sentenced to Three Years For Re-Posting Video on Facebook
content:
A Kyrgyzstan court has sentenced a construction worker and father of four children to three years in penal colony for a Facebook post that was critical of authorities. 

Baktybek Moldaliev, 48, was sentenced last week in the capital, Bishkek, on charges of “distribution of extremist materials.” The material in question is a video by the investigative media outlet Kloop, which he re-posted along with a comment.

While Moldaliev was convicted over the post he made in April, court files obtained by OCCRP show that Kyrgyz authorities had been collecting evidence against him for at least six months before that. 

Police searched Moldaliev’s apartment in November 2025, and brought him to the Ministry of Internal Affairs for questioning about his social media activity. The files do not show any charge against him at that time.

The Ministry of Internal Affairs did not respond to a request for comment.

Moldaliev was detained and questioned again on May 8, according to the files.

He told police: “I had been writing posts expressing my personal opinions on political and social issues occurring in the Kyrgyz Republic, specifically regarding the high cost of living, unemployment, and corruption.”

content: Last week, we introduced you to the creatures of COP31. Today, we zoom in on a species that seems to be slowly going extinct at the global climate conference: the European leader. title: A Federal Women’s Prison Became a “Rape Club.” After Officials Shut It Down, Rampant Abuse Continued Elsewhere.
content:
Officer Felix Wilder sauntered around the women’s prison like he owned the place. 

Prone to showing up to work in gold chains and stylish jeans instead of his concrete gray government uniform, the slender 35-year-old moved, one woman said, “like he had just gotten off of a horse from a long ride.” He spoke slowly and eyed the prisoners as they walked through the drab buildings and shadeless yards of the secluded federal lockup in Aliceville, Alabama.

By the fall of 2024, some of the women there had begun to notice him hovering over a soft-spoken immigrant from Mexico who’d been in prison for only a few years. Ela, as she asked to be called, had dark hair, dark eyes and children to get home to back in Utah. Wilder was just a little too close, a little too familiar.

Ela’s cellmate, who asked to be identified as Ana, watched it all with unease. At 40, she knew exactly what that kind of attention from an officer could mean in a women’s prison.
snippet: Officer Felix Wilder sauntered around the women’s prison like he owned the place.

title: In win against impunity, Indonesian court orders the reform of Military Justice Law
content:
The court ruled that soldiers who committed criminal offenses should be tried by civilian courts

Originally published on Global Voices

Constitutional Court of Indonesia in Jakarta. Photo by Christophe95. Wikipedia. CC BY-SA 4.0

This post is part of Global Voices’ November 2026 Spotlight series, “Justice as infrastructure.” In this Spotlight, Global Voices is partnering with The Hague Institute for Innovation of Law (HiiL) to highlight the ways justice functions as critical infrastructure for any society. You can support this coverage by donating here.

Indonesia’s Constitutional Court ruled that the 1997 Military Justice Law would be invalid unless amended within two years. The decision was hailed by human rights groups because it means soldiers who commit crimes can be tried in civilian courts.

Article 9 of the Military Justice Law requires active-duty personnel of the Indonesian National Armed Forces to be held accountable exclusively under the military justice system, even when they commit ordinary criminal offenses and human rights violations.

title: An atlas of vanished places: how climate change is rewriting the books on our shelves
content:
On August 26, 2026, a huge mass of rock and ice broke away at an altitude of around 5,200 metres in the Himalayas. Within minutes, it became an avalanche of debris and water that hurtled down towards the Nepal-Tibet border, with such force that the seismic signals were initially mistaken for an earthquake.

The region’s glaciers are visibly retreating, and thawing permafrost may well have contributed to destabilising these Himalayan slopes. Above all, the Nepal landslide illustrates something that will only become increasingly familiar: places that appear stable can change almost without warning.

While events like the Nepal landslide have an immediate, devastating impact on the people who live in these environments, they also leave their mark in a less obvious sphere: literature.

Biologist Rachel Carson’s 1951 book The Sea Around Us reminded readers that the boundary between land and sea has never been stable. Throughout our planet’s very long history, the oceans have advanced and receded. What makes the current situation exceptional is the speed of this transformation, as well as human activity’s decisive contribution to it.

title: Fighting in Yemen has made crossing the Bab el-Mandeb even more dangerous – jeopardizing aid and refuge for millions
content:
In recent days, Iran-backed Houthi forces have gained greater control of the Bab al-Mandeb Strait, a vital hub of trade, travel and migration between the Middle East and Africa.

The partial closing of the Strait of Hormuz as part of the war in Iran – and escalating conflicts in Yemen, Ethiopia and Eritrea – had already brought this narrow waterway into new global prominence. Control over the Bab el-Mandeb Strait remains critical to military operations and commodity markets throughout the region.

However, the Bab el-Mandeb’s strategic geopolitical and commercial shipping importance has largely overshadowed its role as a critical humanitarian corridor.

Bab el-Mandeb means “gate of lamentation” or, more poetically, “gate of tears” in Arabic. It remains one of the most dangerous migration passages in the world. Last year, more than 900 people died or went missing trying to cross. In October 2026, a boat capsized off the coast of Djibouti carrying nearly 300 people, many of whom were escaping violence and persecution.

title: As U.S. Boycotts U.N. Climate Talks, California Leads State/City Efforts to Combat Climate Crisis
content:
For the second year in a row, the Trump administration has not sent an official delegation to the United Nations’ annual climate change conference, held this year in Antalya, Turkey. But although no federal representatives are present, more than 120 U.S. state and local leaders are participating, including the governor of the fourth-largest economy in the world, California Governor Gavin Newsom. Newsom, a likely candidate for the 2028 Democratic presidential nomination, has endorsed the Santa Marta Process, a coalition of nations working to develop a global green energy transition.

“The petrostates have made it abundantly clear: Under the current rules of consensus, they are never, ever going to allow COPs to succeed. They’re just not going to sign that agreement. So, essentially, the Santa Marta coalition is making an end run around that, using economic power,” says longtime environmental and climate reporter Mark Hertsgaard.

title: The Paramount-Warner Brothers Deal Could Usher in Another Age of Lost Media
content:
There are all sorts of reasons to be against the merger of Paramount and Warner Brothers-Discovery. There's the obvious problem of increasing concentration in the already pretty-concentrated film and TV industry. People have problems with Paramount's owner Skydance interfering  with its news coverage and late night comedy. But one of the biggest is the way we are losing choice and access to information and culture.  

In the context of the digital world, there are two major problems with these mega mergers. One, as we've said in the past, is that it further degrades the already awful state of mainstream streaming services. In short, by increasing the amount of legacy content under their control, major studios don't have to invest in either new content or well-engineered services to get users. Plus, they can pool the data they have on users together in an increasing assault on consumer privacy. A monthly subscription and more information about your habits and interests? Win-win for them.

content:
Black Friday ja joulu tarkoittavat kiireisiä aikoja paitsi verkkokaupoille myös verkkorikollisille. Kuluttajan tulee olla tarkkana, sillä huijauksia on liikkeellä tavallistakin enemmän. title: ICC: Afghanistan Decision Risks Narrowing Access to Justice
content:
(The Hague) – An International Criminal Court (ICC) decision risks hindering a path to justice for victims of grave crimes committed in Afghanistan, Human Rights Watch said today. On November 12, 2026, an ICC pretrial chamber, citing a lack of activity, effectively closed the court’s situation dealing with crimes by US, Afghan government, and other forces prior to the Taliban’s August 2021 takeover.

The ICC prosecutor’s office on November 13 sought to appeal the decision and to seek a stay of the closure decision. Research by Human Rights Watch and others over many years has documented war crimes and crimes against humanity by the Taliban; the Islamic State Khorasan Province (ISKP), an ISIS-affiliated group; Afghan government forces; and US military and Central Intelligence Agency (CIA) forces.

“Victims of serious international crimes committed by warring parties during Afghanistan’s long conflict have faced many roadblocks to justice,” said Liz Evenson, international justice director at Human Rights Watch. “The ICC judges’ decision threatens to compound barriers to future accountability for US and Afghan government forces.”

title: AI-kahvit: Mitä tekoäly ei näe? Ihminen ja tekoäly yhdessä kirjaston työssä
content:
Tämä Teams-tallenne on osa AI-kahvit-sarjaa, jonka on tuottanut Yleisten kirjastojen tekoälyosaamisen kehittämishanke. AI-kahveilla pohditaan tällä kertaa, miten tekoälyä voi käyttää osana omaa työtä niin, että oma ajattelu, harkinta ja luovuus eivät jää taka-alalle, ja mitkä asiat halutaan pitää ihmisen käsissä.

Aiheesta puhuu kouluttaja Kira Sjöberg Goodinilta. Webinaari alkaa pienellä kokeilulla: osallistujat pyytävät tekoälyltä lukupiirisuosituksia ja tarkistavat vastaukset. Kokeilu näyttää, miksi tekoälyn vastaus voi kuulostaa varmalta, vaikka se ei pidä paikkaansa, ja miksi kaikki pitää tarkistaa. Sjöberg käsittelee, mitä tekoäly ei näe: hiljaista tietoa, puuttuvaa dataa (esimerkiksi pienet kielet ja paikallinen tieto) sekä sitä, miten samojen mallien käyttö voi yhdenmukaistaa sisältöjä. Hän pohtii, mitä työssä kannattaa pitää ihmisen käsissä (vastuu, harkinta ja kohtaaminen) ja miten tekoälyä voi käyttää hakukoneen sijaan ajattelukumppanina. Hän nostaa esiin myös kirjastoammattilaisten osaamisen tiedon järjestämisessä, jota tekoälyn aikakaudella tarvitaan yhä enemmän. Webinaari järjestettiin 17.11.2026.

title: Watch Accurate Recreations of Medieval Italian Longsword Fighting Techniques, All Based on a Manuscript from 1404
content:
Given recent history, the prospect of hundreds of young men meeting on Facebook, then traveling from around the country to a central U.S. location might sound like reasonable cause for alarm. Yet a convention fitting that description had nothing to do with political violence but, rather, a celebration and appreciation of the name “Josh” (full disclosure: this writer did not attend). The gathering of the Joshes in April 2021 in Nebraska could not have been more peaceful, including its finishing battle royale, conducted with pool noodles.

The Joshes had no concern for proper pool-noodle-wielding technique, if there is such a thing. But groups of people who gather around the country to stage medieval-style battles in live-action role playing (LARP) games with weapons both real and fake might benefit from pointers.

So, too, might those who choreograph sword fights on stage and screen. Where can serious historical re-creators learn how to wield a real blade in historically accurate combat? One resource can be found at Wiktenauer, a wiki devoted to collecting “all of the primary and secondary source literature that makes up the text of historical European Martial arts (HEMA) research.”

title: EU Commission eyes rule change to retaliate faster against China
content:
BRUSSELS — The European Commission is considering changes to its trade enforcement rules that would allow Brussels to respond more swiftly to serious economic threats as it develops a new instrument aimed primarily at China.

The EU’s Enforcement Regulation already allows the bloc to impose countermeasures when trade disputes get stuck in the World Trade Organization’s appeals court. The rule was revamped in 2021 when the court stopped working after Washington blocked appointments of new judges.

Now Brussels is exploring whether the regulation could be tweaked again to allow a broader, quicker response to actions by trading partners that harm EU interests, three people with knowledge of the talks, granted anonymity to discuss the confidential deliberations, told POLITICO.

The work follows a request last month by France and Germany for a new “second strike” tool that would allow the bloc to address economic threats more promptly and effectively.

Other names are being considered for the new instrument, as the bloc wants to ensure it doesn’t borrow from nuclear jargon and draws attention instead to its responsive nature.

title: Lapsen ei pitäisi tunnistaa kalashnikovia sen äänestä
content:
”KUN AMMUSKELU alkoi, lapseni tiesivät äänen perusteella heti, minkälaisia aseita ne olivat. He sanoivat: tuo on konekivääri tai tuo on kalashnikov. Lapsen ei kuulu tietää sellaisia asioita.

Elämämme Antsokiassa oli hyvää. Kotimme sijaitsi isolla tontilla, jossa kasvoi avokadoja ja mangopuita. Oli lämmin, tuoretta ruokaa riitti ja eläminen oli halpaa. Opetin koulussa, minulla oli pieni putiikki ja kasvatin kanoja.

Kylässämme elettiin tiiviisti yhdessä. Jos jollain oli ongelmia, muut auttoivat, oli hän sitten sukua tai ei. Kun lähdin, kylän väki piti minulle jäähyväisjuhlat. Lähteminen tuntui siltä, kuin olisin menettänyt jotakin oleellista itsestäni.

Mutta aseiden äänet kuuluivat yhä uudestaan ja uudestaan. Kaikkialla huhuttiin, että aseelliset joukot olivat lähestymässä ja ne tuhoaisivat koko kaupungin. Kun ammuskelu alkoi, lapset piiloutuivat, koska eivät tienneet, minne paeta. Kun on lapsia, mikään ei ole tärkeämpää kuin rauha.

Koska olin työskennellyt Antsokiassa vuosikausia, onnistuin saamaan siirron Debre Birhaniin. Tulin ensin yksin ja aloin työskennellä. Muutaman kuukauden kuluttua hain lapseni tänne. Lapseni uskoivat, että palaisimme vielä kotiin. En kertonut heille totuutta.

title: Democrats in Washington Move to Ban Data Centers on Public Lands
content:
A dozen Democrats in Congress are calling for limiting or banning the construction of data centers on public lands. The moves follow reporting from ProPublica that revealed Interior Secretary Doug Burgum, who leads the White House’s artificial intelligence push, has tens of millions of dollars invested in AI companies.

“Our public lands aren’t a piggy bank for Trump’s powerful friends,” Sen. Catherine Cortez Masto of Nevada said in a social media post that pointed to ProPublica’s reporting. Her office told the news organization that the senator, who serves on the Energy and Natural Resources Committee, is working on legislation to regulate data centers on public lands and will use the panel’s oversight authority to address concerns about transparency surrounding them.

Burgum was asked about ProPublica’s reporting at a recent event hosted by the conservative website Daily Caller. He said that his financial reporting and ethics were “clean as a whistle,” and that he invested in software companies before they turned to AI. “I don’t even know all the names of the companies that are in the portfolio,” he said of his vast wealth.

title: Europe’s Rwanda return hub raises serious human rights concerns – a migration researcher explains
content:
When I met Chadi, a young Tunisian man recently deported from Italy after crossing the Mediterranean by boat, he was already planning his next attempt: “They brought me here, but I’m not planning on staying.”

His story is worth keeping in mind given that five EU governments – Denmark, Germany, Austria, Greece and the Netherlands – have announced that Rwanda will host Europe’s first “return hub”. This will be a migrant deportation centre, where people whose asylum claims have been rejected, but who cannot yet be sent home, will be held or resettled. The first transfers are planned for 2027, starting with a pilot of around 100 people.

Human rights organisations have warned against hubs in Rwanda – with Amnesty International calling them potential “black holes” for human rights. Indeed, Rwanda is a troubling choice.

Its president, Paul Kagame, was re-elected in 2024 with 99% of the vote. UN experts say Rwanda exercises significant control over the M23 rebels in neighbouring Congo, the brutal conflict’s leading perpetrators of sexual violence. While in 2023, the UK Supreme Court ruled Rwanda unsafe for asylum seekers. So how will Europe guarantee the rights of people it sends there?

title: Bond has always reflected the masculinity of his time – Robert Pattinson’s 007 will need to embody a new era
content:
James Bond has always reflected the cultural anxieties and zeitgeist of his era.

Sean Connery’s Bond embodied the confident western post-second-world-war masculinity of the early cold war. George Lazenby brought the character’s emotional vulnerability to light, reflecting the upheavals of the late 1960s. Roger Moore’s performance, meanwhile, added camp humour, theatricality and escapism in the 1970s.

In keeping with Ian Fleming’s more psychologically complex literary creation, Timothy Dalton brought a darker, more ruthless Bond to the screen. Stripping away much of the Moore era’s comedy and camp, his portrayal foregrounded emotional intensity and moral ambiguity. This reflected late-cold-war anxieties as geopolitical certainties unravelled and new threats emerged.

Next up, Pierce Brosnan incarnated a glamorous post-cold-war masculinity, with his lingering sexism teased out by Samantha Bond’s witty Moneypenny and the disruptive casting of Judi Dench as M, the head of MI6. And in the 2000s, Daniel Craig’s Bond was a physically tough but emotionally vulnerable character. His wounded body and scarred mind linked emotional detachment to childhood trauma.
snippet: James Bond has always reflected the cultural anxieties and zeitgeist of his era.
creator: Monica Germanà, Reader in Gothic and Contemporary Studies, University of Westminster

title: Lakes Are Bizarrely Syncing Up Globally, And Scientists Are Worried
content:
Lakes around the world have become increasingly synced up in their ecological conditions—such as warming temperatures, algal blooms, and oxygen levels—a trend that reveals “a possible fundamental reorganization of the world’s lake systems,” according to a study published on Monday in Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences. 

Lakes come in all kinds of shapes, sizes, and volumes, and vary widely in other critical properties, such as temperature, composition, and biomass. This diversity of lake conditions, known as spatial heterogeneity, serves as a handy buffer against environmental disruptions; because each lake responds to events differently, they curb the spread of potential damage.

But when scientists studied satellite imagery of roughly 2,000 lakes around the world since the year 2000, they discovered that lakes “are undergoing a profound shift toward spatial synchrony through time” that “strongly indicates that increasing lake synchrony is a genuine, global-scale phenomenon,“ according to the study.

title: El Salvador: Public debt is mortgaging the country’s future without guaranteeing rights today
content:
The increase in public debt and indebtedness in El Salvador over the last decade has not led to a proportional and sustainable improvement in access to economic and social rights, according to Amnesty International’s new report, “When the budget does not guarantee rights”. 

The report analyses the evolution of the public budget between 2015 and 2025, documenting how the increasing debt burden, lack of transparency and a concentration of decision-making power within the executive branch have reduced the state’s capacity to mobilize the maximum of its available resources to uphold rights such as the right to health, to education and to social protection. 

“The findings highlight an alarming contradiction: the Salvadoran state is spending more and increasing its indebtedness, but these available resources do not manifest as equivalent improvements for the population. When debt servicing accounts for a larger proportion of the budget than health or education, it is legitimate to question where the money is going and why,” said Ana Piquer, Americas director at Amnesty International.

title: Fossil Fuels Are "Undermining Democracy" & Must Be Phased Out: Climate Activist Kumi Naidoo at COP31
content: What will it take to bring an end to the fossil fuel era? We speak to Kumi Naidoo, the president of the Fossil Fuel Treaty Initiative, which aims to reach a binding agreement for a global transition away from fossil fuels. Currently backed by over 25 countries from the Global South, the intergovernmental process began earlier this year in Santa Marta, Colombia. Meanwhile, at the United Nations, “for 30 years of negotiations, we don’t have any mention of fossil fuels [in the outcome document]. That’s like Alcoholics Anonymous holding 30 years of conferences and not mentioning alcohol,” says Naidoo. We discuss the Fossil Fuel Treaty Initiative’s goals, how the oil and gas industry drives global conflict, and the Trump administration’s glaring absence from international action on climate change.

title: Privacy's Defenders Podcast: Snowden Exposes NSA’s Lies
content:
By 2013, EFF had spent seven years arguing in court that the National Security Agency was sweeping up ordinary Americans’ communications, including through the secret room that whistleblower Mark Klein had exposed. The government would neither confirm nor deny it, and outside the courtroom the public seemed to have moved on.  

Then, in early June, documentary filmmaker Laura Poitras and journalist Glenn Greenwald mysteriously missed a Freedom of the Press Foundation board meeting at EFF’s offices. It turned out they were in Hong Kong, meeting an NSA contractor who had been secretly writing to Laura for months. His name was Edward Snowden, he had thousands of secret documents proving the government had in fact been spying on millions of Americans. When he subsequently revealed himself, a photo of him sitting behind his laptop – emblazoned with a big red EFF sticker – went worldwide. 

Welcome to the fourth episode of “Privacy’s Defenders,” a podcast about the people – lawyers, journalists, hackers, and others – who’ve fought to secure your digital liberties since before most people even knew what the internet was.

(You can also find this episode on the Internet Archive and on YouTube.)

title: UN Committee Proposes Drastic Cuts to Afghanistan Investigations
content:
A United Nations budgetary advisory committee has proposed sweeping cuts to the Afghanistan accountability mechanism, established by consensus by the UN Human Rights Council in October 2025 following years of negotiations. 

The Independent Investigative Mechanism for Afghanistan was created to support efforts to hold the Taliban and others responsible for international crimes in Afghanistan to account. It is expected to include a focus on the Taliban’s crimes against humanity of gender persecution. Like similar mechanisms for Myanmar and Syria, it was designed to collect and preserve evidence and prepare files to support criminal prosecutions. Its formation followed years of campaigning by Afghan and international human rights groups on the basis that it could be a key tool in securing justice for victims of grave abuses. Its investigations could also act as a deterrent for current Taliban commanders.

title: Irish regulator stops X training AI with data gathered by agents
content:
Ireland’s privacy regulator has forced X to stop feeding AI models with data collected by its agents, the authority told POLITICO.

The social media giant owned by Elon Musk has suspended the use of so-called third-party data collected by its Grok Bot AI agent, which started mining this data in late October to train its AI systems.

The Irish Data Protection Commission (DPC) raised “significant concerns” about that data processing in recent weeks, Commissioner Dale Sunderland told POLITICO in an interview. “We asked them to suspend the processing, and they’ve confirmed to us today that they’ve done that,” he said Monday.

X did not respond to a request for comment.

The Irish privacy authority is the most powerful in Europe, as it enforces Europe’s data protection rulebook on companies that have their regional headquarters in Ireland, including Apple, Google, Meta, X and OpenAI.

The X action is a test case as privacy regulators shift their focus from AI training that uses data people have shared about themselves, to third-party data that personal AI agents are accessing and gathering on other people.

title: Kuuntelemisen merkitys kasvaa arvoon arvaamattomaan
content:
VOIN TYÖSSÄNI istua tuntikausia sellaisten henkilöiden kanssa, joiden elämä on täysin erilaista kuin minun, ja esittää syvällisiä henkilökohtaisia kysymyksiä.

Toisinaan käy niin, että henkilöllä ei ehkä ole koskaan ollut tilaa puhua juuri siitä asiasta, josta haluan tietää. Huomaan yllättävän usein, että ilmapiiri on kevyempi haastattelun jälkeen, vaikka kysymykseni voivat koskea traumaattisiakin kokemuksia. Vihdoin joku kuuntelee tuomitsematta.

Huomasimme, kuinka tärkeää kuunteleminen on myös vieraillessamme naisten kuuntelemiskeskuksessa Paouassa, Keski-Afrikan tasavallassa. Kaikki tapaamamme naiset olivat kokeneet perheväkivaltaa, raiskauksia tai muita vaikeita vastoinkäymisiä, mutta kuuntelemiskeskuksessa he istuivat ryhmissä, juttelivat rennosti ja hymyilivät.

Jokainen nainen, jonka kanssa juttelin, kertoi, kuinka tärkeää oli ollut, että joku oli kuunnellut heitä ja antanut neuvoja. Oli hienoa nähdä, kuinka prosessi oli vahvistanut heidän itseluottamustaan.

KUN TEIMME syvähaastattelun 21-vuotiaan Olivierin kanssa, huomasin myös toisen pitkien keskusteluiden luoman edun. (Olivier esiintyy Tekoja-lehden seuraavassa numerossa, joka ilmestyy helmikuussa 2027.)

title: I Photographed Her Parents as They Were Sentenced for Her Twin’s Death. Years Later, I Photographed Her Life.
content:
About eight years ago, I was assigned to photograph the sentencing of Travis and Sarah Mitchell, a couple with deep roots in an insular faith-healing sect outside of Portland, Oregon.  

The Mitchells, as members of the Followers of Christ, adhere to a doctrine that forbids medical care. Instead, followers rely on healing through faith. So when Sarah Mitchell gave birth prematurely to twins in 2017 — and both gasped for breath in their first hours — the couple didn’t rush them to an emergency room. Instead, they turned to prayer. 

One twin, Ginnifer, lived for four hours, each one a struggle. The family eventually sought medical care for her surviving twin sister, Evelyn, but only after the county’s deputy medical examiner arrived at the location of the home birth and learned, though not right away, of Evelyn’s existence. Even then, he had to seek help from police, who arrived at the Oregon City home and told reluctant family members to take the struggling infant to the hospital or they’d do it themselves.

title: Burundi’s refugees are under pressure to return: why some choose silence when they do
content:
Burundi has experienced repeated cycles of political violence and displacement, notably following the assassination of President Melchior Ndadayé in 1993. Further unrest followed during an election-related political crisis in 2015.

These cycles of unrest have resulted in thousands of deaths and forced hundreds of thousands of Burundians to flee their country. Over the past two decades, more than 1.1 million have sought refuge in other countries, primarily in neighbouring Tanzania. Others have fled to Rwanda, the Democratic Republic of Congo, Uganda and further.

There’s growing pressure from the Burundian state, as well as from neighbouring host countries, including Tanzania, Uganda and Kenya, to encourage repatriation. This reflects a broader regional shift in which the continued presence of Burundian refugees outside their country is becoming increasingly conditional.

Indeed, under international initiatives led by the UN refugee agency, Burundi has established a formal policy framework for repatriation. But return to contexts of forced displacement, violence and other forms of persecution has prompted questions about whether it can work and how it is experienced by those who return.

title: 'Defense by ChatGPT'
content:
We've written a lot about how AI generated writing has collided with – and created chaos for – the legal system in the last few years, from lawyers using it to do their research and filings for them to judges getting extremely fed up with dealing with these attorneys. In some cases, judges have sanctioned offending attorneys thousands of dollars for using AI to do their jobs, and lawyers give endless excuses when they're busted, with some calling it a “cautionary tale." Today's story is about how the DOJ is getting involved: by trying to catch attorneys doing "defense by ChatGPT."

Lawyers for the Department of Justice are using the AI writing detection service Pangram to argue that opposing attorneys are using AI to write legal arguments, and in one case told the court that opposing counsel was doing “defense by ChatGPT,” and writing “AI slop” filings, according to court filings reviewed by 404 Media.

title: Azerbaijan: Abzas Media staff endure three years behind bars for independent journalism
content:
Ahead of the third anniversary of the earliest arrests of Abzas Media journalists in Azerbaijan, Marie Struthers, Amnesty International’s Eastern Europe and Central Asia Director, said:

“Three years on, seven Abzas Media journalists remain behind bars in desperate conditions, far from their families. They were among the first targets in what has become a sweeping crackdown on independent journalism in Azerbaijan.

“The reprisals do not end with unfounded imprisonment. Relatives and lawyers report increased use of solitary confinement, denial of health care, beatings and other ill-treatment against the Abzas Media journalists and others jailed for critical journalism and dissenting views.

“The Azerbaijani authorities must immediately and unconditionally release all those imprisoned solely for the exercise of their right to freedom of expression. They must provide all prisoners with adequate health care, promptly investigate reports of abuse and put an end to all forms of ill-treatment.”

title: European Commission Plan to Give Frontex Trusted Flagger Status Is A Threat to Free Speech
content:
EFF and 27 other human rights organizations called on the European Commission today to retract a dangerous proposal granting its border agency Frontex power to request that national authorities issue takedown orders for social media content and giving Frontext “trusted flagger” status under the Digital Services Act (DSA), the EU regulation governing online platforms and content moderation in the region.

The extraordinarily improper proposal not only disregards the provisions of the DSA but also places a mechanism of enforcement overreach in the hands of a law enforcement agency that has failed to safeguard people against serious human rights violations at EU borders.

Under the proposal, Frontex has the power to “monitor publicly accessible social media content, detect developments relevant to external border management, and support action against illegal online content linked to border-security risks.” Granting Frontex trusted flagger privileges on top of its existing mandate risks creating a powerful tool for over-enforcement, stifling the free expression of migrants, asylum seekers, and other marginalized groups. We warned the Commission of these risks in a letter.

The DSA is supposed to make online platforms more accountable and protect users’ fundamental rights, not give the EU power to sic its border police on people for exercising their right to free expression.

EFF and other rights organizations have for years sounded alarms about potential abuse under the DSA’s trusted flagger provision, which gives “Digital Services Coordinators” the ability to award entities—including law enforcement agencies—a privileged channel to alert online platforms about illegal content. We’ve taken the firm position that law enforcement cannot be trusted to properly flag illegal content. In July, we told the Commission that giving law enforcement trusted flagger status could undermine fundamental rights and said that police agencies like Frontex should not be made trusted flaggers. 

The EU proposal gives Frontex decision-making power over free expression that is not envisaged under the DSA. First, content removal orders can only be issued by relevant national authorities. The DSA does not foresee a role for entities like Frontex to request such orders. Second, trusted flaggers notify platforms of suspected illegal content—platforms must prioritize these notices and they have sole responsibility to decide to remove content. It’s not flaggers’ role to request removal orders from national authorities. Combining these powers blur enforcement and flagging functions, which the Commission’s own draft guidelines on trusted flaggers explicitly caution against. 

“The risk of Frontex utilizing its power as both a Trusted Flagger and authority that can demand removal orders, to surveil user-generated speech, and over-flag content under the guise of  ‘border security risk’ is clear. This will likely result in platforms over-censoring content and chilling the speech of already marginalized groups, particularly those from migrant and asylum-seeking communities,” the letter says. 

We urge the Commission to rescind the proposal. It undermines the DSA, threatens fundamental rights of citizens and non-citizens, and is enforcement overreach that does not align with international human rights standards.

title: Bangladesh: Education Crisis for Rohingya Refugee Children
content:
(Bangkok) – Humanitarian education programs for Rohingya refugee children in Bangladesh are struggling amid a collapse in donor funding, Human Rights Watch said today. Donors should fully fund the education programs, while Bangladesh should recognize and the United Nations should support a separate Rohingya-led school network.

Humanitarian education programs have enrolled 312,000 out of approximately 500,000 school-age Rohingya children in the Bangladesh refugee camps. But the programs, which aid cuts had shuttered for months in 2025, are barely adequate even for the children they reach and may close again, humanitarian officials told Human Rights Watch. While resources are shrinking, about 90,000 more refugee children need schooling this year, due to population growth and new arrivals fleeing atrocities in Myanmar. The donor-supported programs have largely ignored the schools that Rohingya teachers set up in the camps, which are well-regarded by refugees for their quality of education, but lack legal status and reach only about 30,000 students.

title: What the EU can learn from Mark Carney on digital sovereignty
content:
At Davos earlier this year, Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney offered a compelling response to a world increasingly shaped by great-power rivalry. Middle powers need greater strategic autonomy, he argued, but they cannot secure it by retreating behind their borders.

Instead, they need to build their own capabilities while working more closely with like-minded partners. On technology, he reasoned that countries should cooperate so they are not ultimately forced to choose between “hegemons and hyperscalers.”

At the recent EU-Canada Summit, that philosophy began to translate into policy. Canada and the EU launched an “Alliance for the Future” based on closer economic, technological and strategic cooperation. They also concluded negotiations on a Digital Trade Agreement designed to support a “secure, open and trusted digital environment”​ resilient economic relations​,​ and trusted cross-border data flows.

That principle matters not only for Europe’s new relationship with Canada, but for its approach to other trusted partners.

Sovereignty without isolation

title: Miksi puhdas vesi ja ruoka ovat tärkeitä hätäavussa?
content:
Puhdas vesi ja ruoka ovat hätäavussa elintärkeitä siksi, että ilman niitä ihminen ei yksinkertaisesti selviä hengissä. Veden puute tappaa päivissä, aliravitsemus viikoissa, ja kriisioloissa nämä uhat kertautuvat nopeasti. Alla käymme läpi, miksi vesi ja ruoka ovat humanitaarisen avun ytimessä, ketkä kärsivät eniten ja miten voit itse vaikuttaa.

Kun puhdas vesi loppuu kriisialueella, seurauksena on välitön terveyskatastrofi. Ihmiset alkavat käyttää saastunutta vettä, mikä levittää nopeasti koleraa, lavantautia ja ripulitauteja. Nämä sairaudet ovat hengenvaarallisia erityisesti lapsille ja jo valmiiksi heikentyneille ihmisille, ja ne voivat tappaa tuntien tai päivien sisällä.

Veden puute ei kuitenkaan tarkoita vain janoa. Se tarkoittaa, että hygienian ylläpitäminen käy mahdottomaksi. Käsienpesu, haavojen puhdistaminen ja ruoan valmistaminen turvallisesti edellyttävät kaikki puhdasta vettä. Kun näitä perusedellytyksiä ei ole, taudit leviävät räjähdysmäisesti tiheästi asutuissa pakolaisleireissä ja hätämajoituksissa.

title: CFP: MATTER & MEMORY: The Preservation of Cultural and Material Heritage
content:
SESSION CALL:

MATTER & MEMORY: The Preservation of Cultural and Material Heritage

PORTO

Conference: Heritages 2027
Dates: 16-18, June, 2027
Abstracts due: 10 Dec, 2026

https://amps-research.com/porto-ipca-themes/

SESSION CALL

Cultural heritage is continually interpreted, preserved and transformed through changing historical, social and artistic contexts. This session builds on this and examines how societies construct, transmit and reassess cultural memory through objects, monuments, artworks, archives and historic environments. We argue that within history and art history, such processes raise important questions about authenticity, authorship, representation and the changing meanings attached to cultural artefacts and sites.

Contributions might consider contemporary interventions in historic buildings, restoration and reconstruction, digital technologies, museum practices, or new approaches to documenting and interpreting the past.

title: Inside the first EU Culture Dialogue. Will national governments step up?
content:
On 12 November 2026, the first EU Culture Dialogue took place in Brussels hosted by Commissioner Glenn Micallef. The day was full of important announcements from the Commission, lively discussions among 60 representatives of cultural organisations and a bit of planning for the future of EU cultural policy amidst ongoing political drama. Culture Action Europe was represented by Lars Ebert in the morning and Luiza Moroz in the afternoon. Stay with us for this long read as we unpack what happened, what was said and, most importantly, what we made of it all at the end.  

The structured dialogue is a way for the European Commission and the cultural sector to stay in touch and, hopefully, co-create cultural policies together. It gives cultural organisations, networks, and artists a regular opportunity to bring their experience to the Commission, discuss what it is proposing and help decide what should be on the agenda.

Europpan parlamentin valiokunnissa käsitellään tällä viikolla muun muassa asumisen kohtuuhintaisuutta, demokratian kriisinkestävyyttä, muuttoliikettä, rajaturvallisuutta ja EU:n talousarviota. Maanantaina ulkoasiainneuvoston asialistalla puolestaan ovat Ukraina, hybridiuhat ja Lähi-idän tilanne. Tiistaina puolustusministerien kokouksessa keskustellaan EU:n ja Kiinan turvallisuussuhteista, Ukrainan tukemisesta sekä transatlanttisesta puolustusyhteistyöstä.

Parlamentin valtuuskunta ja ympäristökomissaari Jessika Roswall osallistuvat myös Antalyassa järjestettävään YK:n 31. ilmastokokoukseen (COP31).

title: Iraq Cracks Down on Oil Smuggling in Area Controlled by Iran-aligned Shiite Militias
content:
In a rare bid to assert state authority inside a paramilitary-controlled enclave, the Iraqi government has launched a campaign to dismantle oil smuggling networks in Jurf al-Nasr, a stronghold of Iran-backed militias along the Euphrates River, roughly 30 miles southwest of the capital.

The crackdown takes direct aim at an illicit fuel trade operating inside an area that has long functioned outside of Baghdad’s authority.

The move followed the leak of an intelligence report, seen by OCCRP, that detailed the smuggling operation and included satellite imagery showing container truck movements between pipelines and local storage facilities from 2022 to 2026. The report cited evidence of perforated oil pipelines and makeshift storage facilities, adding that the armed groups controlling the area smuggled the fuel along three suspected routes leading into Baghdad province.

title: In Brazil’s elections, big techs’ transparency and cooperation policies translate as governance washing, according to this expert
content:
Rio de Janeiro’s Federal University NetLab has been following closely how this election unfolds on social media

Originally published on Global Voices Advox

Art by Global Voices, created in Canva Pro.

Amid a series of corruption scandals, the 2026 general election in Brazil is also flooded with headlines about social media companies’ role in the campaign. Users supporting the candidacy of Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, the incumbent center-left candidate running for re-election, have been reporting a sudden drop in their Instagram Stories views when posting about politics. They say that Meta AI refused to generate images featuring Lula’s name and party number, while delivering the same request for Flávio Bolsonaro, his far-right opponent and the son of the imprisoned former president Jair Bolsonaro.

On October 16, Meta admitted technical problems on its platforms which affected how pro-Lula content was delivered to users. As reported by the Associated Press, despite acknowledging “global technical glitches, strict anti-fraud measures, and regulatory compliance rather than targeted suppression,” the company that owns Instagram, WhatsApp and Facebook denied any political bias.

    Told through the eyes of Margarita herself, the film offers a rare portrait of an ancient way of life from a fresh, surprising voice – not an elder or chief, but a young woman standing at a crossroads, questioning her future.

    Margarita’s coming-of-age story unfolds in the present while gaining depth and resonance through intimate family footage spanning over 20 years. With her voice always at the center, she guides us through a tapestry of past and present, revealing a story of extraordinary change in the High Arctic.

title: Advancing CC Signals: Preparing for Public Alpha Testing in 2027
content:
How can we give the people and organizations that share and make collections of knowledge and creativity available in the commons a meaningful way to encourage reciprocity from AI developers?

This question is central to Creative Commons’ ongoing development of CC Signals, a framework of legal tools and guiding norms designed to encourage reciprocity in how AI systems use shared knowledge. 

On November 2-3, Creative Commons convened a group of open knowledge organizations in Chicago to advance this work. Building on earlier conversations and workshops with legal, policy, and technical experts, the two-day gathering focused on refining the first CC Signals legal tool and preparing for the release of an alpha version in early 2027. 

The gathering brought together several organizations exploring early adoption of CC Signals, bringing perspectives from open journalism, scholarly publishing, education, and cultural heritage. Participants included representatives from the Wikimedia Foundation, The Conversation, Cambridge University Press and Assessment, MIT Open Learning, Munch Museum, and Civic News Company.

title: CSC ja Nepalin NREN jakavat osaamistaan GÉANTin Twinning-ohjelmassa
content:
GÉANT Twinning Programme tuo yhteen tutkimus- ja koulutusverkkoja eri puolilta maailmaa tukemaan organisaatioiden kehitystä, osaamisen vaihtoa ja palveluiden käyttöönottoa. Vuoden 2026 twinning-jaksolla CSC:n ylläpitämä suomalainen tutkimus- ja koulutusverkko Funet ja Nepalin NREN rakensivat yhteistyötä ja jakoivat osaamistaan.

”Oli kunnia päästä jakamaan omaa osaamistamme ja samalla oppimaan nepalilaisilta kollegoiltamme. Vaikka toimintaympäristömme ovat erilaiset, tutkimus- ja koulutusverkot kohtaavat hyvin samankaltaisia haasteita eri puolilla maailmaa. Olimme iloisia saadessamme Nepalin pariksemme Twinning-ohjelmassa”, sanoo CSC:n Funet-palveluiden kehityspäällikkö Harri Kuusisto.

Yhteistyö käynnistyi virallisesti keväällä 2026. Se sisälsi viikoittaisia verkkotyöpajoja ja -tapaamisia sekä useamman päivän kestäneen tapaamisen kasvotusten. Kesäkuussa ryhmä Nepalista vieraili CSC:llä Espoossa ennen osallistumistaan Helsingissä järjestettyyn TNC26-konferenssiin. Vierailun aikana osallistujat pääsivät tutustumaan suomalaisiin tutkimusverkkopalveluihin käytännössä.

title: Commission hosts Apply AI Summit to boost Europe’s AI innovation and uptake
content:
Nearly 1,000 high-level policymakers, start-ups, industry leaders and researchers will take part in the Apply AI Summit in Brussels tomorrow.

They will discuss how artificial intelligence (AI) can boost Europe’s competitiveness across 10 strategic sectors and the public sector. The summit will also showcase concrete AI applications, European success stories and innovative projects. 

Henna Virkkunen, Executive Vice-President for Technological Sovereignty, Security and Democracy, will host the summit and present the first Apply AI Startup Award to three European start-ups. The award recognises innovative European startups and scaleups developing AI solutions in the strategic sectors.

Alongside the in-person event, an online conference platform will run from 16 to 20 November, allowing additional 2,500 participants to join part of the summit.

title: 1,840 amendments, one basic question: will the Data Omnibus simplify EU digital rules or weaken people’s rights?
content:
The European Parliament is considering 1,840 amendments to the Digital Omnibus on Data, a proposal that would change the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), ePrivacy and other parts of the EU’s data rules. We have analysed the amendments related to data protection and privacy. Our new guide shows that Parliament faces a choice between genuine simplification that makes rights easier to exercise and changes that would make more (ab)uses of personal data easier while weakening safeguards and exponentially deepening legal uncertainty.

title: Searching for a good day for honey
content: On a perfect summer's day in Latvia, there’s barely any wind and the flowers are producing nectar. “20 degrees and up, with sunshine – that’s an ideal day,” says Valters Brusbārdis, who kept bees for 30 years before selling them all last spring. He also chairs the Latvian Beekeepers’ Association. June and July are usually the most reliable months for making honey, he said. For a professional beekeeper in Latvia, more than 50kg of honey per colony makes a good season. Some of his fellow beekeepers told him they’d had record harvests this year. In 2023, Eurostat counted a record 9.4 million hives on EU farms, 16% more than in 2020. Italy had the highest number, followed by Romania, and Greece. But the figures exclude wild bees, and tell us nothing about the health of the bees living in these hives. Bees and the climate In Bulgaria’s Pirin Mountains, beekeeper Ivan Geshev has seen the effects of the climate crisis on his bees since 2016, from droughts to sharp temperature swings. He estimates that his summer worker bees now live five or six days less than they used to, leaving fewer bees to collect pollen and nectar. Spring is particularly tricky, just as bee colonies begin to grow

title: Interreg Baltic Sea Region programme continues the dialogue with the Strategy on future transnational cooperation
content:
This article is originally published on the Interreg Baltic Sea Region programme site, on 5 October 2026.

What should Interreg Baltic Sea Region, as a transnational cooperation programme, address after 2027? As work on the future Programme progresses, dialogue with regional stakeholders help further develop the cooperation needs identified by the Programme countries. The EU Strategy for the Baltic Sea Region is of particular importance in this process, bringing the macro-regional strategic perspective and helping to ensure that future cooperation needs are firmly rooted in the updated Action Plan and its implementation.

The Baltic Sea region is changing – and so are the challenges that cooperation needs to address. Security and resilience have gained urgency; climate impacts are becoming increasingly tangible; and demographic, green, and digital transitions are reshaping our territories and economies.

title: Corporations Are Using Trump’s Tariff Refunds on Bonuses Rather Than Reimbursing Consumers
content:
When Stanley Black & Decker, one of the world’s largest tool companies, got hit with President Donald Trump’s tariffs last year, the firm made clear that it would be sharing the pain with its customers.

The Connecticut-based company raised prices again and again, moves its executives said were necessary because of the new fees on imports. 

Now, after the Supreme Court struck down Trump’s most sweeping tariffs earlier this year, the company is getting at least $298 million refunded. Instead of sharing that bounty with its customers, however, the firm has chosen different recipients: 

Its own leaders. 

The company is one of at least nine that have disclosed that they are using their refunds not to pay back the cash-strapped consumers who generally covered much of the tariff costs through higher prices, but to give bonuses, according to a ProPublica analysis of thousands of securities filings and earnings calls for publicly traded companies.

Other recognizable companies include the owners of discount department stores TJ Maxx and Marshalls and the golf equipment brand Titleist.

title: FPF sues Defense Department for info on media ‘blacklist’
content:
FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE:

New York, Nov. 16, 2026 — The Department of Defense is unlawfully withholding information about a media “blacklist” it has admitted to keeping internally, according to a lawsuit filed today in federal court by Freedom of the Press Foundation (FPF) and The Intercept.

The plaintiffs, represented by Free Information Group, are asking the court to force the department to disclose documents related to a list of journalists it “disregards,” as described by DOD personnel.

In July, Intercept reporter Nick Turse posed several questions to U.S. Central Command about Iranian attacks on U.S. bases across the Middle East. He was told by CENTCOM staff that if his inquiries on the topic did not stop, he would be put on an existing, internal “list of people to disregard.” A U.S. official later told Turse that the DOD “had a standing order not to engage with” him.

CENTCOM has ignored Freedom of Information Act requests from both Turse and Lauren Harper, FPF’s Daniel Ellsberg chair on government secrecy, for copies of the list of journalists CENTCOM “disregards.”

title: Civil society questions decree that could block access to telecommunications networks in Mozambique
content:

Post-election protests in Maputo, Mozambique, in 2025. Photo by Wilson Thole. Used with permission.

Civil society organizations in Mozambique, such as the Center for Democracy and Human Rights (CDD), submitted a document to the Ombudsman contesting the constitutionality of Decree No. 48/2025, issued in December 2025, which establishes control mechanisms and potential blocks on access to telecommunications networks in the country.

According to the portal Moz24h, journalists and experts are concerned that the measure could threaten rights such as freedom of expression, access to information, and communication, particularly in contexts of social mobilization or political tension. The challenge arises in an environment still heated from the conflicts following the 2024 elections.

title: OPINION: African Democracy on Life Support
content:
By The Rev. Gabriel Odima*

MINNESOTA, USA | 16 November 2026 (IDN) — Africa has become a household name across North America, Europe, Australia, South America and Asia. The only images beaming on the world’s television screens are hunger-stricken skeletons, civil wars, political abductions, human rights abuses and a move towards single-party or no-party rule in countries like Uganda, South Sudan, Ethiopia, Eritrea, Niger, Benin, Tanzania, Gabon and Sudan, to name a few. Democracy is on life support across Africa, and this is a troubling trend.

In the case of Uganda, the military regime, from its installation in 1986 by the gun and bloodshed, has consistently, arrogantly and cynically suppressed and never permitted citizens and their organised political parties to enjoy the freedom to hold opinions on political or public matters, except the opinions of the regime.

In August 1992, the military rulers in Uganda decided to discard their cloak of disguise, which had enabled them since 1986 to falsely present their regime as a coalition in which political parties were represented.

title: Natnael Getenew Zeleke oppi koodaamaan 14-vuotiaana lukemalla setänsä paperista kirjaa – Sitten hän keksi, miten tekoälyä voi hyödyntää ilman nettiä
content:
Pitkä lento ei tunnu vaivaavan Natnael Getenew Zelekeä pätkääkään. Hän on pirteä ja intoa täynnä marraskuisessa Helsingissä, kun hän ensimmäistä kertaa saapuu Eurooppaan.

Helsingistä matka jatkuu Turkuun. Siellä hän osallistuu hackathoniin, eli kilpailuun, jossa keksitään uusia ohjelmistoja ja teknisiä ratkaisuja. 

Sellaisia hän on voittanut jo useita, vaikka onkin vasta 25-vuotias. Suurin saavutus tähän mennessä on Amazonin järjestämän AWS Innovation Awardin voittaminen. Kilpailuun osallistui noin 10 000 kehittäjätiimiä 115 maasta, ja palkintorahoja koko kilpailussa jaettiin 250 000 euroa.  

Voittanut sovellus on nimeltään Ivy. Se on tekoälypohjainen oppimisratkaisu, joka toimii myös ilman internetyhteyttä.  

 Getenew Zeleke tiesi jo teininä, että palkkatyö ei ole häntä varten. Hän halusi olla oma pomonsa omassa yrityksessään. Se oli vanhemmille hieman hankala asia sulatettavaksi.  

“Etiopiassa ajatellaan edelleen vahvasti, että opiskelu ja tutkinto ovat ainoa oikea tie menestykseen”, hän sanoo.

title: 8th International Open Search Symposium – A review (day one)
content:
On the morning of 7 October, the conference kicked off at CODE University of Applied Sciences in Berlin.
First on the mic were Peter Ruppel, President of CODE University of Applied Sciences and Fabian Geier, Professor of Philosophy at CODE University who both welcomed the participants with dedicated kick-off addresses.

“Sovereignty has become a political buzzword. This community can give it substance and it can share how it can look in practice, how to comply, how it can be governed and how it can earn trust from users.” said Peter Ruppel in his welcome address.

„It is pretty clear we are a bit cornered in Europe. In an era where bullying becomes the norm, it is unwise to not be in charge of the technology that we run our societies on.“ stated Fabian Geier.

“This is a conference for Europeans who are builders! (…) I am thankful that OSF is here and to all the people doing the work to help us become a bit more independent as Europeans and not just be on the receiving end of power but built autonomy through technology!” he added, expressing hope for hands-on solutions being shaped in Europe and underlining the importance of conferences like #ossym.

title: Mitä toiseuttaminen tekee kuulumisen kokemukselle?
content:
Yhteiskunnan toistuvalla riskipuheella on erilaisia vaikutuksia lapsiin ja nuoriin. Jokaisella on oikeus tulla nähdyksi yhteiskunnan täysivaltaisena jäsenenä.

Yhteiskunnallinen keskustelu lapsista ja nuorista on ollut syksyn 2026 aikana eri tavoin jännitteistä. Siinä toki ei ole mitään uutta, että lapsista ja nuorista puhutaan riskien, uhkien ja kontrollin näkökulmasta, mutta millä tavoin lapsia ja nuoria koskevassa yhteiskunnallisessa keskustelussa rakennetaan ulkopuolisuutta?

Aikuiset ovat hanakoita määrittämään lasten ja nuorten paikan, jolloin lasten ja nuorten oma toimijuus jää kapeaksi, eikä pääsyä mukaan julkiseen keskusteluun välttämättä ole.  Olennainen kysymys onkin, otetaanko lapset ja nuoret mukaan keskusteluun vai puhutaanko heidän ohitseen.

Lasten ympärillä käydään paljon keskustelua lasten parhaasta, mutta huomattavasti harvemmin siitä, miten erilaiset puhetavat muokkaavat lasten mahdollisuuksia tulla nähdyiksi yhteisön täysivaltaisina jäseninä.

Lapset näyttäytyvät keskusteluissa helposti joko vaaralle alttiina tai vaaran aiheuttajina. Lapsia suojellaan ja heitä kontrolloidaan, usein samanaikaisesti.

title: Beyond DMT: why the true power of Brazil’s sacred jurema plant is social, not just psychedelic
content:
Jurema-preta is the name of both a plant – Mimosa tenuiflora – and an indigenous spiritual tradition of northeastern Brazil. The plant is used to make a potentially hallucinogenic brew that is consumed in sacred rituals. The exact mixture of herbs and other elements contained in the brew is a secret known only by jurema mestre shamans and never revealed.

In 2024 I had the opportunity to visit, as an anthropologist, the city of Natal, in Brazil’s Rio Grande do Norte region, which is a hotspot of the jurema cult. While there, I learned that jurema’s power is as much social as it is chemical.

The sacred and molecular properties of the plant are currently fostering all manner of exciting (though challenging) connections between indigenous knowledge and neuroscience. But jurema’s power goes beyond the plant and its ceremonies, as the jurema cult provides a radically plural space that welcomes all kinds of non-normative identities.

title: Why marine climate refugia matters for safeguarding the world’s oceans
content:

However, these impacts are not distributed evenly. There are areas that buffer these effects and act as true “marine climate refugia”.

title: Eurovision Asia: a diverse and spectacular showcase of Asian pop
content:
On November 14, Asia fired up its wind machines and pyrotechnics for the inaugural Eurovision Song Contest Asia, aka Eurovision Asia.

Eleven countries competed – from Bangladesh and Bhutan to Vietnam and host country Thailand. Notably absent this first year were most of the continent’s most populous nations: China, India, Japan, Pakistan and Indonesia.

The format was familiar: three-minute songs performed with no more than six people permitted on stage. But there was a distinct regional inflection in the staging, costuming and language choices.

Many of the artists wove in elements of traditional sound and traditional dress, and artists expressed gratitude to the audience with the traditional Thai gesture wai (hands together).

While the original Eurovision is hosted in a combination of English and French, Eurovision Asia was delivered in English only. But most artists performed either in their own language (36%) or a combination of that language with English (54%). Only South Korea’s song was performed entirely in English.

By comparison, Eurovision 2026 featured 43% of songs entirely in English, 38% in languages other than English, and 19% multilingual.

title: Chinamaxxing on geopoliittista trollausta parhaimmillaan
content:
Uudenlaisen Kiina-meemeilyn tulkitseminen Kiinan pehmeän vallan kasvuksi ei riitä. Kyse on myös siitä, että osa länsimaalaisista nuorista kieltäytyy tulkitsemasta Kiinaa ylhäältä annetuista raameista.

Absurdin huumorin ystävät ovat saaneet maistiaisia kiinankielisestä sisällöstä jo muita pidempään. Meemiveteraanit muistavat, kun jo vuonna 2020 laulettiin ”xue hua piao piaota” ja vuonna 2021 yhdysvaltalainen näyttelijä John Cena söi jäätelöä ja puhui kiinaa… innokkaasti. Bing chilling!

Ja nyt meillä on chinamaxxing.

Vuonna 2025 nousseella chinamaxxingilla tarkoitetaan yleensä Kiinaan liittyvää somesisältöä, jossa henkilö kokee tulleensa kiinalaiseksi. Meemeissä kiinalaisuutta ovat esimerkiksi vakuutteleminen kuuman veden juomisen terveellisyydestä, ketjupolttaminen tai Tsingtao-oluen juominen. Jotkut vaikuttajat ovat puolestaan tehneet samantyylisiä jumppaliikkeitä kuin kiinalaiset tädit ja sedät puistoissa. Sävy on myönteinen ja hassutteleva. 

Yhteiskunnallisinta on taas sisältö, jossa ihaillaan Kiinan infrastruktuuria, luotijunaverkostoa tai Chongqingin kaltaisten vauraiden suurkaupunkien futuristista ulkonäköä. Sanotaan, että Kiina elää tulevaisuudessa.

Venäjä käyttää kryptovaroja Ukrainassa käymänsä hyökkäyssodan rahoittamiseen. EU:n pakotteet eivät saa vuotaa silloinkaan, kun raha löytää uusia liikkumistapoja.

Venäjä käyttää kryptovaroja yhä enemmän rajat ylittäviin maksuihin ja hankintoihin kiertäen perinteisiä pankkikanavia ja maksuliikennejärjestelmiä. Peiteyhtiöt, monimutkaiset välittäjäverkostot ja harmaat rahoituskanavat kätkevät venäläisten toimijoiden roolin. Ne mahdollistavat Venäjälle pääsyn tavaroihin ja teknologioihin, joita se käyttää hyökkäyssodassaan Ukrainaa vastaan.

Suomi, Tanska, Viro, Ranska ja Liettua vaativat tulevissa pakoteneuvotteluissa vahvempia toimia Venäjän käyttämiin kryptovaroihin ja niihin liittyviin toimijoihin puuttumiseksi.

title: Why the TDM Exception Requires Overriding Mandatory Status in the International Arena

This blog post summarises the study Conflicts in the European Research Area and the European Conflict of Laws: Private Ordering vs. Statutory TDM Exceptions, supported by COMMUNIA, and is published under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International licence (CC BY 4.0).

Drawing upon the findings of a recent study published by Communia, this post explores the impact of Private International Law (PIL) on the text and data mining (TDM) exception under Article 3 of the DSM Directive. While the introduction of this exception marks an important milestone for modern scientific discovery, allowing research organisations with ‘lawful access’ to freely analyse digital corpora, cross-border licensing practices and PIL mechanisms may significantly complicate its consistent operation.

title: "Coffers Are Never Empty…For Bombs": Climate Activist Asad Rehman on Need for Climate Finance
content:
The United Nations climate summit in Antalya, Turkey, is in its second and final week. To get an update on the state of negotiations among countries, we speak with longtime climate campaigner Asad Rehman, the chief executive of Friends of the Earth England, Wales and Northern Ireland. He says rich, developed countries are still dragging their feet on a rapid transition away from fossil fuels while withholding the money that poorer, Global South countries need.

“Whether you’re cutting emissions, whether you’re adapting to the impacts of climate change or dealing with incredible losses which are totalling over a trillion right now, you need public finance,” says Rehman. “And the rich countries are saying, 'Our coffers are empty.' But, of course, the coffers are never empty when it comes to paying for bombs. It’s never empty when it comes to the fossil fuel subsidies to the corporate giants, and it’s never empty when it comes to the billionaires.”

title: Navigating the tricky borders of AI scribes in healthcare
content:
The potential of AI has definitely not been lost on the healthcare sector. AI has the ability to solve many long-standing problems in modern healthcare: lack of resources, risks of human error and difficulties in serving a rapidly evolving patient base. While risks and concerns exist, the AI transformation of the patient journey and other healthcare processes seems inevitable, both in the private and public sectors.

AI scribes, namely AI tools with the ability to convert human interactions into transcripts, visit summaries and other clinical documentation, appear to be a key example of this development. The typical use case is that an appointment between a patient and medical professional is recorded by an AI tool, converted into text and arranged into legally required medical record entries. As a result, the doctor can focus fully on the patient interaction without having to take meticulous notes and save time afterwards as the AI tool has already drafted the required entries.

Legally, things get interesting when we look at what the AI scribe actually does and the extent to which the medical record entries and subsequent clinical activities rely on the AI scribe’s output.

title: EFF’s AI Cybersecurity Policy Framework
content:
The news has been filled with stories recently of AI breaching the security of websites. And while it may feel like a new problem because of AI’s involvement, it turns out that there are longstanding existing cybersecurity safety best practices that these companies—some of the largest tech companies in the world—could and should have taken to prevent these breaches.

Recent cybersecurity incidents have shown that some of the world’s largest tech companies have failed to take basic security precautions when testing frontier AI systems on internet-connected systems. Unfortunately, these failures resulted in breaches of numerous third-party websites, including an AI research-sharing platform called Hugging Face and the Australian healthcare system’s website. Even worse, AI developers failed to detect most of the incidents until long after they occurred due to inadequate monitoring of the AI systems during testing. Had the companies abided by basic, common sense security protocols, these incidents likely would not have occurred.

Verkosta tilattujen halpojen reitittimien, valvontakameroiden ja digiboksien tietoturvapuutteet työllistävät edelleen internetoperaattoreita ja kyberturvan etulinjaa. title: Preserving memory through intergenerational collaboration in Lisbon
content:
Lisbon welcomed 19 participants during a European Heritage Hub Peer-Learning Visit from 4-6 November, exploring how community memories, oral histories and cultural heritage initiatives can strengthen social cohesion, foster intergenerational exchange and reinforce people’s sense of belonging.

Hosted by the City of Lisbon and organised in collaboration with Hub partner Eurocities, the visit focused on the municipal Memories of Lisbon Programme (Programa Memórias de Lisboa), selected as one of the Hub’s 10 Local Good Practices. The programme was led by Memory and Intangible Cultural Heritage Unit representatives Alexandra Aníbal and Mafalda Seoane.

The Memories of Lisbon Programme initiative connects a local older generation of storytellers with young people who interview, film and edit their testimonies about life in Lisbon — demonstrating how personal stories and local heritage can become powerful tools for community engagement, inclusion and cultural participation.
